abilities.desc: The festive aura of this Toon passively gives those around her 50% faster stamina regeneration and a 25% speed boost that lasts for 5 seconds.

toons.strategies:
Bobette is a great all-rounder Toon due to her jack-of-all-trades kit. Her Active Ability, **Precious Packaging**, can be extremely helpful in sticky situations, such as being chased by a Lethal or Ranged Twisted. Unlike Connie's Ability and Smoke Bombs, Bobette's Ability is able to save her from the aforementioned Twisteds, which makes her a great pick for those who prefer to be survivalists. It should be noted that a Twisted may come to your location while you are still in the box, so you must be careful. It's usually safer to use this Ability around corners or against walls because of how Twisteds behave. This is because most do not stall, so they will either move forward or go the other way. Twisteds stop at predetermined locations, so knowledge of their pathing is helpful if you want to play her. The cooldown of her Active Ability won't start counting down until she stops hiding in the present, unless she is under the effects of Ignited.

In runs with multiple people or distractors, Bobette's Active Ability also allows her to assist distractors if they lose sight of any Twisteds by bringing them back to the distractor and using her Ability to force Twisteds to go after the distractor instead. When using this strategy, try to brush against their looping zone without being so close that you steal aggro immediately again. In certain cases, the distractor will be able to retrieve them themselves if they have an Air Horn, are playing Pebble and use his **Speak!** Ability, or if they are using Scrapbook and their Stealth is equal or below 2 Stars, so if the above are the case, it's best to save her Ability than to use it immediately.

Bobette is beneficial to have when it comes to many things. Her 4 Skill Check Stat allows her to be a decent extractor (especially with Magnifying Glass/ Participation Award), however her 2 Star Extraction Speed may hinder this, making her extraction stats the exact same as Tisha's. Her Mobility is above average with 5 Stars in Stamina and a 3 Stars in Movement Speed, allowing her to escape Twisteds easily. Her great mobility Statistics, alongside her above average Skill Check, make her a great Toon to extract Treadmill Machines with. It may be beneficial to help someone on a Treadmill Machine, as the Movement Speed and Stamina boost from her Passive Ability can help finish the Machine faster. This is especially applicable for Duo Machines, as Bobette is already quite capable at extracting all Machine types anyways, being able to support whoever is working with her, if they're on a treadmill attachment.

Despite having 2 Star Stealth, Bobette can be a very good solo Toon. She has the survivability and the (somewhat) good extraction to make it far in the right hands, although she does require some caution, given her status as a Main Character decreasing her heart count and her below-average Stealth equal to some Toons like Vee and Glisten.

Bobette's **Festive Aura** grants a decent stamina regeneration source, as well as a good enough speed boost to escape Twisteds. It works like a combination of a Stamina Candy and Speed Candy, making Bobette a good Toon to help teammates get away from danger. Her only conflict with her Passive is her lower Stealth, but this can also be used to your advantage to take aggro from chasing Twisteds, giving your teammate a better chance to escape. When the Elevator opens at the start of a Floor, you can run in a small circle, or back and forth to give the entire team a speed boost. If you're inside the Elevator during Panic Mode, you can still help your team by standing on the edge (behind the inner yellow line), as the aura is big enough to stick outside of the Elevator. Both of these applications are easier to do if you equip Toy Kit, for you and your teammates.

Bobette's **Festive Aura** can be used to help 2 Star Stealth distractors distract faster Twisteds with ease, like Twisted Pebble. If a Looey, Eclipse, or Goob intends to distract Twisted Dyle with the help of Items, she can also use her Passive Ability to give them a speed boost. The above scenarios will only work if Bobette is using Diary, or the distractor is using Scrapbook. In either case, this allows Bobette to perform a strategy called solar system kiting, where the distractor goes clockwise or counterclockwise and Bobette circles the opposite direction, giving the distractor a consistent 25% speed boost and 50% stamina regeneration. Caution will need to be taken while doing this strategy, as the distractor needs to be careful to not take sharp corners to prevent Twisteds from aggroing on Bobette.

When it comes to Items, those related with Stamina such as Protein Bars or Pop are very helpful. Bobette's 5 Star Stamina can take a while to fully regenerate, and her 3 Star Movement Speed means she needs to run quite often, thus having Stamina Items on hand will allow her to take full advantage of her mobility. Jumper Cables, Skill Check Candies, Instructions, and Valves are good extraction Items that can remedy Bobette's lower Extraction Speed or support her proficiency with Skill Checks. Since she is a Main Character, it's recommended to prioritize Bandages due to them healing one Heart, avoiding any wastage. If you're solar kiting with a distractor, having at least one healing Item is strongly recommended due to the potential danger you're vulnerable to. Mobility Items can also help you keep up with your distractor, especially during Panic Mode.

Overall Bobette is quite capable at practically anything. Extracting, surviving, scouting, supporting, and protecting are all tasks she can effectively fulfill. It's a good idea to choose Trinkets that primarily hone in on one task you wish you do, allowing Bobette to be more effective in that area. However, two separate Trinkets (such as a mobility and extraction Trinket) for different tasks can also be utilized to enhance a generalist playstyle, if that is what you are seeking with her instead.

**Trinket Combinations

Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Bobette to outrun all Twisteds, except Twisted Dyle at max speed before Panic Mode (26.9 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve run speed (28.2 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Dyle during Panic Mode (35 run speed);

• **Diary**, to not disrupt 2 Stealth Distractors;

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

• **Star Pillow**, to regenerate Stamina faster while extracting, taking advantage of her high Stamina and slow extraction.

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Bobette to take full advantage over her 2 Extraction Speed (0.85 extraction speed) and 4 Star Skill Check (134 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction, supporting her 4 Star Skill Check making her an overall decent extractor (26.32 avg/23.95 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability**

• **Sweet Charm,** to reduce **Precious Packaging'**s Ability cooldown (82.8s):

**Solar Kiting**

• **Toy Kit/ Diary**

•With these Trinkets, to allow Bobette to be safely around 2-1 Star Stealth distractors like Looey, Eclipse, Waxwell, Gourdy or 3 Star Movement Speed low Stealth distractors while giving them a speed and Stamina regen boost with a large radius given by Toy Kit. Having Diary around means she can help gather Twisteds for said distractor to help lessen their time running around the map. Do note that Diary won't increase her Stealth to be as high as Pebble or Sprout's. Although, this set alone isn't just for helping distractors—it can also be used to support other 2 Star Stealth Toons in your party while being less likely to take damage.

•If the distractor has Scrapbook or is using a 1 Stealth Toon, Diary can be replaced with Pink Bow for more run speed or Vee's Remote to speed up Machine completion.

toons.name: Gourdy

abilities.name: Trick or Treat
abilities.desc: This Toon applies a random 20% boost for 15 seconds to all Toons within range. Has a cooldown of 35.

abilities.name: Sugar Rush
abilities.desc: Provides a 20% speed boost to all Players for 5 seconds when the Elevator opens and when Panic Mode begins.

toons.strategies:
With max extraction thanks to 5 in both Skill Check and Extraction Speed (tied with Soulvester), alongside 4 Star Movement Speed and 1 Star Stealth, Gourdy is suitable for almost any role, being an amazing and extremely versatile all-rounder. His only genuine con is his 1 Star Stamina (and his 1 Star Stealth if you intend to play him as an extractor, since you could interfere with your distractor often), but this can be easily mitigated with Cooler or simply good Stamina management, especially if you have played Toons with similar Stats, and the 1 Star Stealth can be a non-factor by being aware of how to manage Twisteds.

Gourdy's Active Ability, **Trick or Treat**, functions similarly to Toodles' Active Ability, however it is slightly more potent (+5% extra compared to **Beginner's Luck**) and gives the boost to surrounding teammates within a small radius instead of boosting himself, in addition to it having an extra 10 seconds of cooldown. Unlike most random-effect boosts, it will actually show what the effect is (at least on your target's screen) making it easier to figure out what to do with the buff. His Ability's randomness means it shouldn't be fully relied on to help teammates (ex. giving Skill Check to a Toon being chased), but it is still a helpful tool if you roll something good for your team. Also note his radius is quite small, so you have to practically hug your target, but his 1 Star Stealth can help if you want to boost a teammate who is being chased by taking aggro away from them. Try not to boost distractors (unless in Panic Mode!); you'll take aggro away from them by accident unless your distractor is playing Pebble and **Speak!** is active, they use an Air Horn, or they're playing as a 1 Star Stealth Toon (which you may still take aggro from if you get too close, due to percentage based Stealth decreasing Trinkets like Scrapbook not affecting them). His Ability could be used through a wall or obstacle near the distractor, but due to the boost that he gives being randomized, it isn't worthwhile unless they're struggling. Ask teammates to group around you before the Elevator opens to boost a lot of players at once. Try to use **Trick or Treat** on extracting Toons as you pass them—your 1 Star Stealth makes it easy even while distracting as long as you understand line of sight. You can also ask teammates to run up to you if they pass while you're extracting so you can boost them.

His Passive Ability, **Sugar Rush**, grants everyone (including himself) a +20% Movement Speed boost for 5 seconds at the beginning of a Floor and at Panic Mode, functioning much like a global Pull Toy and Alarm. This is very useful, especially for slow Toons who have trouble reaching the elevator, since a +20% Movement Speed boost is decently potent. It also can help you (or your distractor, depending on how you wish to play Gourdy) find Twisteds faster at the start of a Floor and conserve a bit of Stamina at Panic Mode, and also help with reaching Machines faster.

Gourdy also has great distracting capabilities. He has 1 Star Stealth, meaning he can passively grab aggro from any Toon (besides Brightney, who he may have to get closer to grab aggro from, and Shrimpo), which is extremely helpful for distracting. Unlike Brightney, he has 4 Star Movement Speed, giving him a better distraction playstyle. His Stamina is much lower than hers in comparison though, so be careful and only sprint/sprint-tap when needed.

Given Gourdy's extreme general potential, there is no specific recommended playstyle for him. As such, given his relatively easy requirements compared to other Mains, he is a very good pick for anyone experienced with using Main Characters. There is no "wrong" way to play Gourdy, as his only three deficits (Stealth, Health, and Stamina) can mostly be mitigated by strategy, so feel free to give yourself leeway in trying different Trinket combinations, since there really isn't much punishment gameplay-wise if you lean into a specific role.

Overall, Gourdy is great in teams and selflessness with great extracting, distracting, and supporting potential, with a bit of a struggle in solo runs, though he can still be a good pick as you can easily make his Ability self-sufficient with a Trinket like Peppermint Icing and Ghost Snakes In A Can.

**Trinket Combinations**

Because of Gourdy's 1 Stealth, good mobility, and high Extraction Stats, recommended Trinket combinations for Gourdy are:

**Mobility**

• **Dog Plush/Options**

•This Trinket will unlock the role of distractor to the holder. (19.3 walk speed) Here are some options to pair Dog Plush with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to allow Gourdy to outwalk Twisteds slower than Twisted Toodles and Twisted Shelly (20.2 walk speed);

• **Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool**, to out-walk even faster Twisteds. Keep in mind this only works half the time, and is best used when duo-distracting (21 walk speed);

•Do note this Trinket combo is best used when duo-distracting with another player.

• **Vanity Mirror**, to out-run almost all Twisteds during Panic Mode while active, also supporting his **Sugar Rush** Passive Ability (35.75 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, to completely nullify the Slow Debuff, making Twisted Vee significantly easier to distract, and Ichor Leaks much easier to distract in;

• **Friendship Bracelet**, to be able to sprint for longer periods without a speed debuff, though reliant on multiple alive players;

• **Star Pillow**, to regenerate Stamina faster while extracting, taking advantage of his low Stamina and fast extraction;

•The Trinkets below the **Extraction Section**, to help with floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Gourdy to take full advantage over his 5 Extraction Speed (1.5 extraction speed) and Skill Check (167.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction, supporting his 5 Skill Check (19.91 avg/17.7 with Tech Savvy);

•

• **Stress Ball**, to increase Extraction Speed gradually every successful Skill Check hit, supporting his 5 Star Extraction Speed;

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability/Support**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can/ Peppermint Icing**

•The cooldown reduction synergizes with Peppermint Icing, allowing Gourdy to regain Stamina more often. With Rehearsal/Practice cards, **Trick or Treat** reaches a cooldown of 20 seconds, which means you can consistently support your team and keep your low Stamina in-check.

•These Trinkets can additionally be used separately if you want to solely maximize either his Stamina or his cooldown.

**Note: Diary or Scrapbook are not recommended Trinkets for Gourdy as they do not affect his Stealth Stat since his 1 Star Stealth means 0 Stealth units, and multiplication of 0 will always be 0.**

toons.name: Pebble

abilities.name: Speak!
abilities.desc: This Toon can bark loudly, drastically decreasing Stealth to a value of -40 and alerting any Twisteds nearby to his location. Has a cooldown of 60.

abilities.name: Fetch!
abilities.desc: This Toon can sniff out items, causing them to be highlighted when in the Toon's vicinity.

toons.strategies:
If you like zooming around the place, Pebble is the one for you. Having the highest Movement Speed in the game (5) and high Stamina (4 Stars), Pebble possesses both high survivability and the ability to distract Twisteds proficiently. It is not recommended to focus on extraction with this Toon as his Extraction Speed is significantly lower than other Toons, although having a 3 Star Skill Check makes it a little more bearable.

Pebble is an ideal distractor due to his Movement Speed and Stamina, but if you are in a difficult situation, you are more likely to get hit if you are not careful. If you are distracting multiple Main Character Twisteds, you will need to sprint if Twisted Vee inflicts the Slow II Debuff, Twisted Pebble, Twisted Glisten when enraged; etc. It is recommended to have an Astro by your side when distracting a difficult combination of Twisteds and use his Active Ability to help regenerate your Stamina faster. Only sprint if a fast Twisted catches up to you, even if you are turning corners, do not sprint unless they're about to hit you. You should not have other Twisteds that are significantly slower than others on you when distracting, as they may lose line of sight of you and you will have to go out of your way to regather them, which may lead to some hits or they could turn the other way and hit you. Stay in one area away from Machines or Items so Twisted Pebble will not lose aggro on you and chase after any other Toons who pass through the area where you are distracting.

Pebble's Active Ability is a very useful tool while distracting Twisteds. **Speak!** is able to help save other Toons being chased by Twisteds by forcing the Twisteds to chase you instead. It alerts Twisteds to your location (like a failed Skill Check; most must be nearby to notice) and also lowers your Stealth by 50 units. This means that to steal aggro from other players you will still need to be in the Twisted's detection range, so be careful not to use it from too far behind if chasing a Twisted. If you are distracting in a narrow area and see that a Toon with lower or equal Stealth is attempting to get through the area, consider using **Speak!** to reduce the risk. **Speak!** is most useful when in a sticky situation while distracting, allowing for you to take the aggro off of most Toons and safely allow them to pass. Another alternative to **Speak!** could be collecting Air Horns that you find around the map, as they are a great replacement for the Ability if it not able to be used at the moment.

Pebble's Passive Ability can assist you with finding Items quicker. **Fetch!**, like the name says, assists you with finding Items scattered around the floor by highlighting them, allowing you to find useful Items such as healing or speed Items, the former of which should be pointed out to teammates if unneeded. **Fetch!** is also great if you're searching for Research Capsules to grind Ichor or Research, but be careful to continue paying attention to your surroundings, as **Fetch!** will still highlight the fake Twisted Rodger capsule.

Pebble is an excellent pick for grinding Event Currencies/Research due to high mobility and the ability to detect Event Items and capsules/attract Twisted aggro easily. With the right Trinkets, he can also make a good extractor or solo Toon, making up for any deficits with near-unmatched speed. It can help to have Shelly or Brusha on your team to heat up your extraction, especially when combined with Trinkets and Items. You can also focus on taking care of Treadmill Machines or assisting with Duo Machines, covering possible weak spots of other extractors, or simply to get Floors completed faster overall. When extracting as Pebble, you should still try to support your team using your Abilities and Stats; use your mobility to gather Twisteds for a distractor (if there is one) and to protect slower teammates; use the bark to alert Twisteds away from a Machine, the Elevator, or a vulnerable teammate without having to directly take aggro; use the bark to save low Stealth teammates when a distractor or other Toons can't; use the Item highlight to lead Sprout or Ginger to Tapes, lead Cosmo or injured teammates to healing Items, lead vulnerable teammates to survival Items like Smoke Bombs, or just bring yourself to find Items to help in survival or extracting.

Overall, Pebble is a great distractor Toon, a good support, and also has somewhat of a capacity to be an extractor, though if you aren't aware of your surroundings, he won't be good at any of these.

**Trinket Combinations**

For specific Trinket recommendations, here are some possible combinations:

**Distraction**

• **Dog Plush/Options**

•This Trinket alone allows Pebble to outwalk anything besides Twisted Pebble, Twisted Glisten when enraged, Twisted Coal when a Blackout is present, and some others (22 walk speed). Keep in mind that Dog Plush will make Pebble much faster than slower Twisteds such as Twisted Shrimpo, which would make him lose them more easily. Here are some options to pair Dog Plush with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve walk speed, more preferable for those new to distracting as Pebble (23.1 walk speed);

• **Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool**, to also out-walk before Panic Mode Twisted Glisten, Twisted Pebble, and Twisted Vee when you are inflicted with the Slow II Debuff when active (24.2 walk/33 run speed);

•Do note this Trinket combo is best used when duo-distracting with another player.

• **Vanity Mirror**, to out-run almost all Twisteds during Panic Mode while active (39 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, to completely nullify the Slow Debuff, making Twisted Vee significantly easier to distract, and Ichor Leaks much easier to distract in;

• **Scrapbook**, to be able to distract without other 3 Stealth Toons taking aggro off you;

•Only use this Trinket combo if most of the players in your run have 3 Star Stealth.

• **Megaphone**, to give access to what is essentially Pebble's Active Ability more easily;

•Only use these Trinket combinations if your teammates are unorganized or have 3 Star and below Stealth.

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Pebble to take full advantage over his 1 Extraction Speed (0.75 extraction speed) and 3 Star Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (29.8 avg/27.21 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Distraction** section, to help with survival.

**Ability**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can**, to reduce **Speak!'**s Ability cooldown (55s).

• **Sweet Charm**, to further reduce **Speak!**'s cooldown, though only by a medium amount as the Trinket works with percentages (50.2s).

**Note: It is NOT recommended to use Trinkets that highlight Items such as Memory Locket, Research Map, and Common Event Trinkets, as Pebble can already see Items with his Passive Ability.**

abilities.desc: This Toon can boost the Extraction Speed of a selected Toon by 75% for 15 seconds. Has a cooldown of 60.

abilities.desc: This Toon gains a 25% Movement Speed boost when any Machine is completed for 10 seconds.

toons.strategies:
Shelly has the highest Skill Check Stat available, being 5, which gives her an aptitude for extraction. Her Active Ability, **Inspiration**, is capable of drastically increasing the Extraction Speed of a selected Toon by a whole 75%. As Shelly, you can either find an extractor using or near a Machine and boost them, or go off on your own and extract Machines, boosting those that pass you on the off-chance that they'll stumble across a Machine before the boost wears off. Upon any Machine's completion, her Passive, **Problem Solver**, solves one of her other problems, that being slightly-below average movement stats that hinder travel by giving her a boost of 25% in Movement Speed until the 10 seconds wear off (18.75 Walk Speed/31.25 Run Speed). This boost can stack.

Shelly's **Inspiration** boost is really effective, being able to make 1-2 Star Extraction Speed Toons extract almost as fast as a 5 Star Extraction Speed Toon. Generally, unless duoing, it's best to boost anyone extracting that you can find on low Floors, though note that with multiple targets, you have to think carefully about who you are boosting, like prioritizing a Toon that has just started a Machine over one that's nearly completing it. Toons with high extraction Stats get to have more out of the buff as it lets them find another Machine to complete faster, but if most of the Machines are done, the Floor will finish faster if you buff a slow extractor or the person with the least completion on their Machine. If you're being chased, you can buff a teammate who's almost done with a Machine to get a speed boost out of it. Shelly's boost also stacks with other Extraction Speed buffs, so it can turn things like Instructions or Stress Ball into a real force if you've seen someone bring them or if a Machine is in a risky spot. Lastly, don't buff a Toon that's priming, as it could mess them up. To make the best use out of her Active, memorizing Machine placements is very helpful. Doing this can help you predict if a Toon notices and wants to extract a Machine, therefore giving them a boost earlier.

Shelly's Passive Ability, **Problem Solver**, is a great survival tool for Shelly given the amazing speeds it gives when multiple Machines are finished at once, with 5 Machines completed allowing her to outwalk Twisted Dyle outside of Panic Mode. To see these speeds in full for every Machine that can be possibly finished at a time, see the table below.

In organized runs such as 'Mach Crushers' (runs with 4+ Shellies), a strategy called Duoing is used to capitalize on Shelly's strengths and cooldown, though you can do this if you have a partner to play with you. Duoing has pairs of Shellies stay together, prioritizing one side of the map (left or right) to cover the most ground without being redundant. They try to only boost each other unless there is a Machine near the distractor in need of completing, they can't find their duo/an extraction Machine, or other teammates are doing the last Machines. This strategy is used in more experienced runs and becomes very productive if Vee's Remote is used, as the Shellies can combo with each other early on. Generally, one Shelly "leads", using Vee's Remote first, and the other finds their own Machine to do. Then, when the leader finds another Machine, they boost each other, with the other finding their own Machine. This helps to avoid confusion and to utilize your cooldowns well. Also, Shelly's Passive reduces the need to prime, speeding up Floors further. Again, note that this strategy is used mostly in more organized runs. Duos can also match Skins to coordinate better, but matching colors reduces ambiguity (i.e. green for **Fall Stroll** and **Prehistoric Peppermint**).

Shelly can pair up really well with Brusha for many reasons. For one, a painted Machine's 25% boost stacks with Shelly's 75% boost, totaling to a whopping 118.8%, meaning a team would practically have an infinite supply of Instructions and more. Plus both of their boosts really work with each other's Stat spreads.

Shelly's main weakness is her low Stamina stat. She just has 2 Star Stamina (125 units), resulting in some troubles with Stamina management if not careful. It's recommended to not get below 50 units unless you have some sort of support (an Item, support Toons, experience, or reliable distractors). However, the Stamina problem becomes mitigated once she gains the 70 extra units of Stamina from Dyle's Floor and both Stamina Cards, putting her at 195 units. Even though her Movement Speed is average while ignoring her Passive, she will have trouble running from Twisteds that outpace her in prolonged chases.

As for Items, because she leans towards Extraction, a very obvious choice would be picking and using Extraction Items, allowing her to extract Machines faster for the team. toons.strategies:
Vee is one of the best extractors in the game (only being outclassed by Gourdy and Soulvester), having 4 Skill Check and 5 Star Extraction Speed, making her optimal for those who desire to grind for Ichor or simply just want to extract Machines with ease. However, those powered Stats come at the cost of being one of the worst at escaping Twisteds, as she possesses below-average Stealth and below-average mobility.

As a slow Toon with subpar survivability, Vee requires some support for it, whether it's from other Toons, Trinkets, or Items. With that being said, keeping Boxes o' Chocolates, Smoke Bombs, and Bandages in your inventory when playing as her can be extremely helpful, and having support Toons like Astro or Tisha around is even better when trying to get to places and Machines that are much farther from the Elevator.

If on a solo or alone, Vee will require assistance from other sources, and have to pay attention to her surroundings in order to not have an unpleasant encounter with any dangerous Twisteds that she struggles to outrun. With that being said, it's best to keep in mind that Stamina management is important. Only use Stamina when Twisteds are around, and save up to 60 Stamina in the case of being noticed by one or more Twisteds ever happens. You should also be aware of your Stealth in such scenarios.

Some of Vee's best qualities and benefits come in the form of her Abilities. Vee's Active Ability, **Mic Check**, serves many purposes, being helpful for both distractors and extractors alike. Her Ability shows the location of all Twisteds and Machines on the map, allowing distractors to locate and gather Twisteds easier, and allowing extractors to locate Machines more efficiently. In terms of usage, Mic Check doesn't really need to be saved for specific times, considering it will be beneficial to all whenever you use it, though it can be slightly better utilized at the start of a Floor. Alongside her Active, Vee has a much similar Passive Ability, that being **Camera Hijack**, which highlights two Machines that are nearest to her location. Although seemingly being a worse version of her Active Ability, it can be helpful at times where her Ability is on cooldown. It also helps her locate Machines before anyone else in her team does (this is important considering Vee's lower mobility would hinder her locating Machines faster), or even locate Machines for her teammates at times when her Ability is on cooldown. Both of her Abilities can allow her to point stealthier extractors to more open Machines, or higher mobility extractors to Machines far from the elevator, enabling her to keep out of the way of distractors or just general danger, while still contributing to overall extraction indirectly. Do note that Duo Machines will only be highlighted with a white outline (meaning they're being extracted) if a Toon is extracting on the left attachment, so you may have to look for the Ichor inside the Machine to see if it's being filled, if only the right attachment is being extracted from.

Another small upside to Vee is her light-production during Blackouts. Though it isn't much, Vee will produce a light during such event, which helps her see better during Blackouts. She can also use this light radius to guide other teammates, though due to her low speed, this may not be the safest strategy.

Overall, Vee is a great support and extractor Toon, though has both downsides and upsides. Additionally, playing as her requires carefulness and attention to your surroundings, so it's best to train your senses before trying to play as her during planned or serious runs. She requires patience and can punish reckless traversal, though her **Mic Check** can be extremely helpful in gathering information about the floor.

**Trinket Combinations**

Vee has a lot of good Trinket combinations. Some of them include:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further increase Run Speed and outrun Twisted Pebble before Panic Mode (25.4 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Bobette or similar/higher speed Twisteds during Panic Mode and assist teammates (31.4 run speed);

• **Diary**, to not interfere with 2 Stealth Distractors;

•Only use this Trinket set if there is a distractor that meets such criteria in your team.

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

• **Star Pillow**, to regenerate Stamina faster while extracting, taking advantage of her average Stamina and fast extraction;

•The Trinkets in the **Extraction** section, to help with floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Vee to take full advantage over her 5 Extraction Speed (1.5 Extraction Speed) and 4 Star Skill Check (134 Skill Check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction, supporting her 4 Skill Check (19.07 avg/16.95 with Tech Savvy);

• **Stress Ball**, to increase Extraction Speed gradually every successful Skill Check hit;

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with mobility.

**Ability/Support**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can**, to reduce **Mic Check** Ability cooldown (45s).

• **Sweet Charm**, to further reduce **Mic Check**'s cooldown, though only by a small amount as the Trinket works with percentages (41s), especially if they're afraid a Floor will have dangerous Twisteds such as Twisted Scraps, Twisted Goob, or any Main Character Twisteds.

**Other**

• **Spare Bulb**, to further increase Vee's already large light radius for maximum visibility, although it may cause some slight lag for older devices;

• **Party Popper**, to assist her during Blackouts when extracting, somewhat serving as a weaker version of **Mic Check**.

**Note: It is NOT recommended to use Fishing Rod on Vee, as both of her Abilities already highlight Machines.**

This makes him a good choice to earn Ichor through Machines when starting out. However, since he is heavily dependent on teammates for maximum Extraction Speed, if you prefer playing with a small team (1-4 players), other Toons such as Glisten, Yatta, or Vee will be better suited in this occasion. His Ability, **Wind-Up**, allows access to over 5 Star Extraction Speed, but since these Stats are obtainable without using the Ability slot (which is a source of bonus Ichor), it's similar to playing without any Ability at all. Worse than that is the fact that his Ability relies on factors out of your control, which makes Boxten outclassed by a lot of Toons.

Assuming you're in a team with enough players (around 5-8), you can be a very efficient stealthy extractor, especially if there's a distractor with 2 or 3 Star Stealth. Using Diary furthers this by allowing you to extract near 3 Star Stealth teammates with little to no risk involving Twisteds. This all could make him more viable than low Stealth, high Extraction Speed Toons such as Glisten, Squirm, and Yatta, due to the ability to extract quickly near a variety of distractors.

Generally, it's recommended to use Boxten in games with a lot of Toons to get the most value out of his Ability. Though, he is quite iffy for solo runs, due to his Ability relying solely on other teammates, wasting it. He is a great option for long runs however, because if his teammates can stay alive, it gives him quite a bit more than 5 Star Extraction Speed, with decent Stats across the others.

Boxten benefits from being on a team with Toons that can boost his Extraction Speed, such as Brusha, Shelly, or Cocoa. The boosts multiply with Boxten's passive, creating a particularly potent stacked increase that could allow him to fill Machines in no time, while also getting more use out of the boosts, minimizing potential wastage.

He can benefit from survival Items, helping his average Movement Speed, which can make escape from Twisteds tedious, especially for newer players. Stamina items can help remedy poor Stamina management or improve his mobility. Extraction Speed or Skill Check increasing items can further improve his variably decent-phenomenal extraction. This is especially the case for percentage based Extraction Speed boosts from Items such as Extraction Speed Candy or Instructions, as their boosts will multiply with Wind Up's boost.

His average Stat spread means that while he has no true deficits, he also doesn't have the most potent strengths. Supplementing your personal weaknesses with Trinkets is best while using him. Using Trinkets that stack with his Extraction Speed can also work, such as Stress Ball (where he can reach upwards of 83.3% as a boost with 8 living players).

Looey is an excellent All-Rounded Toon that can distract or extract. With low Stealth and a great Passive Ability that increases his Movement Speed per lost, he's excellent at leading Twisteds around, and his above-average Skill Check Stat is helpful for extracting Machines.

His Passive Ability, **Heart of Helium**, greatly increases distracting capabilities, however, it also increases the risk factor while using him. **Heart of Helium** increases his speed by 20% for each Heart that he's currently missing, allowing him to reach higher speeds than even Pebble under certain circumstances. Looey is also faster than average at completing Machines, giving him a great utility on a team even if he plays as a distractor.

On only one Heart, Looey is the fastest Toon in the game and can easily outrun Twisted Pebble and other fast Twisteds if the player has good Trinkets in use. The most used Trinket on Looey is Dog Plush, which gives him 10% extra Walk Speed, and even more when paired with Speedy Shoes (15.5%), Ribbon Spool, or Clown Horn (both 21% depending on Floor number). Even without Trinkets, Looey can already out-walk average or slow Twisteds on 2 Hearts, and can almost do the same to every Twisted on one Heart (outside of Panic Mode) aside from Twisted Bobette, enraged Twisted Glisten, Twisted Coal in a Blackout, and Twisted Pebble. However, Twisted Vee and her Slow II could make it a bit harder to distract, especially when on 1 Heart, the exception is if Looey has Train Whistle equipped making Twisted Vee more easy to distract on 2 Hearts. Additionally, long-ranged Twisteds like Twisted Goob could be problematic, so it's suggested to have a backup distractor deal with them; if Looey chooses to distract them, Cardboard 'Armor' may help if they struggle to distract ranged Twisteds, as his play-style can put him at more risk of death. Do note its single use per Floor though.

Using Savory Charm or having a Soulvester is quite useful, especially if you are a risky player. Despite keeping 2 Hearts being the meta, some people will opt for 1 Heart for ensured out-walking. However, this does make a hit fatal. Savory Charm and Soulvester's Ability aids this, by protecting you from a small mistake, saving you from lag spikes or cornering and also alerting you to be more cautious. Since you'd likely have a far easier time distracting Twisteds like Twisted Pebble and Twisted Gourdy with 1 Heart, potentially being able to out-walk some of the fastest Twisteds, having Soulvester constantly guarding you can eliminate the risk of death if you mess up or lag occurs; this is especially good in longer runs due to the increased Main Character Twisted spawn rate. Do realize Savory Charm's one time use and Soulvester's bad survivability and need for Hearts to use the Ability. You'd want a healer on the team if you intend to distract to higher Floors with a Soulvester supporting you.

Looey is a great pick if you're trying to learn to distract Twisteds using Toons with 3 Movement Speed. His Ability provides a great buffer against trickier targets, helping you when you're in trouble, and upon being healed the user can return to their learning. His low Stealth greatly aids in keeping Twisteds' attention, which is again, great for beginners. However, compared to Goob and other such distractor Toons, Looey carries more risk for more reward—weigh your preferences.

The user might also elect to immediately voluntarily reduce their Hearts to two or even one (the prior being preferred) for an immediate speed boost, but this effectively turns him into a Main Character with one Ability instead of two (or zero if you don't consider the speed boost as a sufficient enough Ability due to it technically accounting for a Main's extra Star). Still, even this method has unique Stats to offer compared to other Toons, so it's not beyond consideration—just be sure to trust your skill level before trying. If you elect to aim for 3 Hearts, Looey still makes a great back-up distractor and can extract during downtime, especially if a healer like Sprout is in your party.

Speaking of healers, be sure to communicate with teammates what your preferred heart total is, as everyone has their own ideal amount. Even if your party lacks a healer, let others know ahead of time; You may end up wasting a heal Card if they worry for you, or worse, avoiding a needed heal because they assume you prefer low HP. Looey has a harder time sustaining health than other Distractors due to his Ability—heal Cards are often wasted, half of a Health Kit's value must be sacrificed to retain 2 Hearts status, and occasionally Looey will take intentional damage to deal with tough Twisteds, needing to use additional healing to regain a safe HP level.

As an extractor, Looey can extract most Machines at an above average pace, and if injured, he can additionally extract Treadmill Machines fairly quickly. You can purposefully get hit during Panic Mode when everyone else is in the Elevator, or get hit by certain Twisted like Twisted Squirm and Twisted Blot, if you want to have a consistent higher speed. Take note of your Stealth as it can make it easier for other teammates to swap Twisted aggro onto you, or risk getting in the way of distractors. Since without speed Trinkets Looey can still reach a high enough Movement Speed to outspeed various Twisteds, you can help gather Twisteds for a distractor and protect teammates, though only if you know what you're doing–you could end up causing problems or accidentally sabotaging teammates.

The best Items to look out for as a distractor are mobility Items and healing Items. Movement Speed Items can stack with Looey's speed boost and temporarily let you regenerate Stamina in preparation for Panic Mode or changing your distracting location. Stamina Items can help you keep your Stamina up, something important considering the risk involved with having less Hearts. Healing Items will ensure you stay alive, though you should usually focus on having at least 1 Bandage, since you can better control your speed, while also not wasting the value. When extracting, Looey can make good use of Items like Skill Check Candies owing to his high Skill Check Stat, though Items like Instructions are still very useful for completing Machines faster. You can also use speed or Stamina related Items for Treadmill Machines though only if they're more common, as it could end up being a waste otherwise.

Overall, Looey is an excellent Toon to play as, with distraction being his best occupation, reaching higher speeds, though depleted Health makes him a high-risk-high-reward Toon. Even so, his decent extraction keeps him as a solid Toon, especially when it comes to Treadmill Machines.

toons.desc: Poppy is one fun friend! This excitable Toon loves to share what's on her mind! Poppy shows children it is okay to be unique and to not be afraid to share your interests with others!
toons.strategies:
Poppy is a great choice for beginning players. Her Stealth and Movement Speed, along with her Ability, **Panic Pop**, provide good recovery from mistakes, making her ideal for learning the basics. As an all-rounder Toon, she does not specialize as a Distractor or Extractor but leans towards being a Survivalist with her Ability to outrun Twisteds. For optimal performance, it is recommended to equip her with Extraction-based Trinkets such as Wrench and speed-enhancing Trinkets like Pink Bow. This combination effectively improves her Movement and Extraction Speed, and is easily accessible early on in the game, making it ideal for new players. Other helpful Trinkets that new players will find easy to acquire include Speedy Shoes and Party Popper.

Her Ability really helps against specific Twisteds like Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, Twisted Rodger, or Twisted Vee, since the huge speed boost can make escape far easier. Twisted Razzle & Dazzle's circle is quite large, so escaping it when they're enraged could be quite difficult without potentially taking multiple hits (whether from multiple Twisteds or the aforementioned twins themselves) for some other Toons, but Poppy can escape the circle with ease when injured. Twisted Rodger and Twisted Vee can slow Poppy to the point where she can't outrun certain threats, but her speed boost can counteract the Slow, allowing her to avoid taking multiple hits. While these are advantages she has, other Toons can have a similar experience thanks to their Abilities or Stats, and certain Trinkets like Train Whistle could also help make things easier without needing to take a hit in the first place.

This Toon is less advantageous for experienced players, since her Ability only activates upon losing a Heart, limiting its overall viability and contributions. It is most effective for experienced players when dealing with large swarms of Twisteds, especially if multiple healers are present. If you are confident in your kiting abilities and tend to adapt quickly to new games, consider selecting Boxten as your starter instead. For those who enjoy playing as Poppy, transitioning to Looey might be the next step to take to enhance your experience.

If a teammate cannot escape a Twisted—whether because they are playing as a slower Toon, being chased by a fast Twisted like Twisted Pebble, or are low on Stamina—it may be a viable strategy to intervene by taking a hit from the chasing Twisteds. This is especially effective if Blushy Bat and/or Soul Sword is equipped. By doing this, the player can provide both themself and their teammate an opportunity to escape, even if significant Stamina has been expended to reach them. This strategy may not be as efficient as using an Air Horn or good positioning—since it sacrifices a Heart to ensure their escape—but it is worthwhile in situations where low-health Main Character Toons like Shelly or Sprout are in clear danger. Their Abilities are invaluable to the team, with Sprout even being able to heal the player afterward, mitigating the cost of the sacrifice. Inexperienced players **should not** attempt this strategy, as there are many intricacies that may turn this into sabotage rather than a rescue. Instead, wait and learn; surviving is enough in the beginning.

If a player find themself in a situation where they cannot reach the Elevator in time during Panic Mode, it is advisable to walk in order to conserve or regenerate Stamina before intentionally taking a hit. Afterward, they can sprint to the Elevator. Failing to reach the Elevator in time results in an instant death, whereas losing one or two Hearts to Twisteds provides an opportunity for survival.

Note Poppy isn't the best choice for runs attempting to spawn Twisted Dyle. Her Ability becomes far less useful due to his insta-kill and Common Twisteds being easier to avoid than others. Her Stats don't provide any specific strengths by base either, with mediocre extraction or average mobility.

Due to her all-rounded Stats, any Items can be useful for her. Mobility Items such as Pops and Speed Candies can make escape easier, keeping her Ability as a last resort. Extraction Items like Instructions and Skill Check Candies can improve her average extraction, filling Machines more efficiently. Healing Items can help for newer players who get hit more often (unless there's a healer on the team), or to make a body blocking playstyle more safe (though this can eat through heals).

Overall, Poppy is a good starter Toon, but is heavily outclassed later in the game by Toons who have better extraction and escapability. She has a couple niches, but struggles to really shine when other Toons can more effectively fulfill them.

**Trinket Combinations**

For specific Trinket recommendations, here are some possible combinations:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Poppy to outrun all Twisteds outside of Panic Mode besides Twisted Dyle at max speed (26.9 run speed/40.3 when attacked). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve run speed (28.2 run speed/42.34 when attacked);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Dyle during Panic Mode (35 run speed/52.4 when attacked);

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Poppy to take full advantage over her 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Other**

• **Blushy Bat/Any**

•Blushy Bat synergizes incredibly well with Poppy's Passive Ability. Due to its accessibility, this Trinket is a must-have for newer players, giving them a generous amount of time to get distance from Twisteds after a hit. Experienced players are more likely to benefit more from the other recommended Trinkets above.

• **Soul Sword/Any**

•Soul Sword, like Blushy Bat, synergizes greatly with Poppy's Ability. Its speed boost will assist her in escaping Twisteds while Soul Sword slows them down, allowing for easy escapes. This Trinket could also be paired with Blushy Bat to almost guarantee safe escapes, though it does take both Trinket slots, and the Trinkets can counteract each other a bit.

toons.name: Ribecca

abilities.name: The Undead
abilities.desc: Ribecca is immune to all applied debuffs (does not include trinkets). Whenever this Toon's immunity shines, she feels empowered and receives a random buff in its place for 10 seconds.

toons.desc: Ribecca loves the spooky season! She often helps in making costumes for her friends to enjoy! In her eyes a big part of the fun is dressing up and showing off your scary flare!
toons.strategies:
Ribecca is a great All-Rounder Toon for runs, as her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, bypasses all applied Debuffs, such as Twisted Vee's Slow II Debuff applied on a chase; Twisted Astro's Tired III Debuff; Illness III, Slow I, and Ichor Stains from Ichor Leak Puddles being a few examples. This makes the above Twisteds along with any other Debuff sources almost to fully non-threats. Being easily accessible during the Halloween Event, Ribecca is a great option for starters who struggle with Debuffs.

When she normally would be afflicted with a Debuff, Ribecca gets a 10% boost to a random Stat for 10 seconds instead. The buff granted is indicated by the color of the particles (and boost ring if enabled) Ribecca gains. Below are the buffs that she can gain and their colors:

•**Orange - Skill Check** (Increases chance & size only) (35% chance and 165 size)

•**Yellow - Movement Speed** (16.5 Walk Speed/27.5 Run Speed)

•**Green - Stamina** (Increases Stamina regeneration only) (2.64/s and 26.4 Stamina regenerated in 10 seconds)

•**Blue - Stealth** (16.5 Stealth)

•**Purple - Extraction Speed** (1.10 Extraction Speed (~40.9 seconds))

While Ribecca is intended to be a starter Toon and has a really good Passive, you may want to get used to dealing with Debuffs early on as a different Toon. This is because if a starter uses Ribecca for the most part, they may struggle a bit more with Debuffs due to not being used to them when they transition to a different Toon. However, this mostly depends on how you want to progress in the game, so you are still free to play whatever Toon and playstyle you wish. Just remember that it's a good idea to learn how to counter Debuffs by base, especially if you plan to distract at some point as you progress and get more Toons.

Despite the seemingly lacking Ability for more experienced players, Ribecca is actually quite decent in long runs. With the increased likelihood of Main Character Twisteds, she can easily handle Twisted Vee and Twisted Astro, being able to pass them to distractors or pull them away from teammates, all without worrying about the Debuffs. When Twisted Shelly is on the Floor, Ribecca is capable of extracting faster than most other Toons, only being outpaced by Toons with 5 Extraction Speed, above average Skill Check in some cases, as well as certain Trinkets. Twisted Finn's Ichor Puddles can be annoying, especially due to Twisted Barnaby, but since Ribecca is immune to the Debuffs, she'll have less of an issue with the effects, and not be bothered much if Twisted Barnaby latches onto her. All of this is before considering the Stat boost she can gain from Debuffs, which can make her even more capable at extracting or defending.

Since she gets a boost from Debuff sources, it could be viable to go out of your way to interact with them. For example, you can go out of your way to extract from Twisted Brusha's vandalized Machines, even for a moment, allowing you to actively give yourself a decent boost.

Ichor Leaks can be dangerous and become more likely the further you go, with Ribecca not being affected by them whatsoever, greatly improving her survivability and extraction capabilities during these Floor Events. In fact, she directly benefits from walking through Ichor Puddles, so don't be afraid to do so, in order to consistently get a Stat boost.

During the Easter Event, Spring Fevers normally have a significant impact in the form of a constant Tired II, which would typically make maintaining Stamina a bit difficult, but Ribecca's immunity lets her keep her Stamina in check more easily; she can also reap the benefits of Energized II with an additional boost too.

As her Ability description states, she isn't immune to negative Multipliers from Trinkets (such as Cooler's speed decrease), so Trinkets and Items will still need to be used to remedy or counteract such cases.

Since there's only three Debuff sources that can spawn on Dyle's Floor (four during the Halloween Event); Ichor Leaks, Twisted Brusha, and Treadmill Machines (as well as Trick or Treat Doors); Ribecca isn't the most reliable for seeking Twisted Dyle, as her Stats are average and don't lead to her being able to extract any Machine types particularly quickly. When an Ichor Leak does occur though, she does have an advantage, since the Illness that would usually make missing Skill Checks (and by extension, enraging Twisted Dyle) becomes a Stat boost when she walks through them, albeit this has a slim chance of happening, especially if TIME'S UP is selected on an early Floor. With Twisted Brusha, it's dependent on her spawning, which isn't guaranteed but when she does spawn, the immunity to her graffiti allows Ribecca to extract at a normal pace, with the Stat boost given by extracting from vandalized Machines. Treadmill Machines on the other hand are not an option unless you have Mime Makeup equipped, as Ribecca is immune to the speed reduction from failing Treadmill Machine Skill Checks, yet failing a Skill Check will usually enrage Twisted Dyle unless you have the aforementioned Trinket. Trick or Treat Doors only show up during the Halloween Event, and only have a chance to give a Trick that inflicts a Debuff, or the "No Bones About It!" Treat, which empowers Ribecca without needing to interact with a Debuff source; Trick or Treat Doors can make her a little more capable for Dyle Runs, but the randomness isn't reliable.

Her 3 Stars in all Stats means she doesn't have any specific strengths nor weaknesses, so you can usually select Trinkets and focus on collecting Items that best revolve around your playstyle or mitigate your personal weaknesses. Her Ability's boosts can stack with some Trinkets, so that can also be taken into account.

With all of that being said, she can be a pretty decent solo Toon, as Debuffs can be much more impactful when you have no teammates to help you, mitigate the effects, or remove Debuff sources; this isn't to mention her Stat boost from combatting Debuffs. Her Stats may be average across the board, but her lack of needing Train Whistle (a common choice for long solo runs) allows her to invest in a different Trinket.

**Trinket Combinations**

Recommended Trinket combinations for Ribecca include:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Ribecca to outrun all Twisteds outside of Panic Mode besides Twisted Dyle at max speed (26.9 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve run speed (28.2 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Dyle during Panic Mode (35 run speed);

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Ribecca to take full advantage over her 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Note: It is NOT recommended to use Train Whistle on Ribecca, as her Passive already nullifies the Slow Debuff.**

toons.name: Rudie

abilities.name: Antler Charge
abilities.desc: This Toon uses his antlers to quickly charge forward in a short burst, helping him escape tricky situations.

toons.desc: Rudie is one jolly Toon! He loves to show his festive spirit by prancing and dancing to bring in holiday cheer. He's always excited because he thinks EVERY day is Christmas!
toons.strategies:
Rudie is pretty well-rounded due to his fully 3 Stats, being able to extract quite well and having high potential when it comes to mobility.

Rudie's Active Ability, **Antler Charge**, allows him to dash forward by increasing both his Movement Speed by 50 units, giving him 65 Walk Speed and 75 Run Speed. You can utilize this to get around or avoid danger, like for example, when you end up getting cornered in some way, using his Ability can help you get out of the area unscathed. His cooldown is also very short, meaning it's easy to get around places and escape situations at almost any time, especially with Trinkets like Ghost Snakes In A Can. In Panic Mode, you can dash into the Elevator making it easier to avoid dying to the Panic Mode timer and the Twisteds who get faster during that period.

Rudie's Ability gives him the ability to perhaps be a decent distractor if one has the skill to do so. Given its short cooldown and powerful speed boost, as well as his average Movement Speed and Stamina, things like the usual Distractor Trinkets like Dog Plush alongside cooldown reducing Trinkets and Cards are recommended. It should be noted that, even with Dog Plush, Rudie is only able to out-walk Twisted Shrimpo at best, so a better option for Distracting would be Flutter due to her similar Ability and better mobility Stats. You can also simply divert Twisteds away from teammates, or bring Twisteds to distractors, using your Ability to facilitate escape or passing.

Peppermint Icing is a really good choice to use with him. The short cooldown makes it so gaining Stamina would be a lot faster, and seeing as how the Ability would be used in traversal/escaping, a time where Stamina would be appreciated, the added Stamina can help prolong sprinting and make the situations easier. You can also sprint on Treadmill Machines and periodically stop extracting to use his Ability, regenerating the 30 Stamina and allowing for more sprinting, thus faster extraction of Treadmill Machines.

Overall, Rudie is a great all-rounder, with incredible mobility and survivability. He's decent at extracting and has a potential to distract. He's a fairly good Toon in solo runs, especially due to his Ability.

**Trinket Combinations**

For specific Trinket recommendations, here are some possible combinations:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Rudie to outrun all Twisteds outside of Panic Mode besides Twisted Dyle at max speed (26.9 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve Run Speed (28.1 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Dyle during Panic Mode (35 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Rudie to take full advantage over his 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can/ Peppermint Icing**

•The cooldown reduction synergizes with Peppermint Icing, allowing Rudie to regain Stamina more often. With the Rehearsal/Practice cards, **Antler Charge** reaches a cooldown of 8 seconds, which means you can gain a very potent amount of mobility.

•These Trinkets can additionally be used separately if you want to solely maximize either his Stamina or his cooldown.

**Other**

• **Spare Bulb**, to further increase Rudie's light radius for maximum visibility, although it may cause some slight lag for older devices.

toons.name: Shrimpo

abilities.name: Bully
abilities.desc: Stealth is drastically lower than any other Toon. Only play this Toon if you are looking for a challenge.

toons.desc: Shrimpo is one angry shrimp! Often causing issues for Dandy and friends by making a mess and never learning his lesson! No one likes a bully!
toons.strategies:
Shrimpo is a special Toon, having atrocious Stats, with all of them being 1, especially his Stealth, which is **-99**, which is the second lowest Stealth in the game. With that being said, you are advised to **avoid playing as him for general play.**

As the description of his Ability states, only play as him if you are looking for a challenge. In case if one actually wants to play as the character, whether for special runs, just for fun, to complete his mastery or to get Hissy Fit, here are some tips, tricks, and strategies to do at least decently, as extreme Stealth and patience is key.

Since Twisteds will spot him easily, there is very little room for error, and getting chased usually means your run will end early. As such, you may have to wait things out until you are absolutely certain the situation is safe to proceed.

Items can also help greatly as Shrimpo's speed is easily one of his biggest hindrances, and Trinkets can help offset (however, small) some of his drawbacks. In this sense, Shrimpo can be a great character to start learning the game with, as mistakes cost him more than they would any other Toon, even if some Toons have 1 Movement Speed.

Be careful with faster Twisteds like Twisted Toodles since her Speed will overwhelm you. Twisted Toodles' chase speed is the same as Shrimpo's run speed. It's best to stay out of any Twisteds' way as they are likely to spot you. If you do get caught up in the line-sight of a Twisted, looping around any structure not connected to a wall is a good idea as it will allow you to stay out of sight while also running too far away.

Shrimpo may find use from extracting machines near the Elevator as on earlier Floors with good timing you should finish up around when most other machines are complete giving you a good head start on getting to the Elevator, something that is very due advantageous to the danger Panic Mode gives to Shrimpo, though with Vanity Mirror equipped, this can be avoided. It's also easier if you purchase the Valve Item from the Pre-game UI to even finish the first Machine.

One very applicable skill Shrimpo has is watching Twisted Glisten. Because Shrimpo isn't exactly the best at Extraction, and is nearly incapable of kiting, leaving him to make sure Glisten doesn't become hostile whilst the other Toons handle bigger problems is a smart idea.

Of course, you'll need to be told by your teammates when to get away from Glisten and when they are on last, as he immediately becomes hostile when Panic Mode happens.

Despite the atrocity that is Shrimpo and his general gameplay, there is one purpose that he can do better than any other Toon in the game, a strategy unique to him only, which is magnetism. Shrimpo's -99 Stealth means that he can be spotted from very far away, and cannot have aggro taken off him (unless from Blot's Ability), which can be used to his advantage, as shown in the example scenarios below:

•If a distractor is struggling to deal with long-ranged Twisteds, Shrimpo can take aggro off of the distractor from really far away right before the Twisted launches their attack, (if you time it correctly) because of how far you'd be, you will remain in safe distances and get much longer time to escape the attack. While this sounds niche at first, there is much more to magnet distraction.

•If Shrimpo sees a Toon with low Stealth, like Brightney, especially one with bad mobility, Shrimpo can act as a permanent bodyguard as even a Brightney using an Air Horn will have more Stealth than Shrimpo, but do remember that because of the fact Shrimpo has terrible mobility as well, it is important to use the Pop Pack with a mobility Trinket, (or 2 mobility Trinkets, though it might not be as effective), for this.

•If there are Twisteds near the Elevator during Panic Mode, Shrimpo can aggro them to him and return inside the Elevator, surprisingly enough the Twisteds will be frozen all grouped in one place, which unless dealing with Twisted Toodles, means you are basically stunning the Twisteds.

•This also unlocks the ability to distract during Panic Mode by using some Pop from your Pop Pack combined with the Vanity Mirror making you fast enough to outrun most Twisteds while keeping your stamina high.

•This strategy removes the need to take items on the floor, which your teammates could want, and removes the need of extracting, which is something your teammates can do more effectively than you could, but gives you a special strategy that could even save your distractor.

If you follow all these tips right, Shrimpo will start feeling like a Toon with a unique playstyle, as Shrimpo can save Toons low on stamina about to get comboed to death by Twisteds, even if they have low Stealth, as he has the lowest Stealth in the game.

**Trinket Combinations**

Here are some Trinket sets for Shrimpo, to aid in general play:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket slightly improves Shrimpo's survival before Panic Mode (21.5 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve run speed (22.6 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Pebble during Panic Mode as well as luring them away from teammates (27.9 run speed);

• **Friendship Bracelet**, to be able to sprint for longer periods without a speed debuff, though reliant on multiple alive players;

• **Train Whistle**, to completely nullify the Slow Debuff, making Twisted Vee significantly easier to survive. You also won't be slowed from Ichor Puddles;

• **Blushy Bat**, to prevent sequences of hits for running out of Stamina by sparing more time to gain distance from Twisteds;

• **Soul Sword**, to slow the Twisteds down when you get hit so you can escape from them quicker;

• **Star Pillow**, to regenerate Stamina faster while extracting, taking advantage of his low Stamina and slow extraction;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

•The following Trinkets help Shrimpo extract by dealing with his main deficiency, which is his 1 Skill Check (50 skill check size) and Extraction Speed (0.75 extraction speed):

• **Vee's Remote**, to instantly complete Machines in dangerous locations, such as dead ends and open areas;

• **Mime Makeup**, to more safely extract by removing the danger of missing Skill Checks;

• **Thinking Cap**, to increase Skill Check Size, helping to fail less Skill Checks, though Mime Makeup can be more beneficial in some cases;

•If the player has no issues with small Skill Checks, they may consider using **Magnifying Glass** or **Participation Award** to help with Machine extraction more easily, even if the Skill Check window is far smaller. Though, do note that if the player has lag/missing frames, they may want to consider other Trinkets for team progression.

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Shrimpo Run**

• **Brick/ Coal**

•For the **true** Shrimpo experience, this set makes it even more of a challenge to survive, with a 19% decrease in Movement Speed. This combo will cause your speed to plummet to **8.1 Walk Speed/16.2 Run Speed**, making you only be able to outrun really few Twisteds.

•If you don't have Coal from the Christmas Event, you could use **Cooler** to also decrease Shrimpo's speed, **Magnifying Glass** or **Participation Award** to make it even harder to hit Skill Checks, or **Diary** to decrease Stealth even further.

**Note: Diary and/or Scrapbook have the opposite effect to his Stealth, meaning Diary will further decrease it, while Scrapbook will increase it.**

toons.name: Brightney

abilities.name: Night Light
abilities.desc: This Toon can shine lights on Twisteds to make them visible during Blackouts for 8 seconds. Has a Cooldown of 45.

toons.desc: Brightney is one clever lamp, always coming up with bright ideas! She teaches children on how to think up solutions to their everyday problems!
toons.strategies:
Brightney is a great All-Rounded Toon who is best utilized by those familiar with the game. It's recommended to use her if you feel confident in your skills, as her biggest drawback, while potent, can be turned into a strength if used well. Her low Stealth can also be used to save Toons who have a harder time getting out of chases, such as Soulvester, Vee, Rodger, and Gigi.

Brightney works best during Blackouts. Her Active Ability, **Night Light**, is an incredibly useful Blackout-exclusive tool. It counters the primary threat of Blackouts, information loss, and helps teammates stay alive in the dangerous environment. Brightney's light during Blackouts is also notably brighter and larger than all other Toons, granting her high visibility and giving teammates a great source of light. Brightney is ultimately the best Toon for countering Blackouts survival-wise (though Vee comes extremely close), and can be crucial in helping the team. However, Vee may be a better option for the extraction side of things, since she can highlight both Twisteds and Machines, albeit for only three seconds shorter than Brightney can highlight. Vee's cooldown is also five seconds longer, but that really doesn't affect much.

Brightney's Blackout-countering Ability, high extraction, and above-average mobility makes her one of, if not **the** best Toon for solo runs, as her low Stealth becomes nearly (but not completely) a non-factor with the absence of other players dragging Twisteds to your location. It is recommended to use run speed Trinkets to boost survivability as her Extraction is already good. On later Floors, knowing which Twisteds are present, and their locations is crucial for knowing how to tackle the Floor.

Not every Floor is a Blackout, but Brightney can still be useful outside them. She has a great Stat pool, with high Stamina and Extraction Speed at the cost of Stealth. To counteract her poor Stealth, Brightney can use her high Stamina to dash in and out of dangerous situations. Additionally, Brightney can temporarily help with diverting Twisteds using her high Stamina and low Stealth to help lure the Twisteds away from other Toons. With high skill, she can even be used to distract normal Twisteds indefinitely and can distract most Twisteds as well. It's also way easier to bring Twisteds to Distractors (namely Pebble) since they'll lock onto you until you get out of their sight in most cases. However, you could get unneeded attention of dangerous Twisteds that are wandering around or being distracted, especially Main Character Twisteds. The ones you should take most caution around are Twisted Pebble, Twisted Coal (in a Blackout), Twisted Bobette, and Twisted Vee (situational due to Train Whistle existing) since the prior three have almost the same speed as you, which will make them extremely hard to even outrun due to Brightney's 3 Movement Speed, so having Items such as Speed Candies, Protein Bars, or Boxes o' Chocolates can potentially help you escape. If you want to extract safely, check your surroundings and Distractor's location frequently to avoid getting cornered. Do note there also aren't any common Trinkets or Items that can aid Brightney's Stealth, due to it being 0 and all Stealth Trinkets and Items being percentage based, therefore providing no effect. The only Items that can help with Brightney's Stealth are Smoke Bomb and Eject Button, both of which are in the ultra rare tier and best saved for near-death situations, or to avoid using up Stamina. If there is a distractor, try to keep tabs on their location and stay away from them. If you do happen to be seen by the Twisteds, cut line of sight as fast as possible for the distractor to re-retrieve the Twisteds. However, her low Stealth can be used to help slower Toons struggling with fast Twisteds, or to help the distractor should they run out of Stamina. Speaking of Stamina, even though Brightney has a lot of it, you should manage it carefully. It's fine to sprint tap around the map to traverse faster, but don't waste all of it should your low Stealth get you in a chase.

Brightney can really help with completing Dyle's Floor. Her Stats allow her to extract all Machine types efficiently, though the low Stealth can endanger her if Twisted Dyle becomes enraged, and other Toons without the same Stealth can easily lead Twisteds onto her. During Blackouts, she will be able to highlight where Twisted Dyle and the other Twisteds are, which can be extremely helpful as players can otherwise get caught off guard; her incredibly bright light radius can also make it a bit easier to navigate the Floor. The +50 Stamina gained from completing the Floor may not be so useful on paper since Brightney already has 175 Stamina, but her Stealth means she's more likely to get chased by Twisteds, which can especially be a problem on later Floors with more dangerous Twisteds.

Brightney is one of the Toons with no best set of Items. She can mostly be used as a blank slate due to her above-average Stats. However, Stamina-restoring Items, such as Protein Bars and Stamina Candies, are useful, as they'll help to maintain her above-average Stamina. Healing Items also tend to be useful, so it's good to keep them in your inventory if needed without clogging it. If you're not used to her abysmal Stealth, taking hits is near-guaranteed.

Overall, Brightney is pretty great at many things; whether it be extracting, gathering Twisteds, or protecting teammates. She's a great counter to Blackouts survival-wise, but also requires patience and communication if you wish to avoid taking Twisted aggro as much as possible.

**Extraction**

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing her Skill Check Extraction (22.96 avg/20.83 with Tech Savvy);

• **Sweet Charm**, to further reduce **Night Light**'s cooldown, though only by a small amount as the Trinket works with units (36.4s), especially if they're afraid a Floor will have dangerous Twisteds such as Twisted Scraps, Twisted Goob, or any Main Character Twisteds.

• **Party Popper**, to assist her during Blackouts when extracting, somewhat serving as a weaker version of **Night Light**.

**Note: Diary or Scrapbook are not recommended Trinkets for Brightney as they do not affect her Stealth Stat, since her 1 Star Stealth means 0 Stealth units, and multiplication of 0 will always be 0.**
