toons.name: Flyte

abilities.name: Gust
abilities.desc: This Toon places a 'Gust' at Flyte's location that lasts for 10 seconds. Any Toon that walks into the Gust receives a 15% Movement Speed boost while in the Gust and for 3 seconds after leaving. Has a cooldown of 50 seconds.

toons.desc: Flyte is an outgoing fellow who has a grounded view on life! He rather stay out of trouble and make sure others stay away from the same trouble as well.
toons.strategies:
Flyte is an excellent All-Rounder Toon with 4 Movement Speed, 3 Star Stealth, and 4 Star Extraction Speed. His Ability, **Gust**, is quite beneficial, increasing Movement Speed for other Toons.

Flyte's 4 Star Movement Speed and 4 Star Extraction Speed means that he can distract and extract better than most other Toons. However, because these increases come at a cost of their other Stat counterpart (Stamina and Skill Check), there are still some things that get impeded. With 2 Star Stamina, escaping faster Twisteds/sprint tapping will be slightly harder to do as you lose around 2.5 seconds of Stamina that could be used by a 3 Star Stamina Toon. However, his 4 Star Movement Speed and Ability can make this slightly easier to deal with. On the extracting side, 2 Star Skill Check makes using common Skill Check Trinkets like Magnifying Glass riskier due to the smaller size you have to hit. 4 Star Extraction Speed is fine, but if it repeatedly gets halted by Skill Check failures, it won't be as good. However, practicing small sizes or using other Trinkets like Thinking Cap can help.

Though also generally useful, his Active Ability can come in handy for 1 Star Movement Speed Toons like Connie, Soulvester, and Shrimpo, since they may have trouble getting away from fast Twisteds like Twisted Cocoa and Twisted Shelly. In addition, the gust can affect himself, unlike other speed boosting Abilities that can only affect Toons other than the user; this is one of the biggest pros of Gust despite its relatively low potency.

Other applications for Flyte's Ability include:

•Escaping Twisteds, being able to be used like Flutter's **Floaty Dash** Ability;

•Using it in front of other Toons to both boost them and insert oneself in front of the Twisteds to take aggro. Positioning matters; try not to put your boost behind them;

•To grant a speed boost to teammates at the start of a Floor to give your distractor an early start and generally to get the most out of it;

•Helping others get to the Elevator in time, by putting it a decent distance away (so other Toons get the most use out of it) if possible. Pay attention to who's outside/approaching and time it when most of them are close, as the gust does disappear after a while. Therefore, try to save your Ability for Panic Mode once a majority of Machines have been completed;

•Boosting the distractor while they're dealing with dangerous scenarios. Try not to randomly boost them without warning; the speed may throw them off if they're not dealing with specific threats. Use your Ability on distractors at the beginning of Floors, near the Elevator during Panic Mode, when they're dealing with Twisted Vee/ Twisted Pebble, and if they seem to be struggling or to take aggro from them if you're backup. Try not to "help" them otherwise unless they communicate differently. When boosting them, try to anticipate their path and put it there before they even get close so that you don't get in their way unless your Stealth is higher. This tactic can also be used if you are distracting.

•Placing the gust on a Treadmill Machine to make himself or another Toon more efficient at extracting them.

•Placing the gust under a Toon who is low on Stamina or ran out of Stamina, to allow them to safely walk faster while regenerating, though this requires good communication. This can also be applied to himself.

•Placing it in blackouts to light up the paths.

Flyte's Ability affects other Toons equally, acting as a physical "power-up" that others must touch to receive the buff. His Ability works on himself as well, making it easy to use during chases where multiple Toons are at risk. Note that a 15% Movement Speed boost for 3 seconds won't always be enough to escape Twisteds.

Flyte's gust during a Blackout can also produce light. While it's not much light, it can still help other players navigate through the Floors or make it easier for players to know where an Item could be like a Bandage or a Health Kit if they had a hard time trying to find the Item in the dark. Highlighting the Elevator or correct path during Panic Mode may be helpful for new players with low graphics settings.

During Ichor Leaks, you could try to place the gust by Ichor Puddles in order to reduce the slowness applied by them. This can especially help if any puddles are in an important path, such as a distractor's looping area, a safe way back to the Elevator, and a healer's route to an injured Toon. Do note that this won’t fully neutralize or counter the slowness (Toons will still get -2% Movement Speed), but it can reduce it to a minor inconvenience.

Good Items to focus on are Movement Speed Items to allow Flyte to outwalk Twisteds temporarily with his 4 Star speed, or to stack with his Ability's boost. Stamina Items can help with the below average capacity, making things a bit safer especially as a distractor. Extraction related Items, particularly if they boost Extraction Speed like Instructions will help improve Flyte's above average extraction.

Overall, he functions pretty similarly to other Toons with speed boosting support Abilities, just without certain traits like an effective counter to Ichor Leaks or a way to directly help with Stamina. He still has his own strengths and advantages, being a great Toon in solo runs.

**Gust Effect**

•

•The final amount of Movement Speed after an increase from Gust is as follows:

• (10 Walk/20 Run) → 11.5 Walk/23 Run

• (12.5 Walk/22.5 Run) → 14.375 Walk/25.875 Run

• (15 Walk/25 Run) → 17.25 Walk/28.75 Run

• (17.5 Walk/27.5 Run) → 20.125 Walk/31.625 Run

• (20 Walk/30 Run) → 23 Walk/34.5 Run

**Trinket Combinations**

Recommended Trinket combinations for Flyte:

**Mobility**

• **Dog Plush/Options**

•This Trinket will unlock the role of distractor to the holder (19.3 Walk Speed). Here are some options to pair Dog Plush with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to allow Flyte to outwalk Twisteds slower than Twisted Toodles and Twisted Shelly (20.2 Walk Speed);

• **Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool**, to out-walk even faster Twisteds. Keep in mind this only works half the time, and is best used when duo-distracting (21 Walk Speed);

•Do note this Trinket combo is best used when duo-distracting with another player.

• **Vanity Mirror**, to out-run almost all Twisteds during Panic Mode while active (35.75 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, so you can distract Twisted Vee without being slowed, and prevents being slowed by Ichor Leaks;

• **Diary**, to support 3 distractors without taking off Twisteds' aggro;

•Only use this Trinket combination if your distractor has 3 Star Stealth.

• **Scrapbook**, to avoid other 3 Stealth Toons taking away the Twisteds' aggro;

•Only use this Trinket combination if your teammates are unorganized or have 3 and below Stealth.

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Flyte to take full advantage over his 4 Extraction Speed (1.2 extraction speed) and 2 Star Skill Check (67 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

•This combination is also good for shorter solo runs, as Vee's Remote speeds up Floor progression significantly during early Floors, but becomes less effective once you reach higher Floors.

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction. However, it leaves you with a near 1 Window Size (24.19 avg/21.51 with Tech Savvy);

• **Thinking Cap**, to increase Skill Check size, helping you hit your Skill Checks easier if you struggle with such;

• **Mime Makeup**, to avoid attracting Twisteds to your location when you miss a Skill Check, also helps if you desire to complete Dyle's Floor at ease.

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Distraction/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability/Support**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can**, to reduce **Gust'**s Ability cooldown (45s).

• **Sweet Charm**, to further reduce **Gust'**s cooldown, though only by a medium amount as the Trinket works with percentages (43).

toons.name: Ginger

abilities.name: Baked with Care!
abilities.desc: This toon can heal a nearby targeted Toon to full Hearts for 100 tapes with a cooldown of 100. For every extra Ginger, the cost increases by 50 Tapes and the Cooldown increases by 30.

toons.desc: Ginger may be a little shy but has an eye for design! Her art is frosted into delicate details on her favorite baked goods! Though the taste may not be as lovely as the looks!
toons.strategies:
On paper, Ginger has one of, if not, the best healer Abilities in-game, being a direct upgrade to Sprout's Ability with the bonus of average extracting potential. Her Ability, **Baked with Care!**, heals any Toon to full Health with 100 Tapes, a really good Ability, capable of making your team last longer than normal. However, Tape collection, low mobility, low range, and the need to wind up your heal can have major setbacks, to the point that in most situations, she is the worst healer option in the game.

Usually, it's best to use your Ability when someone is at 1, as any other Health level wastes some of Ginger's potential. However, there are other situations where that would not be ideal. A distracting Looey would benefit from a lost Heart, so a Cosmo or Sprout would be a better fit for him. Another situation would be a run with Main Character Toons being the majority. In that case, Cosmo can substitute if the team worries about Health Kit wastage and Sprout can substitute to utilize Tapes in a beneficial way, as well as having the capability of distracting in a pinch.

Unlike Sprout or Cosmo, Ginger's low mobility means Twisteds are an even bigger threat, with Twisteds like Twisted Dyle being extra difficult. This also makes traversal difficult, so Machine or Item opportunities will be scarce, and therefore makes Tape collection a hurdle. However, if your team is kind enough, you may have a decent shot at collecting the Tapes. Sprout's high mobility gives him a bonus of being able to back-up distract for his team, while Ginger's only other role is extracting. Though Sprout's bad extraction does force him to only be a distractor, so if the Floor is too risky or the Sprout is too scared, his last available role, extracting, would make the run a bit long unless there’s Treadmill Machines. However, Ginger doesn't deal with the problem of bad extraction and can finish most Machines at a decent pace, though it still would be faster to let a nearby Extractor such as Shelly or Yatta do the machine instead. Despite this, if the run is operational with quick, 1 Heart heals, Sprout would still be better suited.

Due to her Stats, your form of tape collection should be different from the other 3 Toons with Tape requiring Abilities. Picking up niche or common Items, as well as Tapes near the Elevator or near the distractor, when you know nobody else needs them, is a safe option, but take care that it isn't your number one priority. Pick up Tapes or Items on the way to a destination like an injured Toon, Machine, or the Elevator—use them as a supplemental income rather than a primary income. Since Ginger's speed is low, she benefits from mobility based Items, which means she can use them to move around more easily while also gaining Tapes, without it feeling like wastage. Taking advantage of your Stealth to focus on extracting in open areas or Machines near a distractor's looping area is a good choice too; other Toons with lower Stealth will be less inclined to extract such Machines, since they could be more susceptible to being chased or taking aggro. Each Machine gives you 10 Tapes if you fully fill it, so it's recommended to hone your focus on extracting, especially with the aforementioned Stealth. You can also stand just outside of the Elevator during Panic Mode to gain Tapes from encountering Twisteds, immediately running inside once you get them. Toons like Bassie, Cocoa, and Yatta can facilitate Item grinding, since they can drop Items near Ginger, keeping her from wandering slowly and excessively using up Stamina.

Something to note is that unless you have the 100 Tapes, you can't highlight any Toons and even with the Tapes, can only highlight the nearest Toon granted they're close to you. Therefore, if you need to heal someone, calling out your availability makes it easier. Another way is to tell someone you want to heal them, and ask them to stay back. Running to a Toon to heal them, especially if they are quite fast, will just be a waste of time and Stamina.

Be aware healing distractors would be quite difficult, as they usually need a lot of space, not being able to stand still to let Ginger heal them, so following the distractor would be one of the only options. The other option would be to circle the object the distractor is circling in the opposite direction, though this may still prove unsafe if there are faster Twisteds. Even so, the distractors are likely going to be faster than you, so the attempt could waste a lot of Stamina, not to mention looping distractors might make the Twisteds lock onto you and risk a Heart, especially if the Twisteds being distracted include ones that generally must be looped, such as Twisted Pebble and Twisted Scraps. It is better to just wait for the Floor to end and heal them after the next Floor starts, but if the Distractor is in urgent need of healing, Ginger's various drawbacks often make it nearly impossible to heal them appropriately or in time before the Distractor dies. This could be combated if there is an available backup distractor to take over while the main one loses the Twisteds to get healed by Ginger, but if one isn't available, it could be very risky for Twisteds to be loose, especially faster ones.

One of the only situations where Ginger might be able to heal the distractor in action safely is if a distractor such as Eclipse or Goob is solar system distracting with Bobette. This strategy often does not require an island or much space to circle around, so a Ginger could stand next to Bobette or follow Bobette's path (depending on if Bobette is still or moving) and heal that way, however there is still a chance that the distractor leaves Ginger's range due to how small it is.

Generally, Ginger isn't the best healer in more dangerous scenarios, so its a good idea to bring a Sprout or Cosmo (Cosmo is more recommended) to heal in dangerous situations, while Ginger can offer more effective healing at resting points, especially the Break Room. She acts somewhat like a medical station or hospital in comparison to the other healers. However, experience with slower Toons can make her a really good Toon.

**Trinket Combinations**

Recommended Trinket combinations for Ginger:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Ginger to outrun nearly all Twisteds except Twisted Pebble and any twisteds that have adjacent speeds to him before Panic Mode (24.2 run speed) and helps her retain hearts. Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to outrun Twisted Pebble before Panic Mode (25.4 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Bobette or similar/higher speed Twisteds during Panic Mode and assist teammates (31.4 run speed);

• **Bone**, to help quickly scout for Items at the start of a new floor and allow you to collect Items faster;

• **Diary**, although quite situational, can help if there is a distractor with 4 Stealth such as Bassie so you can safely go near them to collect heals while they distract;

• **Train Whistle**, to help Ginger avoid Twisteds during an Ichor Leak, or while Twisted Vee on the Floor;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Ginger to take full advantage over her 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote, and better Tapes collection;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability/Support**

• **Sweet Charm**, to reduce **Baked with Care!'**s Ability cooldown (92s).

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can**, to further reduce **Baked with Care!**'s cooldown, though only by a small amount as the Trinket works with units (87s).

• **Dandy Plush**, to help you buy healing Items if a Toon that needs Tapes is present, letting you still have sufficient Tapes from usual activities for healing Items.

**Note: It isn't recommended to use Tape-providing Trinkets such as Fancy Purse as it only provides enough for one heal, but can be useful if a teammate takes a hit on earlier floors before you have 100 Tapes. You can also use it to buy a heal from Dandy's Store should it appear, as you cannot heal yourself. Although this Trinket can be used, it is highly recommended to use a Trinket from the Mobility or Extraction sections as the Fancy Purse's effect is one-time use.**

toons.name: Razzle & Dazzle

abilities.name: Comedy/Tragedy
abilities.desc: This Toon swaps between Movement Speed on odd numbered Floors, and Extraction Speed on even numbered Floors.

toons.desc: While Razzle is always ready to take center stage, his second half Dazzle isn't always so excited to be in the spotlight. These two may see things differently but they know they'll always have each other.
toons.strategies:
Razzle & Dazzle have a vacillating playstyle. Their varying Stats give them great potential, enabling them to demonstrate two extreme builds with their hybrid playstyle of swapping between distracting and extracting. In the following segments, Razzle and Dazzle are referred to as **Razzle** when they are on **odd Floors** (speed) and **Dazzle** on **even Floors** (extraction).

Their Passive Ability causes the user to swap their strengths between Extraction and Distraction/Survival on Even and Odd Numbered Floors respectively. Razzle's high Movement Speed (5) is perfect for Distracting Twisteds on odd-numbered Floors or duo distracting with Pebble and other fast toons, and Dazzle's high Extraction Speed is great for Extracting Machines on even-numbered Floors. The major disadvantage of playing Razzle & Dazzle is Dazzle's extremely low Movement Speed, which is much lower than other similar extractors, and Razzle's subpar Extraction Speed. It's due to this factor that it's recommended to play Razzle & Dazzle on a team as opposed to playing on your own, as Dazzle's speed deficit is often fatal if they're chased by a Twisted, and machines will take approximately 1 minute when on odd floors. Razzle & Dazzle's Ability allows them to assume the most powerful stats of a Main Character across each Floor. Their Ability breaks Floors up a little more to make things more exciting, but it comes at a large opportunity cost.

As for Items, Razzle & Dazzle can use anything well. It's recommended to take Healing Items, as those are always generally useful, and to collect Movement Speed/Stamina Items during Razzle's turn to make Dazzle's safer.

The main thing determining Razzle & Dazzle's Ability is their Trinkets. Movement Speed-boosting Trinkets (such as Ribbon Spool, Clown Horn, etc.) are highly recommended as they can boost their mobility, which is helpful for both, and extraction-boosting Trinkets ( Vee's Remote, Magnifying Glass, etc.) can help them extract nicely. Although there's no best set of Trinkets for Razzle & Dazzle, but it's best to use two speed Trinkets or one movement and one extraction, as this can help flesh out one of their Roles better. It's better to pick Trinkets that synergize with one another.

Razzle & Dazzle's best support looks like another distractor that handles Dazzle's Floors. If this is the case, the Razzle user may wish to equip Clown Horn and Dog Plush and the other Toon can equip Ribbon Spool in place of Clown Horn. While this is a common setup for duo distracting, it comes with the benefits of Razzle & Dazzle's extra heart compared to Pebble and extra Extraction during downtime. Downsides include an extreme lack of survivability if your other distractor dies, an inability to take over/backup distract if they're low on Health, and being devoid of a good way to gather Items downtime normally provides.

Razzle's speed is sufficient to distract all singular Twisteds (including Twisted Pebble, though combinations may get dicey) so their user might opt to instead solely equip Trinkets that benefit Dazzle.

Overall it is really only recommended to play Razzle & Dazzle if you're experienced and can deal with their constant-changing Statistics.

**Trinket Combinations**

For specific Trinket recommendations, here are some possible combinations:

**Distraction**

• **Dog Plush/ Clown Horn**

•This set gives Razzle & Dazzle the highest Movement Speed in odd floors, he will out-walk almost all Twisteds and have the same walk speed as Twisted Pebble (24 walk speed).

**Mobility**

• **Pink Bow/ Ribbon Spool**

•This Trinket combination really helps Dazzle's lackluster speed (23.5 run speed). Here are some other Trinkets if you want to replace any of them:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further increase Dazzle's Run Speed (22.6 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, so Dazzle can more easily traverse the map during Panic Mode (26 run speed);

• **Clown Horn**, to out-walk Twisted Glisten and Twisted Vee when you are inflicted with the Slow II Debuff when active and on an odd numbered Floor (24.2 walk/33 run speed);

• **Diary**, to not interfere with 3 Stealth Distractors;

•Only use this Trinket set if there is a distractor that meets such criteria in the first place.

• **Train Whistle**, to simultaneously make Twisted Vee significantly easier to distract as Razzle, Slow in general less dangerous for Dazzle, and Ichor Leaks less dangerous all together;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Razzle & Dazzle to take full advantage over his 1/5 Extraction Speed (odd:0.75, even:1.5 extraction speed) and 3 Star Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (odd:29.8 avg/27.21 with Tech Savvy, even:19.91 avg/17.7 with Tech Savvy);

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Distraction/Mobility** section, to help with mobility; etc.

toons.name: Rodger

abilities.name: Detective
abilities.desc: This Toon gains twice the amount of Research from Capsules and encountering Twisteds.

toons.desc: This Toon is the one to call when there is a mystery afoot. Rodger is a clever detective who is always eager to solve whatever case that may arise.
toons.strategies:
Rodger's main purpose lies in collecting Research (and for lack of other proficiencies, Ichor). He makes a good training character as using him is most beneficial for new players: his low Movement Speed helps players learn to regulate Stamina and his extra Research gain is most beneficial to those that don't have much. The rest of this section should be considered with the fact that he is more aptly-applied with the inexperienced in mind.

Rodger's main Stat, which is his Extraction Speed (4), is above average and will help with completing Machines faster. The only downside is his low Movement Speed, which means finding and using Speed Items will help with traversing around the Floor better (although you may wish to save them for emergencies). He is not very efficient as an extractor compared to other Toons with the inclination due to his propensity for seeking research and the hindrance of having difficulty traversing the map.

Rodger's **Detective** Passive grants him double the Research percentages from collecting Research Capsules and encountering Twisteds. Normally, you would gain **1%** from Research Capsules and **5%** from encountering Twisteds, but with his Passive Ability, it's doubled to **2%** and **10%**. This makes Rodger useful for collecting Research much faster on a Twisted that isn't fully Researched yet. However, this effectively renders him ability-less (similarly to Boxten). For that reason, if you have no motivation to collect Research (either because you have all of it or don't want it), Rodger probably isn't the best Toon for the job. If you do want Research, no other Toon surpasses him—so long as you have the teammates to back it up.

If one is using him primarily to search for Research, Movement Speed Trinkets may help to locate capsules before the Floor expires. Alternatively, Trinkets like Vee's Remote can be equipped to pass Floors faster to encounter more of your target Twisted. Research Map can help you know where the Capsules are, so that you don't need to waste Stamina going to empty rooms.

**Trinket Combinations**

For specific Trinket recommendations, here are some possible combinations:

**Mobility**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Rodger to outrun all Twisteds but Twisted Pebble before Panic Mode (24.2 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further increase Run Speed and outrun Twisted Pebble before Panic Mode (25.4 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Bobette during Panic Mode and assist teammates (31.4 run speed);

• **Diary**, to not interfere with 3 Stealth Distractors;

•Only use this Trinket set if there is a distractor that meets such criteria in the first place.

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

•Any of the trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Rodger to take full advantage over his 4 Extraction Speed (1.2 extraction speed) and 3 Star Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (22.96 avg/20.83 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Mobility** section, to help with survival.

toons.name: Teagan

abilities.name: Tea Time
abilities.desc: This Toon can spend 75 Tapes to heal themself by 1 Heart. Has a Cooldown of 100.

unlock: Buy 25 Items from Dandy's Elevator Shop
toons.desc: Teagan loves to throw the most enjoyable little get-togethers. Tea parties are this Toon's specialty as she knows the perfect type of tea each Toon prefers.
toons.strategies:
Teagan is a pretty versatile All-Rounded Toon, but doesn't exactly focus on a certain niche as a result. She can be good for solo runs due to her impressive survivability, and also the fact that her playstyle can vary based on what you want. The only real issue is her 2 Star Stealth, which may result in her taking away the Twisteds from a distractor and being encountered easily by them, meaning you'll have to be wary of your surroundings when playing as her.

Teagan's Active Ability, **Tea Time**, makes her a great choice for inexperienced players or those who may end up dying more easily during runs. This Ability allows the player to heal themself at the cost of 75 Tapes, which, during certain types of runs, won't be so hard to gather, though do note her longer Ability cool down, as it can hinder your survivability if you aren't aware of it.

Teagan can be a great protector thanks to their Stats and Ability, with the capability of guarding any teammates who are extracting and have equal or higher Stealth. They can also hover around teammates on 1 Heart, bait ranged Twisted attacks to give distractors a head start, and escort slower teammates to the elevator during Panic Mode. They can easily take a hit for others, healing back up with her Ability.

Due to her Tape requiring Ability, players must gain as many Tapes as they can throughout the floors. As Tapes can be found everywhere on the map, mobility and exploration are key to using her effectively. It's important to note that Health Kits and Bandages are quite scarce in the first place, and by the time you reach around Floor 12+, you have a lot of Tapes that you have not spent, so asking teammates to let you pick up extra Tapes will help turn the excess into a very big help.

Other activities that produce Tapes are picking up Items, encountering each Twisted for the first time on the Floor, using her Ability (though it's not sustainable as a source), finishing Machines, and surviving the Floor. Thus, it is recommended to pick up any Items that aren't valuable to your teammates if you have room in your inventory to immediately use them ( Gumballs, Skill Check Candies, and Stealth Candies being some of the least useful) and complete as many Machines as possible. Picking up Jumper Cables is a great option, while buying a Valve from the pre-game shop and/or using Vee's Remote or Wrench may be even more helpful. It is not recommended to go out of your way to encounter Twisteds, but waiting by the Elevator during Panic Mode and stepping out quickly once all of your teammates are safe to aggravate them and then getting back to safety can help get you the extra you need.

Whatsoever, having a Sprout or Ginger in your run might seem complicated, as both require even more Tapes to use their Active Abilities. Because Sprout and Ginger have to distribute heals out to a lot more people, allow them to pick up Tapes as you should get enough simply by doing tasks while playing the game. You can still obtain Tapes from encountering Twisteds, doing Machines or simply surviving the Floor. Infact, Teagan can even be somewhat helpful to healer Toons, as they have one less Toon to worry about (often) per individual Teagan. Teagan can still benefit from being healed by a healer if they are low on Tapes or on 1 Heart, but they overall have less of a need for it.

Teagan excels at doing Dandy Runs, as Health Kits and Bandages are already pretty rare to find on Floors. Since she benefits from Tapes in a run that makes them useless, ask your teammates to leave all Tapes for her to pick up unless Sprout or Ginger are also present, as their Abilities also rely on Tapes.

Teagan is a decent choice for completing Dyle's Floor, as even though their extraction Stats are average, they are by no means terrible. Her above average Stamina can make her quite efficient on Treadmill Machines, and the Stealth can help with saving teammates. Do note that while her Ability can help with the relatively large amount of Twisteds, it’s ineffective against Twisted Dyle due to his insta-kill. With the abundance of Machines, tape income will be high, and the +50 Stamina gained will make your survivability even more potent, even if it may be somewhat unnecessary on earlier Floors with the already above average Stamina.

Unless you are in a solo run, it is not recommended to take any Health Kits or Bandages as they are better left for your teammates due to Teagan's ability to heal herself. However, if you are low on health and Tapes, you can still take one.

**Trinket Combinations**

Teagan's best Trinkets depend on what you want to use them for:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Teagan to outrun all Twisteds, except Twisted Dyle at max speed before Panic Mode (26.9 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further improve run speed (28.2 run speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted during Panic Mode except the aforementioned Twisted (35 run speed);

• **Diary**, to not disrupt 2 Stealth Distractors and scavenge Tapes easier;

•Only use this Trinket set if there is a distractor that meets such criteria in the first place.

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Teagan to take full advantage over her 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote, and better Tapes collection;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Support**

• **Soul Sword** or **Blushy Bat**, to allow Teagan to slow a Twisted of her choice by getting hit by them. Then, with enough Tapes, she can heal herself and remove any damage done. This results in the Twisted being slightly easier to deal with for you and your teammates, and makes her function somewhat like a sentinel.

•Do **not** use both Trinkets together, as Soul Sword's effect clashes quite unwell with Blushy Bat's.

**Ability**

• **Sweet Charm,** to reduce **Tea Time'**s Ability cooldown (92s):

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can**, to further reduce **Tea Time**'s cooldown, though only by a small amount as the Trinket works with units (87s).

**Other**

• **Dandy Plush/Any**, to discount prices in Dandy's Shop, saving you more Tapes to heal yourself during Floors, since healing Items are more cost efficient (Tapes per heart gained) than **Tea Time** (75 tapes per heart).

**Note: It is not recommended to use Tape-providing Trinkets such as Fancy Purse as it only provides enough for one heal, making itself useless later into the run.**

toons.name: Toodles

abilities.name: Beginner's Luck
abilities.desc: This Toon can roll for a 15% boost to a random Stat that lasts for 10 seconds. Has a cooldown of 25.

toons.desc: Toodles is the youngest of Dandy's World. She often wants to be apart of the fun, and loves proving that she is capable for her age in helping out!
toons.strategies:
Toodles is a decent starter Toon with basic Stats and Ability. She leans into the Survivalist playstyle, though her slightly lower Extraction Speed makes her below average at extracting. Her Stealth in particular, along with her cheap price and easily achievable requirement, makes her useful to new players.

Toodles' Ability, **Beginner's Luck**, grants her +15% to a random Stat for 10 seconds, which is an important part of her playstyle. The buff granted is indicated by the color of the particles Toodles gains. Below are the buffs that she can gain and their colors:

•**Orange - Skill Check** (Increases chance & size only) (40% chance and 172.5 size)

•**Yellow - Movement Speed** (17.25 walk speed/28.75 run speed)

•**Green - Stamina** (Increases Stamina capacity only) (173 capacity)

•**Blue - Stealth** (17.25 Stealth)

•**Purple - Extraction Speed** (0.978 Extraction Speed (9.775 units filled in 10 seconds))

Toodles needs to have a good amount of adaptability to make use of her Ability. Depending on the situation, it could grant something useful or useless, which has to be kept in mind. It's generally good to use it either as often as possible or whenever you're in danger (depending on how risky the current Floor is), since the worst it can do is nothing. You shouldn't rely on the Ability due to its unpredictable nature, but it's definitely a useful tool.

Since Toodles' Ability can either grant her something that aids in Extraction or escape (Skill Check and Extraction Speed vs. Movement Speed, Stamina Capacity, and Stealth) you really have a 3/5 chance of getting something helpful for your current activity. Just be sure to keep the possibility of a Stealth increase in mind as it can cause Twisteds to switch targets if you're near Toons such as Cosmo or Ginger. Her above-average Stealth can help her bring Twisteds to distractors though. Since her Ability might not be helpful and doesn't last long enough to switch activities, it's much less potent than most (about as powerful as Gumballs). Its extremely short cooldown does offer some value though, with Trinkets like Peppermint Icing. Toodles can benefit a lot from the Rehearsal/Practice Cards as taking both will reduce her cooldown to 15 seconds, a much more useful frame.

Her Ability can become more useful through strategy, by standing near a non-Treadmill Machine and Treadmill Machine, or a mixed Duo Machine with a treadmill attachment before using your Ability, you can apply your boost (minus Stealth) to whichever Machine will make better use of it (Movement Speed and Stamina for treadmills, Extraction Speed and Skill Check for other types).

Generally prioritizing Treadmill Machines, Barnaby Machines, and extracting Duo Machines with other players can help make Toodles' subpar extraction more bearable. If you run enough, you'll likely finish Treadmill Machines faster than Default or Circle Machines. With Duo Machines (not including Treadmill attachments), as long as you're extracting with another player, you both collectively would at minimum complete a Machine in a baseline of 28~ seconds, or at maximum a baseline of 19~ seconds. Barnaby Machines are inherently the fastest Machines to complete thanks to the frequency of their coins (golden Skill Checks), and they work well with Toodles' lean towards the Skill Check Stat, though note these can be difficult.

On the Stealth side of things, you can be very helpful to a team by taking care of Machines far from the Elevator, out in the open, or near a distractor. Other Toons with lower Stealth can be in a chase, but won't risk switching aggro to you unless they cut a corner; take advantage of that to handle Machines other Toons may struggle with–you make up for your lacking extraction by avoiding getting interrupted and chased in the first place. However, if a teammate is really struggling or vulnerable (i.e low on Stamina, on 1 Heart, out-sped by a Twisted you can outrun), you could try to take a Twisted away from them, though keep an eye on your Stamina and don't rely on your Ability to give you a mobility boost every time.

Overall, Toodles is good for starters, but for late game she is outclassed by most if not all Toons who have better extraction and Abilities. In terms of high Stealth Toons, she has a pretty decent capability survival-wise, but doesn't have any other particularly potent strengths compared to those with equal or higher Stealth.

**Trinket Combinations**

Recommended Trinket combinations for Toodles:

**Survivability**

• **Pink Bow/Options**

•This Trinket enables Toodles to outrun all Twisteds outside of Panic Mode besides Twisted Dyle at max speed (26.9 run speed). Here are some options to pair Pink Bow with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to further increase Run Speed (28.1 Run Speed);

• **Vanity Mirror**, to outrun every Twisted except Twisted Dyle during Panic Mode (35 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, to make escaping with the Slow Debuff easier without losing much Stamina;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Toodles to take full advantage over her 2 Extraction Speed (0.85 extraction speed) and 3 Star Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (27.95 avg/24.84 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Survivability/Mobility** section, to help with survival.

**Ability**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can/ Peppermint Icing**

•The cooldown reduction synergizes with Peppermint Icing, allowing Toodles to regain Stamina more often. With the Rehearsal/Practice cards, **Beginner's Luck** reaches a cooldown of 10 seconds, which means you can stay the whole game refreshing the boost as soon as it ends.

•These Trinkets can additionally be used separately if you want to solely maximize either her Stamina or her cooldown.

**Other**

• **Lucky Coin**, to give her an extra boost, given that this Trinket synergizes quite well with her Ability. If stacked, the boost totals to 28.8%.

•The stacked boosts would result in (193.2 Skill Check Size & 54% Chance), (19.32 Walk Speed/32.2 Run Speed), (193 Stamina Capacity), (19.32 Stealth), or (1.095 Extraction Speed (10.95 units filled in 10 seconds)). In all such cases Toodles nearly gains an extra or 2, albeit temporarily.

abilities.name: Scout
abilities.desc: This Toon can sniff out items across the map, causing items to be highlighted for all Toons for 10 seconds. Has a cooldown of 30.

toons.desc: Coal is Bobette's trusty pet rock! She can often be seen helping Bobette take presents to all their friends! Coal may not be as excited about the holidays as everyone else though!
toons.strategies:
Coal is a decent distractor and support Toon. With 4 Movement Speed and Stamina, she has the capability to be a good distractor if used correctly. Her Statistics are exactly the same as Flutter's, however, her Active Ability, **Scout**, does not help much with distraction, unless certain Trinkets are being used, like Peppermint Icing.

Coal, with her **Scout** Ability, can help find Tapes for Sprout, Blot, Ginger, and Teagan, help locate Health Kits and Bandages for Cosmo and Bassie, find helpful Items for Toons with lower stats, and is overall very useful during Events. Her Ability is similar to Pebble's Passive Ability, **Fetch!**, though Pebble's Ability is constant with nearby items (only highlighted for himself) whilst Coal's is temporary (but highlighted for everyone in the run).

Coal is best used in a team as opposed to runs with few players, as her Active Ability is great at benefiting the whole team. Pebble's Active Ability is better for survivability than support, but can be used for such. Usually, the average Coal player uses their Active Ability when a new Floor starts, but sometimes it's best to not use it on scarier Floors or in Blackouts as people usually won't pay attention or notice it. It may be a great idea to use Scout during the middle-to-end of a Floor, to ensure no items or tapes have been missed (this is especially beneficial to Sprout and Teagan, as they can locate Tapes and Items they may have forgotten to pick up).

Her Ability benefits when players set unique highlight colors in the accessibility settings, since they'll be more easily differentiated and apparent. Since you can change your settings in-game, if you're in a team with or as Coal, you can set the Items, healing Items, Tapes, and Research Capsules as separate highlight colors. If you're a Toon that benefits from any of the aforementioned categories of Items, you can easily beeline straight to them since with the right colors, their outlines will stick out prominently. If you have a teammate who doesn't have custom outlines, struggles with seeing the outlines on bigger Floors, or struggles to remember, you can try to lead them to the specific Items you do see and remember.

Coal is usually outclassed by other Toons, as Flutter is a better distractor and Pebble is better at finding Items/generally contributing. Coal's Ability can be very lackluster despite revealing all Items; the information overload often results in players either missing the bark or not noticing relevant Items, and once it's over you need to wait for it to recharge, which may not be an issue due to her low cooldown duration. As Sprouts and Teagans are likely to try to navigate the entire map anyway, Pebble is superior for them. With Pebble, you don't have to rely on memory to locate Items. Coal can be used to find Health Kits and Boxes o' Chocolates more easily due to their larger sizes (if you don't miss spotting them), but the fact that they're revealed to all players can result in fighting or sub-optimal snatching as Coal isn't made for non-public runs.

**Trinket Combinations**

Some good Trinket sets for Coal include:

**Distraction**

• **Dog Plush/Options**

•This Trinket unlocks the role of distractor to the holder (19.3 walk speed). Here are some options to pair Dog Plush with.

• **Speedy Shoes**, to out-walk fast Twisteds and gain the ability to loop Twisted Pebble (20.2 walk speed);

• **Clown Horn**/ **Ribbon Spool**, to outrun during Panic Mode all Twisteds but Twisted Dyle at max speed (21.2 walk/30.3 run speed);

•Do note this Trinket combo is best used when duo-distracting with another player.

• **Vanity Mirror**, to out-run almost all Twisteds during Panic Mode while active (35.75 run speed);

• **Train Whistle**, to completely nullify the Slow Debuff, making Twisted Vee significantly easier to distract, and Ichor Leaks much easier to distract in;

• **Scrapbook**, to be able to distract without other 3 Stealth Toons taking aggro off you;

•Only use this Trinket combo if most of the players in your run have 3 Star Stealth.

• **Peppermint Icing**, to help her maintain her higher Stamina while distracting more dangerous Twisteds;

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction** section; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Coal to take full advantage over her 2 Extraction Speed (0.85 extraction speed) and Skill Check (67 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote** - This set allows for quicker Floor progression, especially if other teammates also carry Vee's Remote.

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction. However, it leaves you with a near 1 Window Size (29.8 avg/27.21 with Tech Savvy);

• **Thinking Cap**, to increase Skill Check size, helping you hit your Skill Checks easier if you struggle with such;

• **Mime Makeup**, to avoid attracting Twisteds to your location when you miss a Skill Check, also helps if you desire to complete Dyle's Floor at ease;

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Distraction** section, to help with survival.

**Ability/Support**

• **Ghost Snakes In A Can,** to reduce **Scout'**s Ability cooldown (25s)

• **Sweet Charm**, to further reduce **Scout**'s cooldown, though only by a small amount as the Trinket works with percentages (22.6s).

**Note: It is NOT recommended to use Trinkets that highlight Items such as Memory Locket, Research Map, and Common Event Trinkets, as Coal can already see Items with her Active Ability.**

toons.name: Cocoa

abilities.desc: This Toon places a Bonbon candy item that can be picked up and used by anyone. When used, the Bonbon boosts extraction speed (+50%) and movement speed (+25%) for 10 seconds. Has a cooldown of 40.

toons.desc: Cocoa loves to hop into all sorts of fun adventures with her friends! Such a sweet Toon always has sweet surprises to share! "Sharing is caring!" That's what Cocoa likes to say!
toons.strategies:
Given her above average Movement Speed and Stealth, Cocoa is seemingly made to lean into being a support Toon rather than a distractor or extractor. With her Ability, **Bonbon**, Cocoa is able to give other players a slight boost with the BonBons she drops, whether it's a boost for Extraction Speed or Movement Speed.

Placing down BonBons near players on Machines with slow Extraction Speed or when slow Movement Speed Toons are being chased is a way to help out your team, or placing down unneeded BonBons when your team doesn't need any to a Sprout or a Ginger is another way on using Cocoa's Ability as it helps with gathering Tapes for their Abilities. Essentially, placing her BonBons next to Machines and around the map can be helpful for other players and even herself.

Remember that Cocoa's Ability can also benefit herself as well. You can use BonBons from her Ability to boost her slower Extraction Speed frequently, speeding up Floor progression. Her BonBons can also provide her with a speed boost equivalent to the boost of a Speed Candy for a double duration, which can help her escape chases easier, especially with her already high mobility. This can also help Cocoa conserve Stamina, which is very helpful due to her below-average Stamina capacity.

Cocoa, despite her Stealth, is capable of being a decent distractor given her BonBons' speed boost. She can place down BonBons and use them to give herself distance from faster Twisteds, mitigate the Slow Debuff, to escape a chase when Panic Mode is active, or anything else. If planning to distract as her with ease, arrange a run with various 4 and above Stealth Toons as it's much easier to get Twisteds off of them this way, and also equip the usual distractor Trinkets, such as Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes or Train Whistle. If you don’t want or need to use the Trinkets suggested, her Ability is always good for speed, though note its fairly long cooldown.

toons.name: Eclipse

abilities.name: Total Eclipse
abilities.desc: This Toon transforms into a werewolf in blackouts, giving off a glow, gaining 2 Stamina Stars, a 20% Movement Speed boost, and briefly highlighting all Twisteds on the floor.

toons.desc: Eclipse tries her best to show others that wolves don't often have to be the bad guys in stories! With a kind heart and love for the moon, Eclipse is always open for stargazing with a new friend!
toons.strategies:
Due to Eclipse's high Movement Speed and low Stealth, she works primarily as a distractor. However, her Skill Check and Extraction Speed are average, with 3 on both, letting her do Machines at moderate speed.

Her Passive Ability, **Total Eclipse**, increases her max Stamina by 60% and Movement Speed by 20% while in a Blackout, along with giving her a slightly bigger glow. With these buffs combined, Eclipse gains 240 base Stamina and 21/33 base Movement Speed, allowing her to surpass Pebble and especially Waxwell's speed and Stamina, and reach the same speed as 1 Looey. Beware however, as she is immobile for 5 seconds when a Blackout starts (due to her transformation animation). During this time she can not be detected and will lose aggro of any Twisted that had spotted her prior. After this transformation, she highlights all Twisteds on the Floor for 5 seconds and the player regains control. During Blackouts, her speed can allow her to easily outrun Twisteds like Twisted Pebble and Twisted Gourdy; using Trinkets like Clown Horn or Ribbon Spool can allow her to outwalk Twisted Pebble, though it may not be worth it due to the chance of Blackouts being random (unless you duo distract with another Eclipse).

Even without Trinkets, Eclipse can outwalk all Twisteds during Blackouts (outside of Panic Mode) aside from Twisted Bobette, enraged Twisted Glisten, Twisted Coal in a Blackout, and Twisted Pebble. However, Twisted Vee and her Slow II could make it a bit harder to distract, especially with limited vision. Also, long-ranged Twisteds like Twisted Goob could be problematic so it's suggested to have a backup distractor deal with them.

She's still quite capable at extracting thanks to her average extraction Stats. In such a case, using extraction Trinkets like Magnifying Glass or Vee's Remote can enhance her capabilities to a more potent extent. Her speed can let her reach Machines more quickly and make it back to the Elevator during Panic Mode, if she extracts far away from it. She can also utilize her speed to extract Treadmill Machines quite quickly, especially in Blackouts where she could finish them in around 15 seconds, if she only runs. Even while focusing on extracting, she can protect teammates, pass Twisteds to distractors, or help take certain problematic Twisteds like Twisted Scraps and distract them, even outside of Blackouts since her non-Blackout speed is still good. Her Ability highlighting Twisteds at the start of a Blackout can also allow her to support her team a bit while being an extractor.

Her larger light radius makes her also capable of surviving and distracting in the dark, though there are other Toons with a larger light radius. Eclipse's higher mobility when combined with having the Light-Producing Aux. Stat makes her one of the best Toons for Blackouts. Though she may not be able to highlight Twisteds throughout the duration of a Floor, she can protect teammates or just generally thrive in Blackouts with little issue.

The best Items to get depends on how you play as Eclipse. If you're distracting, try to keep at least one Stamina/speed related Item on hand, such as Pops and Box o' Chocolates in case you have to sprint tap or get afflicted with Debuffs; keeping a healing Item on hand is also crucial since distracting puts you in harm's way constantly. If you're extracting, getting Instructions and Jumper Cables can make Eclipse a great extractor, especially if they're paired with extraction Trinkets.

Overall, Eclipse is quite versatile, excelling at distracting, especially in Blackouts. Though, she is also quite capable at extracting. She has great survivability, which combined with the decent extraction makes her a great Toon for solo runs.

**Trinket Combinations**

Recommended Trinket combinations for Eclipse:

**Distraction**

• **Dog Plush/Options**

•This Trinket will unlock the role of distractor to the holder. (19.3 walk speed, 23.1 in blackout) Here are some options to pair Dog Plush with:

• **Speedy Shoes**, to allow Eclipse to outwalk Twisteds slower than Twisted Toodles and Twisted Shelly (20.2 walk speed/24.25 in blackout);

• **Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool**, to out-walk even faster Twisteds. Keep in mind this only works half the time, and is best used when duo-distracting (21 walk speed);

•Do note this Trinket combo is best used when duo-distracting with another player.

• **Vanity Mirror**, to out-run almost all Twisteds during Panic Mode while active (35.75 run speed/42.9 in blackout);

• **Train Whistle**, to completely nullify the Slow Debuff, making Twisted Vee significantly easier to distract, and Ichor Leaks much easier to distract in;

• **Scrapbook**, to be able to distract without other 2 Star Stealth Toons taking aggro off you;

•Only use this Trinket combo if most of the players in your run have 2 Star Stealth, or if you're solar distracting with a Bobette lacking or not including Diary with their trinket combination.

•Any of the Trinkets in the **Extraction Section**, to help with Floor progression; etc.

**Extraction**

• **Magnifying Glass/Options**

•This Trinket allows Eclipse to take full advantage over her 3 Extraction Speed (1.00 extraction speed) and Skill Check (100.5 skill check size). Here are some options to pair Magnifying Glass with:

• **Vee's Remote**, to allow for quicker Floor progression, especially if teammates also carry Vee's Remote;

• **Participation Award**, to speed up Machine completion by maximizing Skill Check extraction (25.57 avg/23.26 with Tech Savvy);

•Any Trinkets listed in the **Distraction** section, to help with survival.

**Other**

• **Spare Bulb**, to further increase Eclipse's light radius for maximum visibility, although it may cause some slight lag for older devices.

twisteds.name: Twisted Astro
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 19 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 22.8 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 21.85 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Can hear a Machine's failed Skill Checks from anywhere on the map and drains half of its completion if left unoccupied. When chasing Toons, he applies the Tired III debuff to whoever he's chasing for 10 seconds (15 second cooldown). Periodically, or after a chase, he goes to sleep and starts having a 3-stage nightmare that causes nearby Machines to start losing completion, and nearby Toons to start hallucinating and suffer from stacking stages of the Tired debuff before eventually taking damage in 60-second time windows, forcing Toons to subdue the nightmare with Star Pillows.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Astro is a large, roaming Twisted that wanders the floors aimlessly. Reflecting his support-oriented counterpart, his unique ability allows him to regress Machine progress after he is alerted by a missed Skill Check. Astro will drain about half the current progress of the machine, meaning he'll have a small effect on barely completed machines and a large one on machines that are almost completed. Twisted Astro will also give the Tired III Debuff if you are being chased by him, reducing your Stamina Regeneration by 75%.

After some time without chasing someone, Twisted Astro will fall asleep and begin having a nightmare. While sleeping, a transparent sphere-shaped radius will slowly grow from his location, increasing in size over time. The radius has three sections, with the outermost being the first and least intense; the first section inflicts Tired I; the second inflicts Tired II & induces hallucinations; the third section inflicts Tired III, induces hallucinations, & darkens the screen periodically. After a while, a 60 second timer begins, which counts down to a 1 damage cycle, before repeating continually. Twisted Astro will wake back up 10 seconds after all Twisted Star Pillows are collected from the Floor, or if his Toon counterpart uses his Ability near him.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Astro is a unique threat, as he can detect alerts from anywhere on the Floor, which includes Airhorns, Pebble's Active Ability upon use, and failed Skill Checks. Thus, it is important to be cautious of your surroundings, and warn your teammate(s) if you decide to purposefully alert Twisted Astro to get his attention. Failing a Skill Check will cause him to drain half of the current progress from the Machine you're extracting if he reaches it, so try to avoid certain Machine types if you struggle with them and generally stay focused.

Comparatively, Twisted Astro is not as hard to distract as the other Main Character Twisteds, as his Tired III Debuff isn't too hindering to deal with. Unless you are distracting, you're going to be using Stamina to run away from him, though the Debuff will slow your Stamina regeneration after you escape, leaving you more vulnerable to other Twisteds. On the other hand, distracting him on his own isn't too bad as his speed is just barely above average. However, if paired with Twisteds such as Twisted Vee, combined with his Debuff can cause conflicts as it'll lead you to run out of Stamina much sooner and potentially take a hit or even die. In this occasion, it's important to carry Stamina items such as Pops, Bottles o' Pop, Chocolates, Stamina Candies, or Protein Bars. Having Astro on your team is a huge help as his Ability can fully restore your Stamina, as well as leave an extra 50% regeneration boost for 10 seconds, though it can be situational with the fairly long cooldown. Bobette's Passive can also help, although it's not recommended, as it won't completely nullify the debuff, though the extra Movement Speed from **Festive Aura** can allow you to walk safely without using more Stamina than necessary. It is good to note that Bobette's below-average Stealth can also lead to bigger problems, unless Bobette is equipped with Diary, or you have Scrapbook, and in both scenarios you are a 2 Stealth Toon, though being a 1 Star Stealth Toon would negate the need of either of the aforementioned Trinkets. Dog Plush paired with a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon lets them out-walk him, though by a little, making the Debuff nearly useless, unless other faster Twisteds are chasing you like Twisted Toodles or Twisted Shelly, and during Panic Mode where Twisted Astro gains notable speed increase. If you are distracting as Looey or Eclipse (in Blackouts), Twisted Astro will be much less difficult, especially with Dog Plush, since they can outwalk Twisted Astro with ease along with almost all other Twisteds with the exception of Twisted Pebble (as well as Twisted Gourdy during the Halloween Event, and Twisted Bobette during the Christmas Event) depending on how many the player has in Looey's case, effectively nullifying Twisted Astro's Debuff to an extent.

Even though in some cases it's not that bad, Twisted Astro's Tired III Debuff can be a hassle, even when not distracting. If you manage to escape him but are still under the effects of the Tired III Debuff, there is a chance you might get seen again, but by that point you run out of Stamina. Toons like Yatta and Gigi should be extremely careful when dealing with Twisted Astro, as their low Stamina will go down quickly and its regeneration will be very slow. However, a Toon like Yatta's high mobility makes the Tired III a reduced-threat, but Gigi on the other hand will have trouble. Pink Bow is an okay option for average and slow Toons with low Stamina, but once they're out of Stamina, you want to hope you can cut a corner to lose chase.

After a while, Twisted Astro will fall asleep and start having a nightmare. Initially the nightmare is small, only being a radius that affects Toons who are closer to him, this first section of the nightmare inflicts Tired I for as long as a Toon is within it, which can be mildly dangerous, but a -25% Stamina regeneration reduction isn't that potent, especially if you have Stamina Items on hand or are a Toon who can keep their Stamina up. After about four pulses, a second section appears within the first, while the entire nightmare radius increases; the second section inflicts Tired II and induces hallucinations onto players, with the hallucinations consisting of either random fake Twisteds running quickly at the player before disapearing, or a fake Health Kit appearing on the ground nearby, before spinning and bouncing around when approached. After a few more pulses, a third section appears in the center of the nightmare radius as it grows even more; this third section inflicts Tired III and periodically sends out a black pulse, which drains the completion of Machines caught in its range. After even more time, a counter appears on the left side of players' screens. The counter counts from 60 seconds, with it reaching 0 causing a Heart to be lost, before repeating continually.

To wake Twisted Astro up, you need to collect all of the star pillows that emerge from him when he initially falls asleep. The amount you need to collect scales with the amount of living Toons and will be shown above Twisted Astro's head. All of the pillows will be highlighted, so it isn't too difficult to find them, however it's good to be cautious while heading for a pillow, since other Twisteds can get in the way. After collecting all of the star pillows, he will take a moment to wake up, having a golden aura around himself to indicate this. Once he wakes up, he will simply continue roaming. If Astro is on your team, he can immediately wake up Twisted Astro with his Ability, which can save time and eliminate the risk of death or injuries.

(I’d like to point out that Pebble’s ability also works in waking up Twisted Astro but Twisted Astro gets faster and his eyes glow red if you use Pebble’s ability to wake him up from the nightmare)

Care should be taken during Ichor Leaks, as Twisted Astro's ability to hear failed Skill Checks from anywhere can synergize with the Illness III Debuff applied by the Ichor puddles, making failing Skill Checks far more likely. This additionally increases the odds of him draining progress from Machines, making floors take a bit longer. The Ichor puddles also apply the Slow I Debuff, which can be troublesome or even lethal when combined with Twisted Astro's high speed and Tired Debuff, making escapes more difficult and dangerous. The former isn't an issue if Twisted Astro is currently being distracted or is preoccupied from a different alert, though the latter can be a huge problem for distractors, unless they have Train Whistle equipped. When Twisted Astro is asleep for a while, having a constant Tired Debuff combined with Ichor Puddles scattered can be really difficult, especially since the nightmare he admits can cover puddles with the smoke-like particles. It's a good idea to try to keep Twisted Astro awake for this reason, especially since trying to retrieve all of the star pillows can be harder with Ichor Puddles in the way.

Ribecca is completely immune to Twisted Astro’s Tired Debuff due to her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, making him easier to deal with, though the high speed and attention span still make him a bit of a threat. This means she could save teammates from him; particularly Toons that are slower, have low Stamina, or are on one Heart. Caution should be taken if attempting to save a teammate when there are other dangerous Twisteds, especially due to Twisted Astro’s previously mentioned high attention span and speed. When Twisted Astro is sleeping, Ribecca won't have any issue with Stamina, but you still need to worry about the Twisted Astro's nightmare damaging you.

Using Stamina regenerating Trinkets like Star Pillow, Peppermint Icing or Whispering Flower can help counteract the Tired III and make Twisted Astro easier to deal with. However, which Trinket you choose to use is heavily dependent on your playstyle, preferred role, Stats, Ability, and Ability cooldown. Though you can also just use a Movement Speed increasing Trinket instead, choose whichever best covers your weaknesses or leans into your strengths.

twisteds.name: Twisted Bassie
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 19 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 22.8 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 21.85 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Spawns six flowers around the floor to apply Slow III and Tired II to Toons. Also spawns vines toward the player when spotting them that deal Slow II and later 1 if stepped on. Her vine ability has a cooldown of roughly 30 seconds.
twisteds.research: Twisted Bassie has a unique mechanic where there are specific points on the map where she spawns six flower traps. When walking into or near these flowers, the player will be applied with the Slow III and Tired II Debuffs, decreasing Walk Speed by 50% and Stamina regeneration by 50%. Additionally, when spotting a Toon, Twisted Bassie will freeze and spawn a long vine towards you. At first, they deal Slow II, but after around 3 seconds, large spikes will shoot out, dealing 1 of damage to anyone on them. Then, they will recede, which results in Twisted Bassie locking onto the Toon she had spotted previously, regardless of Stealth, with a heightened attention span.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Bassie is basically a fusion of Twisted Vee, Twisted Scraps, Twisted Sprout, and Ichor Leak fusion, by slowing a Toon upon sight, spawning a damage-causing projectile onto the floor that always shoots towards a Toon, and spawning small patches of flowers around the Floor that cause slowness and hinder Stamina regeneration. Lower Movement Speed Toons, such as Shrimpo, Soulvester, and Connie, may have a hard time traversing and an even harder time escaping her due to their already abysmal 1 Movement Speed. Make sure to be aware of where each flower trap is placed, avoid those places while in a chase, and be wary of Twisted Bassie's location to not get hit by her vines.

Avoiding the flowers she puts is usually easy by noting down any unobstructed islands that are close to you and being wary of their location. Additionally, speed Items like Boxes o' Chocolates or Eject Buttons can help you pass though them easier. However, you may want to save them if you have faster Twisteds with you like Twisted Pebble or enraged Twisted Glisten. If you are being chased by them, try avoiding the flowers if you can.

If a flower blocks off a pathway to/spawns on something important, like a Machine or healing Item, you should try making sure most of the harder Twisteds are farther away so you can do the Machine or take the Item without getting spotted, getting stuck, and getting hit. Also, you can, again, have speed Items so if a Twisted manages to stat chasing you, you can sprint out without getting slowed by her flowers.

However, Twisted Bassie's vines are much harder to deal with. When you notice getting seen by Twisted Bassie (noticeable by the sound she makes when spotting), if possible, try finding out where Twisted Bassie is (especially in Blackouts) and run perpendicularly from her. Note that the vines are relatively thin, so moving out by a bit could still work. However, if you are being chased by other Twisteds/may run into another Twisted, find another path, as the spikes that could jump out of the vines could block your path for a while, enough to make you get hit by another Twisted. However, Twisted Bassie gets stunned while the vines are there, so you can try going towards Twisted Bassie and going around her.

If you have to distract her, her slightly above average speed could be bad, though it isn't that hard to manage if you are playing as a 5 Star Movement Speed Toon or a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon with at least Dog Plush. However, to deal with her vines, you should do it in an open space, as her vines may block off a large portion of your distracting area. Generally, pretend like you are distracting Twisted Scraps and Twisted Sprout by making the vines spawn somewhere unobstructive. However, do note that Twisted Bassie stays still the entire time the vines are there, so if you are looping, make sure Twisted Bassie doesn't block your path. Additionally, make sure no flowers are near you.

This stunning is actually quite good sometimes, as you can use it as a stun for 5 seconds. However, be careful of the vines she spawns.

Ribecca is completely immune to Twisted Bassie's Slow and Tired Debuffs due to her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, making her a reduced threat (though the longer attention span, above average speed, and vines can still be a problem). This allows Ribecca to traverse the Floor with no issue, not having to avoid the flowers, and being able to more easily dodge the vines. She is also potentially able to save teammates who can get inflicted with Debuffs, particularly those with low Movement Speed, Stamina, or Health. However, care should still be taken with Twisted Bassie's vines, as well as other potentially dangerous Twisteds.

In conclusion, Twisted Bassie should be thought of as a delayed long-ranged attack and an Ichor Leak, so if you have experience with those, she should be easy.

twisteds.name: Twisted Bobette
twisteds.speed:
8.5 walking, 25 chasing
Panic Mode: 10.2 walking, 30 chasing
Suppression: 9.78 walking, 28.75 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Can hear Items, Tapes, and Ornaments being picked up. Does not include Research Capsules.
twisteds.research: Twisted Bobette has a distinct ability, when you pick up any Item anywhere on the Floor within a relatively large hearing radius, she will bolt at full speed toward that location unless preoccupied with chasing a player. All items, including Tapes and Ornaments, and excluding Research Capsules alert her when picked up within this range.
twisteds.strategies:
Be wary when picking up Items near Twisted Bobette, as this will trigger her aggressive state in a similar way to failing a Skill Check near a Twisted. After picking up an Item (including Tapes and Ornaments), try to run far away from the location where the Item was picked up. Her ability to run to a collected Item can also be used to your advantage, as you can lure her somewhere by picking up an Item and then evacuating the area. However, this can be dangerous if she spots you or one of your teammates while running to the collected Item's location, so be careful. Toons like Bassie, Cocoa, or Yatta are great Toons for this strategy, as their Abilities drop Items that can be picked up. Another strategy is to listen to her footsteps and pick up Items while she is chasing someone or if someone is distracting her, as she cannot run to your location if she is occupied.

As Tapes are included in the list of Items that Twisted Bobette can run to, it may be a problem for Teagan, Blot, Ginger, and Sprout, as they all need Tapes to use their Abilities. For this reason, try to attempt the aforementioned strategies. You could also get aggro Tapes from seeing Bobette and hiding from sight without getting hit. Do note that you can only get aggro Tapes once from a Twisted, so don't try it again after you've been seen by her for the first time.

Toons with lower than average Movement Speed will have a harder time surviving Twisted Bobette in her chasing state due to her incredibly excessive speed. However, she has a long, 5 second cooldown after successfully hitting a Toon to combat this. For this reason, using Trinkets like Pink Bow will help slower Toons with escaping her more easily. It's also good to avoid getting too close to her even if she's looking away from you, as her circular vision is very large, making sneaking by her difficult.

When distracting Twisted Bobette, it's highly recommended you use Speedy Shoes and Dog Plush, or any similar speed Trinkets. It is recommended you have a backup distractor distracting the other Twisteds to evade disruptions or mess-ups. Having Astro or Tisha on your team will be helpful to keep up Stamina or provide speed boosts when distracting her. While distracting Twisted Bobette, find an island around the map. Hug tightly to the island to slow Twisted Bobette down, but if you feel like she's catching up, sprint around the corners. This can secure a steady rhythm where she sees you every turn on the island, making sure she won't lose line of sight on you. If no islands are available, it is possible to distract her without one by walking in a straight line and not turning or moving in another direction. This can let you regain Stamina whilst occasionally sprinting when she catches up to you. Another strategy is finding a large open area with a few obstacles, and looping Twisted Bobette near said obstacles. This results in contact with her and objects consistently, slowing her down a bit.
