twisteds.name: Twisted Gourdy
twisteds.speed:
None (When passive)
18 walking, 26 chasing
Panic Mode: 21.6 walking, 31.2 chasing
Suppression: 20.7 walking, 29.9 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Has a meter which fully depletes when a Toon gifts him items. When the meter is full, Twisted Gourdy will enrage and gain a huge speed boost. Upon panic mode, he enrages instantly. Once the meter is full, there is no way to get it back down to passive. The stats shown below are for when he is enraged.
twisteds.research: Twisted Gourdy, upon spawning, speaks once as a Toon enters the Floor (specifically 5 or higher), being guaranteed to spawn every 20 Floors. Similar to Twisted Glisten, he has a rage meter on his head, but needs Items for it to decrease. The bar turns red gradually and jitters at 90%. Upon enraging, he gains a huge speed boost and becoming hostile for the rest of the floor while dealing 1 upon damaging a player. Unlike Twisted Glisten, who roams around the map, Twisted Gourdy is a stationary one. He also has higher speed than Twisted Pebble and Twisted Bobette when enraged (26) which nearly matches 4 Run Speed, and 31.2 in Panic Mode, making him the fastest damaging Twisted in-game, depending on whether or not you count Twisted Dyle's max speed, due to it being variable.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Gourdy acts similarly to Twisted Glisten in the sense that players must monitor a bar's drainage before the Twisted will aggro. His bar increases slower and he stays stationary until angered, yet his needs may be more costly depending on your inventory. Gigi and Cocoa are the only Toons able to permanently sustain his passivity so long as they keep feeding him consistently, though he may need to be checked up on often.

Players must give Twisted Gourdy Items to keep him passive. His meter resets completely if any Item is given to him, no matter the value. Much like Twisted Glisten, once his meter completely fills, there is no way to revert him back to his passive state. Note that once all Machines are completed and Panic Mode is activated, Twisted Gourdy will enrage no matter the circumstances. Ensure that any teammates have distanced themselves from him before you complete the last Machine, especially slower ones.

Twisted Gourdy will always take the Item in the first slot available. Assuming you've used the optimal inventory arrangement, your important Items like Bandages or Health Kits should be safe in your second or third slots. Not doing so could put your valuable Items in danger. Similarly, Twisted Gigi also takes your Items in slot order, so it is recommended to consistently try and arrange your Items correctly during runs to ensure the least valued Items are lost first. If you are playing as Bassie, you can rearrange your inventory if needed to avoid giving him valuable items unless it's absolutely necessary. Also, because every Item will drain Twisted Gourdy’s bar equally, players should wait for the bar to fill a bit before giving an Item to Gourdy, though waiting too long could risk his aggro. Keep an eye on him and when he warns players when his halfway point is reached.

Since less Items spawn when less players are present, Twisted Gourdy is balanced to have his meter increase slower depending on the amount of players alive when the Floor begins. If he is to spawn when there's one player left, it will take 3 minutes for his bar to fill without player intervention. However, if 4 out of 5 players were to die on the Floor he spawned, the last remaining player will only have about 106 seconds (slightly longer than 1 minute) before Twisted Gourdy becomes enraged.

Recommended Toons to accompany Twisted Gourdy are:

•Bassie: Her 4 inventory slots can help hold any useless Items, so when Twisted Gourdy appears, Bassie will have the Items ready, and if necessary, she can use her Active Ability to drop and rearrange her inventory to protect her own valuable items. Her high mobility will also assist her in escaping him once he enrages, not including her high Stamina and Stealth stats.

• Blot: In case Twisted Gourdy enrages, Blot can use **Blot Jr.** to stun Twisted Gourdy, giving teammates time to escape him. Similar to Bassie, his high speed and Stamina will help him escape Gourdy when he enrages.

• Brightney: Her Ability can help locate Twisted Gourdy and other dangerous Twisteds so that if a Toon is lost and Twisted Gourdy is close to enraging, they can return to him, while avoiding dangerous Twisteds, and feed an Item to him. However, note her Ability works in Blackouts only, though her good Extraction can make Floors finish faster and her 1 Stealth can help save vulnerable Toons, though her Stealth can be just as much as a weakness, specifically in solo scenarios.

• Bobette: (Situational): Her Active Ability is able to make her safe from Twisted Gourdy in case he enrages. However, due to her being stationary, other potentially more dangerous Twisteds can approach her right after her Active Ability finishes which would cause issues. Luckily, her good mobility can make escapes easier, though her higher Stamina may not be as useful as having higher Movement Speed. Additionally, she can help other teammates get away from enraged Twisted Gourdy through her Passive and then utilize her 2 Star Stealth to lead him away. Note that Bobette would need to have her Ability active, have a speed Trinket equipped, or be near a decently sized island to make an effective getaway in most scenarios.

• Coal: Her Active Ability **Scout** can highlight all Items currently on the Floor to help her teammates find Items easily and feed them to Twisted Gourdy. Additionally, her 4 Star Movement Speed and Stamina Stats can aid her in escaping Gourdy if he enrages.

• Connie: (Situational): Similar to Bobette, Connie is able to become invisible to avoid Twisted Gourdy's attacks. However, due to her low speed, reaching the Elevator could be troublesome, especially if Twisteds are nearby. Her high Stealth somewhat mitigates it, but doesn't help too much.

•Cocoa: Her Ability allows her to drop BonBons to give to teammates or herself, and feed them to Twisted Gourdy to pacify him indefinitely until someone finishes the last machine as long as she feeds him at the right time. The Movement Speed and Extraction Speed boost from the BonBons can also make Floor progression faster and running from Twisteds easier.

• Finn: (Situational): In case Finn is near Twisted Gourdy and he has the last Machine/he is far from the Elevator, the speed boost from his Passive Ability can help him get back safely. However, low Stamina may be problematic.

• Gigi: Because of her **Surprise!** Active Ability, Gigi can roll for a random item and discard any useless items in her item slot. However, she may roll something worth of value instead and be forced to give it up to Twisted Gourdy. Her 1 Star Stamina can also be a hassle in escaping Gourdy if he enrages.

• Goob: Like Coal, Goob has 4 Stars in both Movement Speed and Stamina, making him good for zooming around the place to find as much Items as possible, maybe also helping other players bring the Items to Twisted Gourdy by pulling them towards him with **Hug!**. During Panic Mode, Goob can also pull another player into the Elevator and protect them from Twisted Gourdy's dangerously high speed.

• Pebble: Similar to Coal, his Passive can highlight nearby Items, though the highlights are only visible to him. This can be countered however, just by leading your teammates to the Items. Pebble can pick them up himself (unless his inventory is full) anyways. His high mobility stats can also help him escape, and even distract Twisted Gourdy.

• Shelly (Situational): Like Finn, her speed boost can help her with escaping Twisted Gourdy, though its less potent than Finn's **Reel In** Passive. Like Finn, her low Stamina can be troublesome to deal with when escaping Gourdy.

• Teagan (Situational): If Teagan happens to have a Bandage or a Health Kit in her first inventory slot, she doesn't have to worry about wasting it on giving it to Twisted Gourdy, as her Active Ability, **Tea Time**, already allows her to heal herself as long as she has at least 75 Tapes and not on Cooldown.

• Vee (Situational): Similar to Brightney, her Ability can help locate all the Twisteds on the Floor, making traversal to Machines and Twisted Gourdy safer. In addition, her good Extraction and her also being able to locate Machines can make Floor progression a lot faster, though her lackluster mobility can make it hard for her to move around, and paired with low Stealth, she can be at risk if/when Gourdy enrages.

• Waxwell: Waxwell's 5 Star Movement Speed allows him to easily search for all the Items on the Floor and bring them to Twisted Gourdy. He can speed up the Cooldowns for Gigi and Cocoa's Active Abilities with the help of his own Active Ability,**Ignite**. His Active Ability also removes his Tired Debuff and help him escape if Twisted Gourdy is enraged. Despite these advantages, his low Stealth and Stamina can still be a struggle.

• Yatta: Her Passive Ability will help produce the Items needed to keep Twisted Gourdy sane, so if a Yatta is present, consider letting her finish Machines to be able to take her items and feed them to Twisted Gourdy. When he does enrage, Yatta will also be able to sustain herself against him with Boxes o' Chocolates she gets from her Passive (though it is a bit RNG based) and get away with her 4 Star Movement Speed, though her low Stamina can cause issues.

Use Trick or Treat Doors to your advantage as well, as three Treats and two Tricks can give you extra Items, allowing you to keep Twisted Gourdy calm, especially helpful for higher Floors with more Machines. Keep in mind that you do also risk getting the "What's yours is mine!" Trick when opening a door, losing an Item that you could've given to Twisted Gourdy, but this is a pretty low likelihood.

In the unfortunate event where Twisted Gourdy becomes enraged, extreme caution is key to survival, especially in Blackouts and Ichor Leaks. His speed is not to be underestimated, being faster than Twisted Pebble and Twisted Bobette, and his extreme hearing radius makes failing Skill Checks practically a death sentence. If expected to distract him, he can be distracted by looping him around a medium-sized island. Looping is also a strategy used with Twisted Pebble where you'd take him to an island and let him see you on every turn, keeping both aggro and distance. Choosing a well sized island is important when attempting this. Having it be too big will let him catch up (especially with islands that don't have many sharp corners), or cause problems if you distract him with slower or even average paced Twisteds, due to them lacking behind and likely losing aggro, and too small will increase the risk of him turning around. Due to Gourdy's big hitbox, this will slow him down due to collisions. Be careful though due to his high speed. This can also be used for those who want Twisted Gourdy's Research, staying next to them to get it. Twisted Gourdy has an extremely short attack cooldown, a quality shared with other Main Character Twisteds, but his high speed and large circular vision makes this short cooldown an even harder challenge to overcome, with escapes and damage boosting (deliberate hits to take advantage of an attack cooldown) being difficult. Using Blushy Bat or having Soulvester on the team can make it far easier to escape from him by giving extra time after getting hit (or defended in the case of Soulvester).

During Panic Mode, Twisted Gourdy is an extreme threat. His speed is 1.2 units higher than the Run Speed of 5 Star Movement Speed Toons (and 0.1 unit lower with the Suppression Card selected), so he **will** catch up to you no matter what. The only Toons that can outrun him during Panic Mode without the use of Trinkets and Items are Eclipse in Blackouts and Looey on 1, both of which are situational or risky prerequisites. Pink Bow or Speedy Shoes will give 5 Star Movement Speed Toons enough Run Speed to full outrun Twisted Gourdy, but it isn't enough for 4 Star and lower. Some Toons like Bassie and Cocoa could use Bone instead to outrun Twisted Gourdy, but it does require good timing and in the case of Cocoa, good resource management and BonBon placement. Tell teammates if you are on the last Machine with GTE (or its Sticker) or stay away if you're not extracting. If the Machine is next to him, use an Item to escape or ask a faster, lower Stealth Toon to divert him.

Solar kiting with Bobette can make distracting or escaping Twisted Gourdy far easier; 5 Star Movement Speed Toons, Eclipse in a Blackout, and Looey on 1 Heart with Dog Plush can outwalk him; with both Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes, the aforementioned Toons can out-walk by a larger margin, and 2 Heart Looey will be able to sprint-tap easily; any Toon with 2 Star or higher speed can outrun Twisted Gourdy; with 3 Star or higher Toons can outrun him during Panic Mode. He cannot be outwalked with Bobette's boost during Panic Mode, unless Eclipse in Blackouts or Looey on 1 Heart has both Dog Plush and Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool equipped. Overall, if you're seeking to have an easier time with Twisted Gourdy (primarily on higher Floors due to more Machines and a tendency for teams to have rarer Items that can't be given up), having Bobette can be very useful. Do note that Bobette would need to have Diary to solar kite with 2 Star Stealth distractors.

twisteds.name: Twisted Pebble
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 24 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 28.8 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 27.6 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: None
twisteds.research:
Twisted Pebble is a massive, roaming dog-like monster that stomps and wanders around the halls aimlessly. His unique ability allows him to detect Toons from far away if line of sight is triggered. Be sure to break line of sight as soon as getting spotted, as he will quickly catch up, even from a great distance. Because of his extremely fast speed, it is very hard to get away from him if he spots you in bad terrain or gets close and you have average mobility. Because of his many high stats, Twisted Pebble is extremely dangerous and should be avoided if possible.

Twisted Pebble produces muffled, yet pounding footsteps when roaming and feral noises when chasing, and since the footsteps are hard to detect, it can be a big surprise when he comes up on a floor that you think is safer.
twisteds.strategies:
Due to his extreme speed, Twisted Pebble (with two build exceptions) is impossible to outwalk and hard to outrun (especially Toons with below-average mobility), while also being one of the most dangerous Twisteds in-game. Looey on 1 or Eclipse (during a Blackout) with Dog Plush and Ribbon Spool or Clown Horn gives a walk speed multiplier of 69.4%, resulting a walk speed of 25.41, while Pebble, Bassie, Razzle & Dazzle (on odd-numbered Floors), and Waxwell with the aforementioned Trinkets gives a walk speed multiplier of 21%, resulting in a walk speed of 24.2, making them the only Toons who can outwalk Twisted Pebble outside of Panic Mode, but only slightly. Looey on 1 Heart and Eclipse (during a Blackout) can also outwalk Twisted Pebble with Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes, albeit by 0.25 units.

3 Movement Speed Toons barely outrun him, while 2 Star and 1 Star Movement Speed Toons aren't capable of out-speeding him while running (3 Star Movement Speed Toons run at 25, 2 Stars run at 22.5, and 1 Star Movement Speed Toons run at 20, while Twisted Pebble runs at 24), especially Connie, Razzle & Dazzle (on even-numbered floors), Shrimpo and Soulvester, so escaping Items and Speed Trinkets are paramount to survival while he's on a Floor. Make sharp movements around corners to slow him down and cling tightly to walls, keeping an eye out for outcroppings you might get stuck on. Since he is quite large, small islands are hard to kite him around and should be avoided if you don't have much distance on him. Toons with survival or mobility based Abilities like Connie and Glisten may benefit from saving them primarily for escaping from Twisted Pebble, as opposed to using them to escape from a slower Twisted, which would otherwise put their Ability on cooldown and leave them potentially vulnerable to Twisted Pebble.

Twisted Pebble will only bark and growl continuously while chasing Toons. Hence, if you hear his footsteps speed up but no loud barking followed by continued growling, he is heading towards a failed Machine and not a Toon, and you shouldn't rush in.

Twisted Pebble's footsteps might be quiet and unnoticeable at first, so make sure to listen for barks or growling, especially in Blackouts.

Since Twisted Pebble is capable of detecting Toons at great distances, hide from him if he has line of sight or there isn't much cover nearby. Try to stay away from long corridors and open spaces, as disruptions to his line of sight are important to keeping him off of you. As mentioned above, slower Toons should not dare get chased, easily being outran or being barely faster. Stay behind cover if he's fairly close and maintain knowledge on his location to prevent deaths. Vee and Brightney's Abilities can be a great help to locate him.

If expecting to distract Twisted Pebble, you'll likely need speed Trinkets. Speedy Shoes or Dog Plush are the most used Trinkets for distracting. Having Astro or Tisha on your team may be helpful, as this can help with gaining or conserving Stamina. The best Strategy for distracting Twisted Pebble is finding an island located on a Floor that you will be able to go around when baiting him. Hugging tightly to the island will slow down Twisted Pebble and make it significantly easier to Distract him. If you are unable to find an island to go around, trying running/walking in a straight line without turning or pressing other movement keys since Twisted Pebble will take slightly longer to hit you meaning you will be able to regain Stamina. Keep in mind that whenever Twisted Pebble loses line of sight of you when you are going around the island, he can aggro onto somebody else if he sees them, so try to find a safe area where other Toons will not be seen as much, such as the broken elevator area or communicate your plans ahead of time. If other dangerous Twisteds are on the Floor, consider having other Distractors help, or if none are available at the moment, you will have to just take the lesser threats and let Twisted Pebble roam around, moving or dodging when he gets nearby. If using a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon, you are able to kite Twisted Pebble, though ONLY him, as other Twisteds would turn the other way and possibly get you hit.

It is possible to distract Pebble as a 4 or 5 Star Movement Speed Toon without speed Trinkets, however it is much more challenging. If you want to do this, either because you want to help your distractor while having extracting Trinkets, or for the challenge, you’ll need to hug an island tightly. Try to brush against the island in a consistent manner, avoiding getting caught on crates or similar objects in the island by slightly moving outward. ONLY sprint tap if you're turning and when Twisted Pebble gets a bit too close to you; you want to maintain your Stamina incase you have to change your looping spot, or to be prepared for Panic Mode, as you more than likely have to run during it. You absolutely can ONLY distract Twisted Pebble when you do this.

When solar distracting with a Bobette, a Toon with 4 Star Movement Speed and at least Dog Plush can outwalk Twisted Pebble (only by 0.06 units), though additionally using Speedy Shoes (outwalks by 1.26 units) or Clown Horn/Ribbon Spool (outwalks by 2.47 units) will help ensure a more steady and comfortable difference.

If playing as a Toon and with a Trinket combination that can outwalk Twisted Pebble (even by a decimal amount) you may instead opt to follow a large circular path around an island, as this’ll allow you to have to minimally sprint tap and keep your Stamina up until Panic Mode. This additionally makes it easier to retain Twisted Pebble's attention as opposed to accidentally losing it from hugging an island and cutting corners. This is of course dependent on the Floor, how many teammates have shared or lower Stealth than you, and the other Twisteds you may have to distract. This is particularly viable if you’re solar distracting with a Bobette, as cutting corners can risk getting her hurt or killed, plus it’ll allow the Bobette to more easily provide her boost, rather than try to keep up with a more erratic or angular path.

Care should be taken during Ichor Leaks, as Twisted Pebble's high hearing range can synergize with the Illness III Debuff applied by the Ichor puddles, making failing Skill Checks far more likely. The Ichor puddles also apply the Slow I Debuff, which can be very troublesome or even lethal when combined with Twisted Pebble's extremely high speed, making escapes incredibly difficult and dangerous. The former isn't an issue if Twisted Pebble is currently being distracted or is preoccupied from a different alert, though the latter can be a huge problem for distractors, unless they have Train Whistle equipped or are immune to Ichor Leaks.

In Panic Mode, he is much faster than all Toons without Suppression, nearly matching the run speed of his Toon counterpart (Pebble), Bassie, Waxwell, Razzle & Dazzle (on odd-numbered floors), Looey (at 2 Hearts), and Eclipse (during a Blackout). The only way you would be able to outrun him during Panic Mode is if you are playing as Looey at 2-1 Hearts, Eclipse (during a Blackout), or a 5 Star Movement Speed Toon. Otherwise, running away is useless or incredibly difficult if you are near him. With Suppression, 4 Star Movement Speed Toons are able to outrun him, but be mindful of your stamina if playing Toons such as Gourdy or Yatta. 3 Star Movement Speed Toons can also outrun him with Suppresion, if they have both Pink Bow and Speedy shoes equipped. It is advisable to get to the elevator before Panic Mode begins. If you are unfortunately seen, either get in the Elevator as fast as possible (if no one else is outside), lose sight of him or just hope that he is far enough from you to not get hit. Distracting Twisted Vee at the same time is a huge disadvantage to speed, as her Slow II Debuff will help Twisted Pebble reach you easier. Though this can be deflected with Tisha's pulse on Pebble, Twisted Vee uses her Debuff periodically, which is much shorter than Tisha's cooldown. Vanity Mirror can be a good assistant in this Panic Mode, with 5% remaining in support instead on the run speed and keeping distance from Twisted Pebble still. Do note this Trinket may not be a viable choice and is only in use if this is activated. Train Whistle is the best option for this, as you cannot get slowed and still be able to outrun Pebble.

Fortunately, despite being a Main Character Twisted, he lacks any special mechanic that actually hinders you, so avoidance will make his presence on a floor easier.

twisteds.name: Twisted Shelly
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 20 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 24 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 23 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Applies the Confused I Debuff to every Toon on the Floor, causing them to extract much slower than usual (-25% Extraction Speed)
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Shelly has a high chasing speed of 20, being as fast as Twisted Toodles, along with an above average attention span, being the same as Twisted Shrimpo's. She also applies the Confused I Debuff to all Toons on a given Floor, giving them all -25% Extraction Speed. While this may not greatly affect Toons with better Extraction Speed or high Skill Check Stats, progression is important and it can be annoying when distractors have to perform their role for slightly longer—especially when handling not only Twisted Shelly but more problematic Main Character Twisteds, such as Twisted Vee, who inflicts Slow II to reduce Movement Speed, Twisted Pebble, who is even faster than Twisted Shelly, Twisted Sprout, who constantly summons tendrils that can block the distractor's path, and Twisted Astro, who inflicts Tired III to reduce Stamina regeneration. Twisted Shelly can become more intense to distract if with long-ranged Twisteds such as, Twisted Goob, Twisted Scraps, and Twisted Gigi (if you have valuable Items, such as Health Kits), as keeping track of the long range attack cooldown but also the speed of Twisted Shelly is incredibly difficult and you will get hit if you aren't careful. If you can't focus on both her speed and the ranged attacks, then you can get hit and escape (though this isn't the best method), which, in summary, makes Twisted Shelly extremely problematic, although a fast Toon like Pebble shouldn't have a problem, being able to out-walk her; although they'll have to distract for a longer time, either way. Extraction Speed Trinkets can help combat the debuff she gives, the most notable being Vee's Remote and Wrench. However, Golden Skill Checks are unaffected by the Confused I Debuff and continue to add more completion, reducing total extraction time. Toons with a 5 Skill Check— Gigi, Gourdy, her Toon counterpart, Soulvester, and Waxwell—as well as some 4 Star Skill Check Toons, can effectively utilize the Magnifying Glass Trinket for faster extraction.

It's worth noting that Treadmill Machines are not affected by the reduced Extraction Speed since they don't utilize the Stat. Therefore, if you will extract Treadmill Machines faster than other types due to your mobility Stats in comparison to your Debuffed extraction, it's advised to prioritize those first. Try to coordinate with your teammates to do every Duo Machine together, as the combined Stats of both players on one Duo Machine can effectively reduce, neutralize, or even overpower the Confused I. Barnaby Machines can also be a breeze for Toons with higher Skill Check Stats, Magnifying Glass, and/or Participation Award; as the coins can at most show up every other pair of seaweed, which combined with high Skill Check value, could effectively negate the decrease in Extraction Speed.

If you're planning to distract her, using Movement Speed Trinkets such as Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes is your best option. Distracting her as a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon using these Trinkets makes you only slightly faster than her, so remember to occasionally sprint on turns and in small areas. Unlike Twisted Toodles, Twisted Shelly's hitbox is larger, making her harder to distract. Since her attention span is slightly higher than average, you can also loop her around an island if needed and not worry about losing aggro as easily as Twisted Toodles. Blushy Bat and Soul Sword are quite good Trinkets against Twisted Shelly, as her speed can be knocked down a bit and/or stop moving, making escapes a bit easier.

Ribecca is completely immune to Twisted Shelly's Confused Debuff due to her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, meaning she has an advantage over other Toons with equal Extraction Speed or Skill Check Stats if Twisted Shelly is on the Floor. She can even extract faster than Toons with 4 Star Extraction Speed (whose Extraction Speed is barely above that of 2 Star when Confused). This can be used to her advantage, by focusing on more dangerous or far away Machines, though Toons with 5 Star Extraction Speed or above average Skill Check Stats will typically extract faster, even under the effects of Confused. Also note that she only gets one Stat boost at the start of the Floor, and won't be continually empowered by Twisted Shelly. Refer to the Machine Times table at the bottom of this section for comparison to Ribecca's average completion time of 35 seconds (31.11 with Tech Savvy).

Shelly's Active Ability, **Inspiration**, can also help with the Confused I Debuff, as the Toon that gets the effect from her Ability not only has the effect completely nullified, but also gets a 31.25% Extraction Speed boost, helping with more dangerous Machines throughout the Floor and making progress faster. Brusha can also help in a pretty similar way with **Artistic Inspiration**, as she can boost Toons' Skill Check chance and Extraction Speed. The increased chance means Toons can make up for their slowed Extraction Speed with more Skill Checks, while the Extraction Speed increase can nearly neutralize (though not fully counteract) Confused I, reducing it to a -6.2% decrease. These are even better if paired with a Ribecca.

Toons with Abilities that boost their own Extraction Speed, such as Boxten or Squirm, can mitigate the Confused I and allow themselves to still extract at an almost average or even above average pace.

twisteds.speed:
8.5 walking, 17 chasing
Panic Mode: 10.2 walking, 20.4 chasing
Suppression: 9.78 walking, 19.55 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: When detecting a Toon, Twisted Sprout will leave a deadly tendril under the detected Toon, attacking anyone that steps on it for too long. Has a cooldown of 10. If Twisted Cosmo is on the floor as well, Twisted Sprout will occasionally follow him. He will also sometimes stop to look at posters of his Toon counterpart.
twisteds.research: When Twisted Sprout spots a Toon, he will pause his movement, spawning a puddle of Ichor at that Toon's position containing a tendril that, shortly after being summoned, will attack anyone who comes too close to it. This ability has a cooldown of 10 seconds, and the tendril disappears after 15 seconds, meaning that the maximum amount of tendrils that can be on the floor at the same time is 2, though there's no limit to how many Twisted Sprout can spawn during a chase.
twisteds.strategies:
As Twisted Sprout is capable of summoning non-movable tendrils, vacate any Machines before you are in his detection range, to reduce/eliminate time taken for tendril dissipation. When you are planning to distract him, avoid cramped rooms with a lack of exits, as it will decrease your chance of survival. Having many exits reduces the amount blocked by his tendrils and makes escapes easier. While distracting him in open areas, hugging one side of either the island or outer walls reduces the area the tendril covers (unless other aggressive Twisteds are chasing you). Also, if done quickly and across the edges, it is possible to run through his tendrils without taking damage.

His short cooldown and tendrils should be noted for slower or low-Stamina Toons, like Shrimpo, Gigi, or Soulvester, as running while he is spawning tendrils is a good way to lose him, so preserve Stamina for the occasion.

Since his abilities are physical, try to keep him away from Twisted Razzle & Dazzle so their attack radiuses don't intersect, as this could cause problems. Similarly to them, his tendril attacks can be avoided even if you step into the attack range circle if you're quick at leaving it.

Unlike the other Main Character Twisteds who have almost the same or higher chasing speed as/than regular Twisteds, Twisted Sprout is the slowest Main Character Twisted, meaning that it's possible for 4 Movement Speed Toons or a ≤2 Looey to outrun him easily and even out-walk him without the use of Movement Speed Trinkets, albeit by a tiny margin. Do note that Panic Mode significantly increases the speed of Twisteds, letting him catch up to you easier.

During Blackouts, his ability will be more dangerous due to the dark color of his tendrils, similar to Twisted Blot's hands. Make sure to watch where you're going and keep your camera angle pointed ahead. Be ready to sprint off at a moment's notice—there's no easy way to tell if he's the one chasing you until it's too late. Turning down your game graphics can help visibility in Blackouts. Using Spare Bulb and picking the Sparkplug Card can help with that problem too, although these are not very useful for other Twisteds in the long run, and playing as light-producing Toons, such as Eclipse, can end up being more beneficial.

If Twisted Cosmo is on the same Floor, and there are no distractors, try to avoid being seen by Twisted Sprout, as Twisted Cosmo could also spot you (due to Twisted Sprout following Twisted Cosmo) and vice versa, leading to you having to shake off 2 Twisteds.

twisteds.name: Twisted Vee
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 18 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 21.6 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 20.7 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Applies Slow II (-25% Movement Speed) to players being chased by Twisted Vee for 5 seconds (10 second cooldown), as well as spawning pop-up ads on players screens (45 second cooldown). Can detect sounds from anywhere.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Vee is a large TV-screen, roaming Twisted that wanders the halls aimlessly. Reflecting her media personality counterpart, her unique ability allows her to bombard players with pop-up advertisements. These ads need to be closed by clicking the red "X" button in the top right of the pop-up window, pressing the "X" (or "B") button on an Xbox controller, or the "O" button on a Playstation controller. If you do not close out the ads, they block the view of the player's screen. She will send these popup ads to all players upon entering the Floor and every 45 seconds afterwards in groups of three. She poses no direct threat, and besides their tendency to cover Skill Checks and your vision, it's relatively harmless. Along with this, the pop-up windows will automatically close after 30 seconds of being on the screen. When she spots a Toon, she will make agitated electronic noises, and will also send a single pop-up ad. These ads will then inflict the Slow II Debuff to a player for approximately 5 seconds when she has begun to chase and will inflict it every 10 seconds if the chase is continued. The Slow II Debuff she creates can make her hard to escape (especially with Toons with low Movement Speed, such as Shrimpo, Connie, Soulvester, and Razzle & Dazzle (on even-numbered Floors) and her usage of such makes it much harder for any Toons to attempt escaping or distracting her.

In addition to the pop-ups and her Slow II Debuff, if a Toon fails a Skill Check, uses an Air Horn, or uses Pebble's **Speak!** Ability, she will run to the source of the sound from **anywhere on the Floor**.
twisteds.strategies:
Escaping Twisted Vee during a chase is no easy task, especially while using slower Toons such as her Toon counterpart or Rodger. One way to get her to lose sight of you is to run around rooms in the Floor instead of circling boxes as you would with any other Twisted. Finding space to get a large distance between you and Twisted Vee will make your escape a lot easier, once you are a few rooms away from her, it's usually safe to duck behind boxes.

Twisted Vee's presence is usually easy to notice, as her bright and vibrant colors don't blend in with most Floors (in contrast to some Twisteds like Twisted Finn), her ads make her presence apparent and her footsteps are easy to hear and distinguish from other Main Character Twisteds' footsteps. She should be relatively easy to avoid getting chased by so long if you're stealthy.

If you have trouble distracting Twisted Vee, it's recommended you keep either an Astro or Tisha near you if you're not using a 5 or faster Toon (eg. Looey on 1), as Twisted Vee's Slow II Debuff can and will drain Stamina while distracting. To counter her Debuff, try to sprint tap so that you're far away enough from her while it's inflicted to ensure she doesn't get too close before the effect goes away. A suitable distance will make it unneeded to sprint when she slows you down, which allows you to conserve Stamina, though this can change with any faster Twisteds. However, 5 Star speed Toons (such as Pebble), Looey (on 1 Heart), Eclipse (in Blackouts), with Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes/ Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool equipped, given the right circumstances, are able to naturally out-walk Twisted Vee. Try not to Distract her in small spaces or with other fast and/or dangerous Twisteds such as Twisted Pebble, Twisted Shelly, Twisted Bobette, and Twisted Coal (in Blackouts). In fact, you could ask a backup to distract the faster Twisteds if expected to distract all. If you have any Items, such as a Speed Candies (which will minimize the slowness to -6.3%) or Pops, those will be useful to help distract Twisted Vee. On the topic of Items, an Eject Button helps a lot when you encounter Twisted Vee, if you wish to escape from her, the Eject Button helps you get rid of the Slow II Debuff while also giving you a significant amount of speed to escape.

If you are overall inexperienced with distracting Twisted Vee, try letting somebody else distract her while you distract the rest of the Twisteds.

To handle Twisted Vee's pop-ups, close the player menu on the side of the screen, as pop-ups can spawn there and you may not be able to close them out. Be especially careful while you are being chased by a Twisted or doing a Machine. When doing a Machine, you may get pop-ups and fail the Skill Check. Paired with Twisted Vee's ability to go to a failed Machine from anywhere, if you aren't prepared, this can be deadly. If you are being chased and pop-ups appear, you may run into several walls, allowing Twisteds to hit you. Always be ready to close out Twisted Vee's pop-ups; otherwise, you may face an early demise. If you need to use an Item, use the number keys instead of the cursor to not overwhelm your cursor and to use it quickly. If you have a controller connected to your computer, you can spam the A button for Xbox or B button for a Pro Controller and they will close the pop-ups very quickly, so you can switch to a controller when the pop-ups appear and immediately close them.

It's important to note that Twisted Vee's pop-ups can cover Default Machine Skill Checks and your Sticker Wheel. For Default Machine Skill Checks, try to listen for the clicking sounds of the red line passing over the white and gold zones. If the pop ups appear after a Skill Check shows up, try to remember where it is or listen for the sounds, but with smaller Skill Check sizes, the clicks may be unreliable. Be wary if they cover your Sticker Wheel, as you could end up sending the wrong one and causing potentially dangerous confusion (such as accidentally requesting help instead of telling your team to get to the Elevator). Remembering which Sticker is in what slot is a safe strategy, as you can still click the Stickers through the pop ups. If you're able to communicate with your teammates through chat or voice, this shouldn't be the biggest problem. In both cases you can still close the pop ups, but it's good to have a backup plan in case you have to complete a Skill Check (especially helpful for players who can't multitask while hitting Skill Checks) or send a Sticker on time (such as one that alerts the team that you need to be healed).

Care should be taken during Ichor Leaks, as Twisted Vee's ability to hear failed Skill Checks from anywhere can synergize with the Illness III Debuff applied by the Ichor puddles, making failing Skill Checks far more likely. The Ichor puddles also apply the Slow I Debuff, which can be troublesome or even lethal when combined with Twisted Vee's slowness Debuff, leaving you much more likely to be slowed, making escapes incredibly difficult and dangerous. The former isn't an issue if Twisted Vee is currently being distracted or is preoccupied from a different alert, though the latter can be a huge problem for distractors, unless they have Train Whistle equipped. Ichor Stains can also combine with Twisted Vee's pop-ups, sometimes covering nearly your entire screen, try to avoid puddles as much as possible, since the Ichor Stains always last for 25 seconds and can't be manually removed. Ichor Puddle Immune Toons won't have as big of an issue when it comes to this, though they aren't immune to Twisted Vee's slowness which can still be incredibly dangerous (with the potential exceptions of Blot and Flutter, as their speed, Stamina, and Abilities help with escape and even distracting with the right teammates/Trinkets).

Using Train Whistle will completely counteract Twisted Vee's slowness Debuff, making players able to escape her like any other normal Twisted. This additionally makes distracting Twisted Vee a lot easier, especially when you're dealing with a bad combo like Twisted Vee paired up with Twisted Pebble. Twisted Vee's average chasing speed makes her even easier, with the only threat being the pop-ups. However it will cost one of your Trinket slots and her Main Character status makes her quite rare, making it quite risky early on.

Ribecca is completely immune to Twisted Vee's slowness Debuff due to her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, making her a near non-threat (though the longer attention span and pop-ups could still be troublesome). This allows Ribecca to potentially be able to save teammates from Twisted Vee; particularly Toons that are slower, low on Stamina, or on one Heart; though caution should be taken if there are other, more dangerous Twisteds chasing teammates. Due to the fact Twisted Vee applies Slow II every 10 seconds, and Ribecca's empowered boosts lasts for 10 seconds, she can endlessly have a 10% boost while being chased by Twisted Vee. She is additionally immune to Ichor Puddles, which does give her a slight advantage over Toons with the Ichor Puddle Immunity Aux. Stat, as she's totally immune to Twisted Vee's Debuff, though she also has average mobility Stats, and thus not much of a capacity to (easily) distract during Ichor Leaks.

twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Brusha paints Ichor over a Machine, which causes the chances of Skill Checks to be decreased by 15% when extracting.
twisteds.research: She will roam around, occasionally stopping at Machines to vandalize them, debuffing them and making Toons extract slower as a result. She also possesses a decently large vision range.
twisteds.strategies:
Brusha doesn't possess much of a threat but can still be troublesome to handle, especially with her rather high vision range. However, it can make it easier to redirect her, where you bait a Twisted and hide behind an object for them to go somewhere else. This can even make Twisted Brusha go to places faster, as the distance it takes for Twisted Brusha to see is enough for you to walk a bit while still keeping distance.

If there are no distractors present or you are doing a solo run, always be aware of your surroundings, since Twisted Brusha can easily sneak up on you if you let your guard down. It’s generally safe to preserve around 40-70 Stamina to outrun her.

If you notice her graffiti any Machines, take note that Skill Check chance will be decreased (-15%), so it may be better for Toons with high Extraction Speed to extract as they aren’t as reliant on Skill Checks. Skill Check chance on vandalized Machines by default will be lowered to 10%, which is quite a small amount and can really reduce frequency, especially impacting Toons with 4 or 5 Star Skill Check, or with the Trinkets Magnifying Glass or Stress Ball equipped. Participation Award and Paint Bucket counteract debuffed Machines with their own chance increases, so using either or both of them can be helpful (Participation Award maintains chance at 35%, while Paint Bucket lessens the reduction to only 20%). Toons with lower Skill Check Stats could actually benefit from the reduced chance since failing Skill Checks halts extraction, but this isn't particularly beneficial for players who can hit smaller Skill Checks, especially if they can hit the golden zones.

Tisha can clean up the graffiti to revert Machines to a normal state, though note that this puts her Ability on cooldown, which could leave her unable to provide a speed boost to a teammate in danger; try to only clean the graffiti if you don't have other Toons/Twisteds who can counter it, if there aren't particularly fast Twisteds, if teammates consistently maintain their Stamina, and if it isn't almost Panic Mode. Alternatively, Twisted Tisha can also clear up the graffiti that Twisted Brusha leaves, so if she's also present, you could wait behind cover for her to clean it up. Playing as Brusha will allow you to cancel out the graffiti and still provide your buff, but keep in mind that leaving the painted Machine alone can result in Twisted Brusha cancelling out your buff in return.

Ribecca ignores the Skill Check chance reduction, and thus can extract at a decent pace, especially compared to other Toons who may rely on Skill Check extraction. Additionally, she will gain a random Stat boost by extracting from a vandalized Machine, which can make her even better at extracting, or potentially let her escape from Twisteds more easily. Getting off and on a vandalized Machine every 10 seconds could be useful, but this isn't recommended if it would disrupt a more potent boost from a teammate or Item.

Twisted Brusha only graffitis a Machine when she spends her full duration at one (about 5 seconds), so interrupting her while she's vandalizing will still prevent the debuff. Do note that if you fail a Skill Check and Twisted Brusha approaches, she is most likely going to vandalize your Machine, so try not to fail them.

10 walking, 18 chasing

Suppression: 11.5 walking, 20.7 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Sweeps the floors, idling in areas for 10 seconds at a time. Also increases the size of Ichor Puddles by sweeping in them, and can clear away Brusha's paint and Twisted Brusha's graffiti from Machines.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Tisha roams around and overall acts like a fairly normal Twisted, with her only unique property being her longer idle time than other Twisteds, sweeping at the ground.

When there's Ichor Puddles on the Floor, she will increase their size when "cleaning" them. If Machines are painted or vandalized, they will be cleaned when she approaches them.
twisteds.strategies:
Under normal circumstances, Twisted Tisha is a roaming Twisted that usually possesses no special abilities, other than her 10 second idle as she stops to sweep the floor with her feather duster. This means she can camp Machines or passageways, and can slow the Floor's progression in solo runs or runs without Distractors. Like with other Twisteds, some Stamina should be saved in case the player is spotted so she can be ditched. In a situation where she is idle around a Machine, she can be lured into a different area, or the player can wait until she moves on.

However, things change when she is on the same Floor as an Ichor Leak and/or Twisted Finn. She can start sweeping at any Ichor Puddles, increasing their size to troublesome degrees, blocking off entire pathways or disrupting a distractor's intended looping area. It’s helpful to have Tisha on the team as she can clean up Ichor Puddles, just be aware that puddles from Ichor Leaks will come back on their own, allowing Twisted Tisha to continue increasing the sizes.

It's also good to keep an eye out if you or any of your teammates are Brusha, as buffed Machines can get cleaned up, removing the Extraction Speed and Skill Check boosts. Consequently, this can make extracting from these cleaned Machines return to an average rate and slow things down a bit. Though Brusha could also paint a certain Machine to possibly bait Twisted Tisha away from teammates or certain locations, taking advantage of the special ability. Fortunately, she can be beneficial if Twisted Brusha also happens to appear on the same Floor as her, as she can also clear away Twisted Brusha's graffiti, removing her debuff from affected Machines, though since this alters her pathing, she may find her way right to you or a teammate.

twisteds.strategies:
Due to her above-average speed (matching Twisted Astro and Twisted Gigi's Run Speeds), it's recommended to use a Toon like Pebble or Looey (at one) when distracting to avoid getting hit during Panic Mode. If you are playing as a 4 Movement Speed Toon, it's recommended to gain distance before Panic Mode starts to avoid taking damage from her as out-walking her during that time is not possible without the use of Items.

If you aren't distracting or playing as a slow Toon like Connie, Soulvester, Shrimpo or Rodger, having a Movement Speed Items like Speed Candies or Boxes o' Chocolates will be helpful to counter Twisted Yatta's Movement Speed during a chase. Sprint-tapping will also help if you have no items, as it allows you to cover some ground from her, though clicking at the right time is crucial to not lose Stamina too fast or be too slow.

If planning to distract Twisted Yatta, it will be slightly harder than regular Commons, as her speed is higher by 1 unit in comparison to most of them (all Commons except Twisted Shrimpo have 18 run speed units), and her hitbox is much bigger. If distracting her as 4 Star Movement Speed Toon with at least Dog Plush, take a sprint when making a round turn. If you are a faster Toon, you don't really need to worry about her speed that much until Panic Mode.

Be cautious about Twisted Yatta's large circular vision, as it can be harder to sneak by her when her back is turned. Also note that her hearing radius is larger than other Common Twisteds, so failing a Skill Check could alert her from further than you think, causing her to ambush you.

Do note, Twisted Yatta leans forward while chasing. This increases her hitbox range a little, so be sure to be careful when making turns when escaping from her. Take multiple sharp turns so she loses sight of you.

Twisted Yatta's incredibly low roaming speed can be a problem–if there's no distractor–for a few reasons. She can pass by a Machine or Item and force players to wait until she's far enough, unless someone decides to pull her away, dragging things a bit. If you lose her attention near a dead end, you may have to wait until she leaves, primarily if you're lower on Stamina, laggy, or otherwise can't just grab her aggro again before shaking her off elsewhere. For these reasons, it's important to be cautious with using Bobette's **Precious Packaging** and (sometimes) Connie's **Haunting Escape** while being chased by Twisted Yatta. When the aforementioned targeting immunities end, Twisted Yatta may be close enough to reaggro onto you, this is especially a risk if she idles or turns around towards you.

twisteds.name: Twisted Connie

8 walking, 18 chasing
Panic Mode: 9.6 walking, 21.6 chasing

twisteds.mechanic: Wanders around invisible while passive, temporarily possessing any machine she finds and walks up to. Gives warnings during possession by causing the Machine's red light to turn blue and make rattling noises. Sends an unavoidable attack if a Toon tries to extract it.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Connie is one of, if not, the easiest Twisted to deal with. However, carelessness can make you lose a for preventable reasons, so keeping an eye on her is important.

A strategy for surviving Twisted Connie is to communicate with your teammates when a Machine has been completed. Make sure to alert others as soon as you see that Twisted Connie is on the Floor even if you trust your teammates to watch out; it will be helpful for distractors if they want to use Vee's Remote on a Machine and don't know that Twisted Connie is possessing it. If caught by Twisted Connie, you cannot avoid the attack, so try to pay attention. It might be beneficial to have someone follow Twisted Connie around, so people know where and in which Machine Twisted Connie is if your party has surplus members. In runs where you are alone, keeping track of which Machines you have completed can help. The best method, however, is to simply check the Machine handles before extracting. All in all, awareness will help you survive on the Floors where she appears.

If Twisted Connie has not yet been encountered on that Floor, the Tape collection sound will play if she's inside a Machine the player approaches when her Research is collected. Thus, deliberately avoiding her Line of Sight in order to retain this one-time alert is a niche-but-helpful strategy. Furthermore, during Events, the Event's Currency will be given if a Toon walks by a Machine that she is possessing, which is far more noticeable and can further prevent slip-ups.

If Vee uses her **Mic Check** Ability while Twisted Connie is inside of a Machine, the word "Twisted" along with an arrow pointing to the Machine will appear, but her model will not be highlighted. As this is unique to her, this will always indicate her presence on a Floor.

Although it's not recommended, you can try to follow Twisted Connie, as there will be a chance you will run into an uncompleted Machine due to her idling patterns. However, this could waste time as she is very slow, and could lead you to Twisteds.

Before extracting a Machine, wait 2–3 seconds to make sure Twisted Connie is not in the Machine.

twisteds.name: Twisted Finn
twisteds.speed:
8.5 walking, 16 chasing
Panic Mode: 10.2 walking, 19.2 chasing
Suppression: 9.78 walking, 18.4 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Finn will spawn in 3 Ichor Puddles in random positions around the floor he occupies, with the third one having Twisted Barnaby hidden inside of it. When a player steps on the puddle where Twisted Barnaby is hidden, he will latch onto the player for a few seconds (10 for solo, 15 for 2-4 players, 20 for 4+) and their location will be revealed to Twisted Finn at all times. Twisted Finn will chase the latched player no matter what.
twisteds.research: Twisted Finn crawls around the floors of Gardenview at a speed significantly slower than the average Twisted, occasionally creating Ichor Puddles similar to Ichor Leaks; Sometimes, his toy fish, Twisted Barnaby, would swim inside.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Finn is not a severely difficult Twisted to deal with. When you notice him on the Floor, immediately take note of any Ichor Puddles you see. The puddles inflict Slow I, Illness III, and Ichor Stains, so be wary of reduced Movement Speed, Skill Check size, and partially obscured vision. If possible, try avoiding them or taking a different path, as you wouldn't want to risk taking his aggro. However, in the case of an Ichor Leak, doing this could be much harder. Therefore, you should try to take a close look at each puddle and see if Twisted Barnaby is there, you can also listen for splashing or swimming sounds. If he isn't, you can just pass through. Note that Twisted Finn's color matches an Ichor Puddle's color, so when seeing one, check if Twisted Finn is playing in one.

If Twisted Barnaby is on you, try to see where Twisted Finn is at to plan your escape route. His slower Movement Speed could help you find a spot without losing much Stamina, though you would want to find a spot close to your location to not accidentally attract other Twisteds. When Twisted Finn catches up to you, start looping around the island. Try preserving Stamina while trying to lose him, as looping could attract another Twisted. When Twisted Barnaby releases, hide behind the island and wait for Twisted Finn to lose interest. If you see your teammate with Twisted Barnaby, you can try to free them. Although any Stealth Toon can release him, lower Stealth Toons could take Twisted Finn's aggro, getting yourself hit. If a distractor is present and Twisted Finn is attracted, you should try to find an island closer to the distractor so they don't get into trouble with the other Twisteds when recovering him, albeit stay out of the other Twisteds' sight.

Twisted Finn's puddles can't affect Ichor Puddle Immune Toons ( Blot, Connie, Flutter, and Soulvester) meaning they can pass over Ichor Puddles with no issue, though Twisted Barnaby can still latch onto them and afflict them with the slowness. It's still important to check puddles for Barnaby even if you're immune. Ribecca on the other hand is totally immune to all Debuffs afflicted, including Twisted Barnaby's, so the only real problem she can face involving the puddles is Twisted Finn relentlessly chasing her while Barnaby is attached.

Tisha can clean up Ichor Puddles created by Twisted Finn, making him less of a threat. Additionally, if she cleans a puddle Twisted Barnaby is swimming in, he will be forced away as well, giving her the potential to prevent teammates from being hindered by him. Bobette and Connie can also make Twisted Barnaby latch onto them, before using **Precious Packaging** or **Haunting Escape** respectively to shake him off, effectively forcing him out of a puddle in a similar vain to Tisha. It's additionally very good to note that Twisted Finn can be an annoying or dangerous problem when Twisted Tisha is on the same Floor as him, since she can increase the size of his puddles. This creates a synergy that can be hard to control unless you have Tisha or a distractor on your team.

Twisted Finn's short height and dark color make him harder to spot in Blackouts than most Twisteds. It's good to have a Toon that can highlight where he is (like Vee or Brightney in Blackouts) to avoid running into him. His abysmal speed can cause him to appear in places you don't expect or lose aggression and circle back. Keep your guard up if you don't currently know his location.

Due to her long attention span, it'd be best to turn around a long object and run as far away from her as possible in order to lose her. Alternatively, you could also walk around a circle table until she gives up, though these may not always be on the map, but be sure to be careful, as she tends to turn around while you are looping and this can get you hurt. This means you don't have to worry too much about her losing interest in you, though she can be problematic with even average speed Twisteds, as she can lack behind and possibly switch aggro on another close target. The only other threat she poses is she can lead you into fast Twisteds, or if you have 2 or 1 Star Movement Speed, as she is actually able to catch up to you when you walk.

It's important to note that all 3 Star Movement Speed Toons can outwalk Twisted Ginger without using Movement Speed Trinkets. This is because the Movement Speed of 3 Stars has a value of 15 (walking), while she has a value of 14 (chasing). You can use this to your advantage while being chased by her, so you don't waste too much Stamina, which is especially good for Toons like Gigi who have low Stamina. However, it is important to note that she does speed up in Panic Mode, with her chasing speed becoming nearly as fast as a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon's walking speed at base without speed Trinkets. (assuming the Suppression card wasn't picked).

twisteds.name: Twisted Razzle & Dazzle
twisteds.speed: None (Static)
twisteds.mechanic: If a Toon runs within the dark red ribbon circle around them, their hostile state will activate. Upon spotting a Toon, they will cause vines to shoot up from the ground underneath the Toon, stabbing at their feet and causing one Heart's worth of damage. If 15 seconds pass without a Toon entering their circle during their hostile state, they will return to their idle position.
twisteds.research: Twisted Razzle & Dazzle are a Twisted that can appear on a random place of the map with a circle of vine-like ribbons. They can be harmless, and you can even stand in their line of sight. They will not attack you as long as you are careful and do not run. If you or another Toon sprint in their circle, they will become hostile and shoot ribbons at the Toon from below, dealing 1 worth of damage. While in their circle, regardless of the Toon's speed, they can still attack if previously aggravated. If a Toon doesn't run in their circle for 15 seconds, they will return to their idle state. If you are in the circle but are hiding behind anything that blocks their Line of Sight, then Twisted Razzle & Dazzle won't detect you and you won't take damage.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Razzle & Dazzle are not a problem as long as sprinting isn't needed and their placement is not on the way of other things (e.g. Machines, distracting spots, and such others). Given that they're not activated with the use of Air Horn, Pebble's Active Ability, or any similar sound alerting cues, dealing with them truly is just about being careful on where you're sprinting.

Distracting when Twisted Razzle & Dazzle on your way is one of the main threats they pose, as distracting Twisteds like Twisted Pebble and Twisted Vee could be pretty dangerous, as they require sprinting to distract with ease. For that reason, try to find other spots to distract that aren't around Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, or try to avoid them as best as you can.

Extracting Machines while around Twisted Razzle & Dazzle is another issue that can be easily solved. One way you can stay safe while extracting near Twisted Razzle & Dazzle is by occasionally checking your surroundings (if no distractors are present or if your current distractor has the same or lower Stealth than your Toon) and alerting other players that you're in their circle so that they don't unintentionally harm you by running in it. If a Treadmill Machine is in their circle, take note that sprinting on one will not activate Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, so you can run on it to extract it faster with no real danger. Once you finish or are almost finished with the Treadmill Machine, make sure you aren't sprinting, in order to ensure you don't activate them after leaving the Machine.

Some Toons are great for dealing with Twisted Razzle & Dazzle or avoid being killed by them, such being listed below:

• Astro: If his Active Ability **Nap Time** is ready to be used, he can use it to put Twisted Razzle and Dazzle back to sleep, allowing him to safely pass by them more quickly.

• Connie: Her Active Ability, **Haunting Escape**, allows her to disappear from any Twisted's line of sight (save for Lethals), meaning that if she uses her Ability whilst in their circle on time or if she runs in it while her Ability is active, she won't be attacked nor activate them. Do note its short duration, however, as one wrong move can cause you to lose a.

• Eclipse (situational): In Blackouts, her speed is extremely high, especially when combined with Trinkets and Items. She can use this to avoid running in the circle if she's getting chased by Twisteds, since she has the potential to exceed their speed from walking alone. She also doesn't sacrifice any Hearts for her speed, giving her more of a chance to survive, even if Twisted Razzle and Dazzle are activated or another Twisted hits her. Outside of Blackouts however, she's likely to struggle.

• Flutter and Rudie: Their Active Abilities, **Floaty Dash** and **Antler Charge** respectively, won't activate Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, as long as they aren't sprinting. This allows them traverse through the circle more safely and quickly, especially when being chased. Their Abilities can also help escape the circle more easily if they're activated.

• Goob: His Active Ability, **Hug!**, allows him to pull any Toons back if they run into Twisted Razzle & Dazzle.

•In a similar fashion, Scraps, with her **Crafty Grapple** Ability, can grapple to any Toons or Machines in across from Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, or even use it to escape their circle when they're activated. Glisten with his **Reflection** has a similar capability, though with the ability to teleport through walls, at the cost of not working on Machines.

• Teagan (situational): Her **Tea Time** allows her to easily heal up from any damage done, either from being hit from another Twisted due to not running in the circle, or being hit by Twisted Razzle & Dazzle themselves when activated. This doesn’t directly help her escape from the circle like other Toons though.

If you plan on using Twisted Razzle & Dazzle as a way to get Tapes/Research/Events' Currencies, **alert your teammates**. Make sure that nobody has a reason to go near them before running in their circle. Note that you only get this encounter if you run in their Line of Sight, and you will not get the Tapes or Research if you activate them outside of it. Doing this is Panic Mode is also a good strategy, when you know everyone is in the Elevator, but you might waste Stamina activating them to get to the Elevator.

For distractors, Twisted Razzle & Dazzle can conflict in Panic Mode, since if a 4 or below Movement Speed Toon is distracting during Panic Mode, they are likely going to sprint as they cannot out-walk majority of the Twisteds in Panic Mode.

Bobette, Flyte, and Tisha can help minimize the need for a distractor to sprint, but this brings up the concern of any of them getting hurt or possibly sprinting. For this reason, Tisha should take advantage of her rather large AOE (which prevents her from having to get into the circle, or getting too close to the distractor), boosting from just outside the circle before heading directly to the Elevator. Flyte can place the gust inside of the circle, walk out of its bounds, and proceed to head towards the Elevator; he can alternatively place a gust on the border of the circle or just outside of it. Tisha and Flyte in most cases could simply walk for the entirety, due to their high walk speed. Bobette (if solar distracting) should get a head start when Panic Mode begins, do one or two more loops before beginning to head through the circle (this is to accommodate for her lower speed compared to the distractor), then start running or sprint-tapping as soon as you leave the circle. Let the distractor lag a bit behind, as to not force you to try to catch up with your average speed (this is dependent on the distractor or your Trinkets as well. For example, a Goob who is distracting could simply run ahead after leaving the circle, and pull you into the Elevator). Bobette (if NOT solar distracting) should hover around the edge of the circle closest to the Elevator; once the distractor first enters the aura ring and gets the speed boost, immediately start walking or running towards the elevator. Avoid entering the circle, as compared to Tisha/Flyte, Bobette's average walk speed can make it rather dangerous for her since she usually needs to run from Twisteds, risking the activation of Twisted Razzle & Dazzle.

twisteds.name: Twisted Rodger
twisteds.speed: None (Static)
twisteds.mechanic: Spawns from a fake capsule being picked up, applies Slow III and Confused III when his fake capsule is picked up. Goes idle if not spotting anyone for 15 seconds.
twisteds.research: Twisted Rodger has the ability to disguise himself as a Research Capsule, based on the investigative nature of his Toon counterpart, waiting for any Toon to attempt to collect him in his clever disguise. When this succeeds, he inflicts two Debuffs on that collector (Slow III and Confused III) to reduce their escaping and extracting time before they can escape from his laser-like attack, giving a worth of damage to any Toon hit. As he is stationary, he has a 360-degree Line of Sight, waiting for a Toon to enter it. If nobody is in his range for 15 seconds, he will sink back to his usual disguise.
twisteds.strategies:
Like Twisted Razzle & Dazzle, he requires Line of Sight to attack a Toon. His attack is also easy to escape the range of, which will also cause him to lose interest, though the Slow III could be hard to manage. Twisted Rodger's fake Research Capsule can be easily distinguished from a real Research Capsule. If there are no Tapes around the middle of the Capsule, it is fake. If there are two tapes around the center, it is real. There can only be one fake Research Capsule containing Twisted Rodger on the Floor.

If a Flutter accidentally picks up Twisted Rodger's Capsule, her **Floaty Dash** Ability isn't affected by the slowness Debuff, so it can be used to quickly escape. This also applies to Rudie and his **Antler Charge** Ability, though it is less potent. If you are not playing as either of them, you may be able to escape by sprinting to cover, as his rising animation takes some time before he can attack.

If you accidentally pick his Capsule up while distracting, an Eject Button will allow you to escape and continue distracting, however the other Twisteds may lose sight of you if used, especially slower ones like Twisted Shrimpo and Twisted Finn due to the high speed, risking an escape of the Twisteds' Line of Sight. If you are playing as a slower Toon such as Connie, Shrimpo, or Razzle & Dazzle (on even-numbered Floors) and accidentally trigger Twisted Rodger's Capsule, you can also use Train Whistle to nullify the debuff.

Twisted Rodger is not highlighted when using Vee and Brightney's Active Abilities. If you notice a Twisted is missing while there was supposed to be one more, Twisted Rodger is on the Floor. While Pebble's Passive Ability and Coal's Active Ability may detect his Capsule as an Item and lead to confusion, there are two Capsules per Twisted on the Floor, meaning an odd number is not possible, making it easy to tell that he's one of the Capsules. Additionally, Twisted Rodger's Capsule isn't highlighted by Research Map, which can be a telltale sign.

Since Twisted Rodger is mainly a threat due to applying the slowness Debuff, Ribecca won't be in much danger if she accidentally picks up his fake Capsule either, due to her Passive Ability, **The Undead**, though you will still have to sprint behind cover or directly away from him. Ribecca could use him as a free boost source, but this is risky in team runs, particularly if Twisted Rodger isn't in a closed off space away from Machines and Items. It also isn't the most efficient since you have to wait for him to return to his passive state before trying for another boost, but opening him in troublesome situations could end up being handy for Ribecca (though this isn't guaranteed due to the randomness).

Ribecca can be a good Toon to play as, if visually disabled players or players with general difficulty seeing the game (i.e. device brightness or glare on their device's screen) are worried about getting hurt or killed by Twisted Rodger. You can also choose to equip Train Whistle for a similar purpose. If Blackouts are hard to see in for you, the aforementioned Toon or Trinket will help save you incase you end up opening his fake Capsule.

twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Toodles is a roaming Twisted that possesses no mechanics. Reflecting her Toon counterpart's young age, her attention span is short, and she can easily lose track of a Toon. However, she is the seventh fastest Twisted in the game (sharing her spot with Twisted Shelly) and easily one of the biggest threats on any Floor except Dyle's Floor. Making three sharp turns normally shakes her off your trail due to her low attention, so use that to your advantage.

Due to this, call out Twisted Toodles if she is loose and if your team has a Shrimpo, Soulvester or Connie. If you plan to distract her, losing her line of sight is barely a problem with her speed. Though distracting with 4 Movement Speed can still be tricky even with Dog Plush and Speedy Shoes, as you are just slightly faster than her. Using Pebble is a great choice to continue distracting steadily, even in Panic Mode. Remember to check your distance from her. If she's catching up to you, sprint to keep yourself safe. Repeating this until everybody is in the Elevator is a smart way to keep your. This technique can also be used with Twisted Shelly and other high-speed Twisteds.

During Panic Mode, she slightly exceeds the speed of Twisted Pebble's chasing speed, making her extremely dangerous. Make sure that once all the Machines are completed, you carefully head to the Elevator, especially if you are a slow Toon under 3 Star Movement Speed like Vee or Rodger.

Due to her darker design, she can be a problem in Blackouts, try to look around corners, utilize Brightney or Vee's Abilities, and play as or stick near light-producing Toons. Her high chasing speed is troublesome in Ichor Leaks, as the slowness caused by Ichor Puddles can allow her to catch up to you. Try to steer clear of puddles, and if you have to walk through one, check your surroundings to ensure she doesn't catch you off guard while you're under its effects.

Keep in mind that, from the behind, Twisted Toodles looks extremely similar to her Toon counterpart, so be careful about mistaking her as a normal Toodles.

twisteds.name: Twisted Blot
twisteds.speed: None (Static)
twisteds.mechanic: Spawns arms across the map, damaging the player by 1 when they get too close to the arms.
twisteds.research: Twisted Blot is a stationary Twisted, meaning he will not move, similar to Twisted Razzle & Dazzle and Twisted Rodger. He will reach into the ground and cause giant Ichor arms to appear on the map, and he will control them whenever his eye is open. The arms will attempt to attack Toons that get too close. After some time, the arms will despawn and Twisted Blot will rest and lift out his hands for about ten seconds, before spawning them again in a different location. Unlike Twisted Razzle & Dazzle and Twisted Rodger, his attack is not conditionally activated, and his arms will attack as long as a target is in range. This Twisted can also be a threat to new players, as when approaching close, his hands will try and lure players with a hand gesture signaling the player to come closer, and could make them think that there is a prize or a buff of some kind, but most new players will not fall for this, since it's apparent that the hands pose a hazard.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Blot himself is passive; he will sit on the floor, stationary, occasionally waking up to move the placements of his two Ichor arms. Getting close to his main body doesn't harm you, but unlike Twisted Glisten, even when he is awake, you won't gain Research, Tapes, or Event Currencies by being close to him.

Even though Twisted Blot himself is harmless, the arms he spawns are aggressive and getting too close to either of them will result in the hand attempting to hit you, resulting in a of damage if successful. Twisted Blot's hands can be dodged, but you have to be quick about it. They have a windup period before they attempt to strike, so use that little time to exit the range of the hand. Sticking to the edge of the hand's range may make this easier to accomplish. Both hands have a somewhat short range, so they should be easy enough to escape. Do note that Twisted Blot could summon either of his hands right on top of his main body, so it is not a good idea to afk near his main body. After triggering Twisted Blot's Ichor hand to slam down, it will be stunned for about 1 second, allowing you to walk past it without getting hit. If a Blot hand is in the process of attacking but changes location in the middle, you will not take damage.

Encounter Research, Tapes, and Events' Currencies are granted by Twisted Blot's hands. Remember that to get the 5% encounter Research and Tapes, you may have to risk getting hit by the hand to gain it. One way to try and avoid being damaged is to walk into the very edge of the hand's range, triggering the attack (and the encounter Research), then immediately turning around before using Stamina to sprint back out the way you came. However, this is more difficult to do with slower Toons.

Twisted Blot's hands can be very inconvenient. They can temporarily block off entire passageways and even Machines, which forces Toons to wait for the hand to disappear, and they can force Toons to lose a Heart if there is another Twisted chasing them and there is nowhere else to exit. The hands could also spawn in a distractor's loop, causing them to swerve back and potentially get hit, along with causing a greater difficulty in distracting or forcing the distractor to change locations. The hands can spawn on top of players, making afking a bad decision on Blot Floors. If Twisted Blot's hands start to spawn near you, immediately evacuate to avoid getting hit. You may have to wait it out if Twisted Blot's hand spawns in an inconvenient area. Do keep note that like Twisted Sprout's tendrils, being fast enough, walking on the edge, and dashing as Flutter or Rudie could let you pass with no hits.

Try to avoid Twisted Blot's hands as much as possible, especially in Blackouts, since they will blend in with the atmosphere, similarly to Twisted Sprout's tendrils. Try to walk carefully to avoid running into them if a Blackout is present. You can also try to communicate where Twisted Blot's hands currently are, so they don't catch teammates off guard. Equipping Spare Bulb can help in seeing his arms even clearer, though it is a very situational Trinket to select, especially considering Twisted Blot is a Rare Twisted and won't spawn too often, until later on.

Ichor Leaks can be very dangerous if the Ichor hands appear above their puddles, due to the Slow I making it really difficult to dodge them. It's best to wait for the hands to move if you need to walk through a specific puddle, otherwise you risk losing a Heart. In the event that an Ichor hand is above an Ichor Puddle during Panic Mode, you should try to find another path to the Elevator, otherwise biting the bullet and taking a hit may be the only option, as losing 1 Heart is better than dying to the Panic Mode timer.

Floors that have Machines in dead ends are dangerous if Twisted Blot is on the Floor (or places with 2 exits, with Twisted Blot's hands covering both), as his hands could block your way in or out. If you want to do Machines located in closed spots, it is advised to wait for the hand to sink down or make sure his hands are somewhere else. If you are trapped while extracting, also wait. If it is the last Machine, do not finish it, as you could lose time waiting for Blot's hand to sink down. Finishing the last Machine will either get you hit trying to dodge the hand or even die to the Panic Mode timer. You could try to run through, but there is always a risk of getting hit. As such, the best way to escape safely is to get in range of the hand, let it attempt to hit you, and then run past it. Having a high Movement Speed could help here. Additionally, Treadmill Machine Skill Checks can trap you on a Machine while hands spawn—there isn't really a way to avoid taking damage in this case.

twisteds.strategies:
On normal Floors, Twisted Coal doesn't pose much of a threat due to her speed. However, her attention span does make it harder to lose her as she might turn towards you if you're trying to shake her off by going around an island. When trying to escape her, maintain your speed and don't turn too fast if you're around an island. The most preferable way is by going to a table and walking around it while staying out of her sight.
