On Blackouts however, you need to be careful. With her speed being equivalent to Twisted Bobette, and her heightened detection range and hearing radius, you should avoid getting into her sight at all costs—especially if the Toon you're using has 2 or lower Movement Speed, as it is not enough to outrun her. Overall, when dealing with her, use a similar strategy to facing Twisted Bobette: try your best to not get in sight. If she does spot you, quickly go around an island and cling to it while making sharp turns until she loses interest in you. However, this may be harder to do due to her high attention span, as once you're back inside her line of sight, you'll be spinning around the island longer, which could cause you to lose lots of Stamina and get you hit in the process. Unlike Twisted Bobette, she can be more difficult to spot due to her smaller size, dark color palette, and to her lack of sound emission. In this case, Brightney and Vee's Abilities can be useful to help spot and avoid her. It's best to carry around speed or Stamina Items like Chocolates, Pops, and Speed Candies to help you get away from her.

If you have 4+ Movement Speed, it should be possible to loop her around an island in Blackouts, as long as you don't run into other roaming Twisteds. Just communicate your plans on where you intend to distract—her high detection range could cause her to spot another target while you loop her.

In the case where no distractors are present, you'll have to be cautious and hope for the best. Vee's Remote can be very helpful for doing Machines out in the open to reduce the risk of being spotted with Twisted Coal's immense eyesight range. 8 walking, 21 chasing
Panic Mode: 9.6 walking, 25.2 chasing

twisteds.mechanic: Has a chance to hop over obstacles, both while wandering and in chase.
twisteds.research: Twisted Cocoa's main ability is being able to jump over most obstacles that don't reach the roof, both while roaming and chasing. Additionally, she has decently high chase speed, low roaming speed, and a really low attention span, likely to balance out how she can be hard to lose due to her ability.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Cocoa may act like a faster Twisted Toodles, but her jumping mechanic completely changes how you avoid her.

In terms of speed, the only Toons Twisted Cocoa can outrun (without Movement Speed Trinkets) are Connie, Razzle & Dazzle (on even numbered floors), Shrimpo, and Soulvester due to their 1 Movement Speed, leaving them with 20 Run Speed units. To counter this, however, Movement Speed Trinkets like Speedy Shoes or Pink Bow might improve your chances by a large factor.

However, when it comes to other Toons, Twisted Cocoa can **NOT** be outwalked (unless you are a 5 Star Movement Speed Toon with a Movement Speed Trinket, or a 4 Star Movement Speed Toon with both Dog Plush and Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool (while Active)), meaning you will have to rely on running, though two exceptions include 1 Looey and Eclipse in a Blackout, both who have the same speed as her chasing speed as long as they don't turn too many corners without sprinting.

When you are being chased by her, you should try to get far away, as her short attention span can make her easier to lose, especially if you hide behind a obstacle with distance from her, even if it can be jumped over. However, if the map is not that large or there are other dangerous Twisteds you don't want to run into, try going through multiple rooms with high walls to hide or loop her, as Twisted Cocoa cannot get through walls. Avoid using smaller islands to loop her away, as she can jump over them.

If you are distracting her, kiting is no issue, but if you are using an island, you have to be wary, as if you turn, Twisted Cocoa could get stunned in an attempt to jump over the island, which could temporarily block your looping path, or jump ahead of you, making you either get hit or need to swerve away from her, something that could be detrimental if you have a ranged Twisted like Twisted Scraps with you.

Note that Twisted Cocoa can jump to secondary levels on maps with slightly raised floor areas. This can allow her to catch you off-guard, especially when working on Machines. Pay attention to her and be prepared for sudden chases. Additionally, this mechanic allows her to spot you even on AFK spots on certain maps (most notably the Diner map variant 1), so be really alert of this if she does spawn when you and your team plan to go AFK.

Twisted Eclipse could be quite annoying due to her higher speed, attention span, and ability, which leads other Twisteds towards her location. Because of this, it could attract dangerous Twisteds like Twisted Dandy or Twisted Pebble, so try to avoid her if Twisteds like those spawn. In case she does see you, immediately run away and find an island to remove Twisted Eclipse and the other Twisteds that were attracted. Note Twisted Eclipse uses her howl every time she aggros or switches aggro on a Toon. If she's nearby, make sure to avoid missing Skill Checks as to not attract her to the location of the player (save for when she's already chasing another Toon). Do note that the aggro goes to where Twisted Eclipse howled, so it is better to run from Twisted Eclipse herself instead of staying in your spot and looping. Her very high detection range may be an issue to people who play as 1 Stealth Toons like Brightney and Gourdy, as they can easily aggro on her from afar.

However, her ability is useful for distractors, such as Pebble if his Active Ability is on cooldown and Looey (if he doesn't have an Air Horn in his inventory). She functions like a running Air Horn, triggering non-occupied Twisteds, which removes the time needed to round all the Twisteds up, though hearing ranges still apply.

Twisted Eclipse is much more annoying in solos due to the absence of a distractor resulting in Twisteds always wandering around unoccupied, making it more likely her howls will successfully call Twisteds over. This can also get really annoying on Floors with a higher Twisted count, and dangerous if there are difficult Twisteds like Twisted Pebble. In solo runs during Halloween, it's helpful to have a Smoke Bomb handy, especially on Floors with more dangerous Twisteds, in order to negate the effects of Twisted Eclipse's howl, though they are one-time use.

Be careful during Blackouts as Twisteds are more than likely to catch you off guard when alerted by Twisted Eclipse's howl. The reduced visibility can also make it harder to avoid her, so try to keep an eye out for her glowing eyes, and always check around corners.

Ichor Leaks can be bad when paired with her for multiple reasons. The Illness III can make it harder to hit Skill Checks, with failing them potentially alerting Twisted Eclipse, in turn possibly creating a chain reaction ending in her howling. Additionally, depending on how nearby Twisteds are positioned when she howls, escaping from them and Twisted Eclipse could require having to run through or awkwardly avoid an Ichor Puddle, which can be very dangerous if you don't have the Ichor Puddle Immune Auxiliary Stat.

Note that Twisted Eclipse attracts Twisteds towards the location of where you were **originally** seen, so if you get away from there, the Twisteds won't see you. This could make escaping her easier, but running away could cost some Stamina, so be mindful when escaping.

twisteds.research: Twisted Flutter is a fast Rare Twisted who hunts down the Toons similarly to Twisted Toodles. While Twisted Flutter is slower than Twisted Toodles, she makes up for this with her higher detection range to see Toons slightly further away. Her higher range also gives her more perception of her surroundings, allowing her to see Toons slightly easier to the sides and behind her compared to Twisteds with a normal detection range. Completely opposite of Twisted Tisha she has no idle time, meaning she doesn't stop at all while roaming. Her roaming speed is also almost the same as her chasing speed, allowing her to patrol the floor faster than other Twisteds.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Flutter has almost the same Stats as an average Twisted, but her constant speed and unstoppable search is a requirement of constant alert and patience. This Twisted can be gone for a while and then unexpectedly turn back to her previous nodes in a short time thanks to her idle time being zero (0) frames. If you have average or below average Movement Speed, some obstacles that can shield you from both patrolling and pursuing can help while she is targeting you, as she can suddenly give up on you only to catch you in her sight again, wasting the Stamina you had used to escape. Due her fast Walk Speed, she can come to the same place that you're in many times, making it quite time-consuming to finish Machines in those places. For that reason, it is slightly easier to be a fast extractor like Gourdy or Yatta, so you finish Machines fast before she patrols to you and your Machines.

It is very easy to distract her as she just matches Twisted Teagan's speed, so her mechanic won't affect you at all.

During the Easter Event, when a Spring Fever occurs Twisted Flutter will be the most dangerous Twisted along with Twisted Flyte, as her roam and run speed will be much faster from the Energized II Buff. Given that she will be faster than even Twisted Pebble when roaming, it can make her a big threat when doing Machines in an open area, as she can ambush you unexpectedly. Thankfully, due to the secondary effect Spring Fevers give to Twisteds, being Dazed II, Twisted Flutter's attention span is halved, making it easier to escape from her sight.

twisteds.name: Twisted Gigi
twisteds.speed:
10 walking, 19 chasing
Panic Mode: 12 walking, 22.8 chasing
Suppression: 11.5 walking, 21.85 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Attempts to steal the Items in your inventory with her hand, stealing from the first slot to the last and bringing it to her machine. Players can retrieve the stolen items from her machine unless their inventory is full or the machine itself is full. Has a cooldown of 12.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Gigi is a specially-ranged Twisted like Twisted Goob and Twisted Scraps. Thus, she can use her hand to launch a high ranged attack on Toons if spotted. However, unlike them, she uses this ability only if the pursued Toon has Items in their inventory, taking them in an order from left to right.

When she spawns, her Item stash claw machine spawns with her at any of the Machine spawn points on a given Floor. 50% of the Items on the Floor are already stashed away in the claw machine. While roaming, she will pick up Items from the Floor, carrying them back to the claw Machine. Once the claw machine is filled up with 30 Items, it will turn off, preventing Toons from getting their items back and making any Item taken after the machine breaking irretrievable. In that case, Twisted Gigi pauses for 5 seconds after stealing, before continuing chase in a Toon is in LOS.

She ignores all Toons while bringing an Item back to her stash, regardless of Stealth or other circumstances.

She is a bit faster than the average Twisted's speed, being as fast as Twisted Yatta, and can keep a high tracking time on the Toon she is attempting to charge at.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Gigi should be carefully maintained with her speed and ability cooldown while you are trying to distract. If she successfully hits you with her ability multiple times, your Items will diminish, resulting in a much smaller chance of survival. If you have no Items left and there are no Items on the Floor, she will behave somewhat like other normal Twisted and is barely a threat. Do note that there are other Twisteds that can be dangerous while distracting, such as Twisted Pebble, Twisted Vee, Twisted Scraps, and Twisted Goob. If you only need to distract Twisted Gigi, try to loop around cover so that her grabbing arm loses line of sight, letting you keep your Items.

If you plan to distract multiple Twisteds alongside Twisted Gigi, it may seem easier just to let your Items go, however this can potentially cause issues. This is mainly because she will dart straight to her claw machine after stealing an Item, ignoring you and all other Toons regardless of Stealth, making it harder to grab her attention again without risking injury or death. A better idea is to use up whatever Items you have, if possible, to keep Twisted Gigi from taking your stuff and running away. You could also have a backup distractor with no Items take her, since they can keep her on them, preventing you from having to waste your Items.

Try to let teammates know if she's currently running to her claw machine, though it'll be evident by an unique running animation (her arms are further apart and move more erratically), as well as an Item's icon appearing above her head when she steals it. This icon also shows how many uses are left for multi-use Items like Box o' Chocolates. Teammates may panic and get themselves or others hurt, without realizing that Twisted Gigi can't attack them in her stealing state, so ensuring good communication can keep things from becoming chaotic.

If you aren't distracting and you are holding any important Items, like a Health Kit, it could be good to fill your first Item slot with niche or minimal use Common Items like Gumballs. Since Twisted Gigi will always go in order of your first Item slot first, filling your first Item slot will make sure she can't reach your second and third slot. This leaves you without the need to find her stash and try to get your valuable Item back, especially if you can find a similarly niche item to act as item bait. Stamina should also be used carefully while trying to lose Twisted Gigi, as she has a higher speed than other Twisteds. Make multiple sharp turns in corners until she's given up to be safe. Due to her high attention span as well, try to lose line of sight quicker by going around islands. As Twisted Gigi immediately attempts to use her grab if not on cooldown and if the player has at least one Item, she is one of the easiest Twisteds to escape safely if encountered while the player is in a dead end. Thus, try to keep at least one Item if extracting with her present. While stretching her arm out to steal an Item, she can't hurt any Toons, so you could bait her before running straight through her (though this is far riskier if you have low speed or a slow reaction time).

It is recommended to play as Bassie to avoid losing important Items and even be able to retrieve Items for her team. Her Active Ability, **Springful Sharing**, lets her either drop her Items somewhere to prevent losing them or be able to return any Item stolen from Twisted Gigi by taking things from her stash. She can even act as a transport system between other Toons by letting others get their Item stolen for Bassie to retrieve from the claw machine, giving it to any Toons that could use it. Her 4 Star Stealth and high mobility makes this easier too. However, this method of trading can be done without Bassie.

Bobette's **Precious Packaging** makes her invincible to Twisted Gigi's grab, allowing her to keep her Items safe, though it’s important to consider the long cooldown and a need for good timing. With this in mind, Bobette could bait the grab to give a distractor a head start, or to help prevent teammates' Items from being stolen. Scraps can also do this with **Crafty Grapple**, but she does require an anchor point (other Toons, Machines, and Twisted Gigi's stash) to use her Ability.

Having Bassie, Cocoa, or Yatta can be very helpful as they can try to drop Items in places away from the Elevator or certain Machines, forcing Twisted Gigi to go after them to pick them up. They can also use their Items as fodder for teammates, in order to protect more valuable Items from being stolen and brought to the stash.

When trying to retrieve an Item from the claw machine there are a few things you should note:

•If Twisted Gigi steals or picks up an Item, she will run over to the machine, which can cause her to consequently chase, hurt, or kill you after she tosses the gachapon into the machine;

•While roaming, she can path straight to the machine to count her stash, leading her to spotting you;

•The Item you retrieve is random, so you may have to make multiple attempts to get the Item(s) you specifically want;

•It takes 3 seconds of holding down to activate the claw, so try to check your surroundings before doing so;

•When an Item is retrieved, it'll be dropped out of the machine in a gachapon. The gachapon rolls like a ball, so try to pick it up quickly before you lose sight of it.

The claw machine can hold up to 30 Items. If it reaches this limit, the claw machine breaks, stops playing music, and you can no longer retrieve Items from it. After the claw machine breaks, Twisted Gigi will steal your Items with no way to get them back, and without running to the claw Machine. After stealing an Item in this situation, she idles for 5 seconds while ignoring all Toons.

During the Halloween Event, be cautious about opening any of the Trick or Treat Doors; chances are, if she's not already present on the Floor, she can potentially appear and steal the Item in your first slot when you open it, no matter where you go. If you have a healing Item or otherwise important Item in your first slot, abstaining from opening Trick or Treat Doors might be the best option, albeit this is still a bit rare.

Even though part of her hand doesn't count as her hitbox, it is still very large, as she is lying down, so be careful when looping her. Only take sharp corners if you've built some distance, as she could barely reach you and end up hitting you.

twisteds.name: Twisted Glisten
twisteds.speed:
6 walking (When passive)
15 walking, 24 chasing
Panic Mode: 18 walking, 28.8 chasing
Suppression: 17.25 walking, 27.6 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: He has a meter above his head that increases when a Toon is not near him for some time, and decreases when one is close. When the meter is full, Glisten becomes faster and aggressive. After you finish all the Machines, he becomes aggressive immediately. Once he is enraged, there is no way to get him back to passive.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Glisten is a unique Twisted who roams passively at the start of each Floor, unable to attack Toons. He has a meter above his head that determines when he becomes enraged. This meter begins empty when he first spawns, then continuously fills; the more alive Toons there are, the faster it rises. The only way to reduce the meter is by staying close to him; if he can see any alive Toon within range, his meter will slowly deplete until it is empty.

If no Toons accompany him and his meter is allowed to fill completely, he becomes enraged, gaining drastic speed and becoming hostile for the rest of the Floor. While enraged, Glisten never pauses while roaming, similar to Twisted Flutter and Twisted Flyte. He also becomes instantly enraged during Panic Mode.

Glisten speaks several times throughout the Floor: once when the Elevator opens as a warning, whenever his meter rises to 50%, occasionally when he spots a Toon while passive, and once when his meter becomes full.

There is no way to return Twisted Glisten to his passive state once he has become enraged.
twisteds.strategies:
A good strategy is to put a designated Toon in charge of watching Twisted Glisten, which allows the rest of the team to focus on the Floor as normal.

As Twisted Glisten is not very fast in his passive state, most Toons should be capable of accompanying him. He wanders around aimlessly, sometimes into the path of other Twisteds, so if you're accompanying him, be aware of your surroundings. If he walks by a Machine, either leave him and complete it quickly, or ask someone else to babysit him while you do the Machine. His meter does not fill very quickly, taking about 70 seconds before he becomes enraged, so leaving him alone for a little while to escape other Twisteds or when a teammate is on the last Machine is viable. If he wanders into the path of a distractor, don't go too close. Instead, wait for him to leave their area and resume accompanying him. Keep in mind, while Connie and Bobette's Active Abilities are being used, Twisted Glisten's meter will not decrease.

As he instantly enrages when the last Machine is completed, good communication is key. Alert your teammates when you're on the last or even second-to-last Machine to ensure Twisted Glisten's comforter is not caught off-guard. When the last Machine is being readied, you should make your way away from him. It's better to use his Trinket, Vanity Mirror, because it helps you escape from him in his enraged state during Panic Mode. You can also use Alarm, which has a similar effect, but do note Alarm's effect only lasts for 10 seconds.

If you're doing a solo run, it's recommended to stay near him and do Machines as you come across them. If he's getting far away from your current Machine, quit extracting and resume following him. Once only one Machine remains on the Floor, ditch him and extract it. Another solo run strategy is waiting until his 50% Dialogue appears and wait beside him until it's on 0% again, then extract Machines and repeat this process until the last. This strategy works better on maps with more visibility and with faster extracting Toons like Vee, as during Blackouts he can prove difficult to track down again, which is why a Toon, such as Rodger, can help during a Blackout by using the lens in his head, which helps the player see Twisteds such as Twisted Glisten.

In the event of an Ichor Leak, try to avoid the Ichor Puddles as much as possible, since the Slow I can make it harder to escape from Twisted Glisten, or reach him before he enrages. Ichor Stains can make it harder to see where he is, enraged or not. Ichor Puddle Immune Toons can have some sort of advantage since their speed can't be dropped and their vision won't be affected, but be aware that not all of them have the capacity to babysit or escape from Twisted Glisten.

If Twisted Glisten is near the Elevator, it's also highly recommended to alert your teammates to stop extracting and wait until he's walked away. Do note that his meter will, still of course, increase during this time period, so you should also have it be around 0%. Regardless, whether alone or with friends, trying to prime the closest Machine to the Elevator to finish last is a great idea.

Since keeping Twisted Glisten calm is a high priority, Toons with high Stealth such as Astro, distractors that can ditch (or simultaneously distract) any followers, and supporter Toons with low extraction are good picks when trying to occupy him. It is extremely important to find Twisted Glisten as fast as possible because his passive state will only last 70 seconds without anyone accompanying him. His meter can go down only when someone is in his detection range, meaning if a low Stealth Toon is going towards him, it can be useful when he is about to be enraged. Do note however, once Panic Mode is about to begin, the chances of that Toon's survival against him might not be easy.

In the unfortunate event where Twisted Glisten shatters and you're distracting, it is recommended to be a distractor Toon such as Looey, Pebble, Blot, or Goob, as they have high mobility; use Dog Plush (can also be paired with Speedy Shoes/ Clown Horn/ Ribbon Spool) to help distracting Twisted Glisten. Treat Twisted Glisten like Twisted Pebble, and loop him around a structure. Do note, however, that his hitbox is smaller compared to Twisted Pebble's, so it's a bit tougher to slow him down on objects. If you feel that Twisted Glisten is catching up to you, try sprint-tapping or gain a distance from him and try looping again. Note you don't have to use a heavy amount of Stamina if you loop him around an island. Do note that looping him on a small island and hugging it tightly could basically reduce the need to sprint.

If Twisted Glisten shatters in a solo run, survival is key, since he is almost identical to Twisted Pebble, sometimes faster if looping obstacles. Try to find a long obstacle and loop him around it, having a speed Item like the Speed Candy could increase your chance of escaping.

Be aware that he will be quite fast in Panic Mode and that other Twisteds will mess you up if you try this strategy.

Recommended Toons to accompany Twisted Glisten are:

•**Astro** (situational): If a Toon with higher Movement Speed is unable to help take over with Twisted Glisten, Astro is a great fix to watch him. As aforementioned, Astro has high Stealth, so he can escape from Twisted Glisten easily in Panic Mode. His passively faster Stamina regeneration can help him maintain his Stamina. He can even give some Stamina to the chased Toon to prolong the sprinting.

• **Bassie**: Her high Stealth and mobility makes her a very good choice, as she can easily lose Twisteds interrupting the babysitting, easily catch up to him if he wanders too far, and escape easily when Twisted Glisten enrages. If any teammates take Twisted Glisten's aggro, she can gift them a mobility or healing Item to help them survive and escape.

•**Blot**: Blot's 4 Movement Speed and 5 Star Stamina helps him escape from Twisted Glisten's high speed when enraged. He can also use his Active Ability, **Blot Jr.** to support himself and his teammates and help them escape Twisted Glisten easily.

•**Bobette** (situational): Bobette's immaculate Stamina capacity allows her to run for a good while, which can help if she needs to avoid other Twisteds while babysitting, or make it to the Elevator during Panic Mode with little risk of running out and dying. Her Active Ability can be used if enraged Twisted Glisten gets too close to her, or if she ends up getting pincered by multiple Twisteds. Her Passive Ability can help teammates or distractors make it back to the Elevator safely, or even outwalk Twisted Glisten. The biggest problems with Bobette are however her average speed and low Stealth; The average speed means she relies on Trinkets and Items to outrun Twisted Glisten during Panic Mode.

•**Connie** (situational): If a Toon is able to take control for her, or she is able to use her Active Ability, she can easily escape Twisted Glisten long enough for him to leave or her to get to the Elevator. Connie can also use her high stealth and Ability in order to avoid having Twisteds interfere with her being able to stay around Glisten. However, due to her low Movement Speed, Connie may be unable to escape from him should her ability or Stealth fail her.

• **Cosmo**: Since Cosmo has both high Stealth and Stamina, he can run from Twisted Glisten with a low chance of being hit during Panic Mode. He can also heal up any teammates who take aggro from Twisted Glisten and get hit by him, though don't forget that healing will use up one of your.

• **Cocoa**: Because of her **Bonbon** Ability, she can generate BonBons, which can give her or Toons that are babysitting Twisted Glisten a 25% Movement Speed boost in case the Toon babysitting Twisted Glisten needs it in Panic Mode. If she does babysit Twisted Glisten herself, her 4 Star Stealth and 4 Star Movement Speed will pose little problem getting away from an enraged Twisted Glisten. Be aware of her lower Stamina, due to it only being 125.

• **Eclipse**: While in most circumstances the most she has is her 4 Star Movement Speed, this still gives her a sufficient capability of escaping from Twisted Glisten during Panic Mode, especially since her Stamina is a fair average. Her low Stealth can be troublesome but it also means she can keep Twisted Glisten on her and protect slower Toons. During Blackouts however, she becomes even better, with an extremely high amount of Stamina, and speed that far exceeds Twisted Glisten's, she can babysit him with little to no issue (save for certain Debuff sources and ranged Twisteds potentially endangering her).

• **Finn** and **Shelly**: Their similar Passive Abilities reward them a speed boost when a Machine is finished, which gives them enough speed and time to outrun Twisted Glisten during Panic Mode. Finn may be the best pick for this, as he gains a higher boost than Shelly (35% > 25%).

• **Flutter** and **Rudie**: Due to the similar nature of their Active Abilities, they are both a great pick for babysitting Twisted Glisten, as it allows them to dash away from Twisted Glisten when he becomes enraged in Panic Mode. Flutter may be a better pick, as, paired with her high mobility and longer dash, she will have little to no issues escaping.

• **Flyte**: Because of his Ability and high speed, Flyte can increase his speed and then flee from Twisted Glisten in Panic Mode. Be wary of his Stamina though, like Cocoa.

• **Glisten** (situational): His Active Ability lets him be a perfect solution to his Twisted counterpart, as he can teleport to a teammate when the time is necessary. Like Scraps, though, this relies on your teammate being in a good area. This especially applies with Glisten's 2 Star Stealth, because if Glisten is unfortunate enough, Twisted Glisten will spot him.

•**Goob**: Goob has 4 Star Movement Speed and Stamina, making him able to get to the elevator quickly. If Twisted Glisten happens to be chasing a teammate with low Movement Speed such as Rodger or Connie. Goob's Active Ability **Hug!** can bring them into the elevator safely.

• **Gourdy**: His Passive Ability, Sugar Rush, can give himself and his teammates a speed boost when Panic mode starts, giving everyone a chance to escape. While Gourdy's 1 Star Stamina and Stealth may be a bit risky for him, his 4 Star Movement Speed can make up for them.

•**Pebble**: His incredible mobility makes him a really good babysitter, since he can easily escape from Twisted Glisten even during Panic Mode. He can use his Active Ability to keep Twisted Glisten from chasing other teammates with lower Stealth than him (save for Shrimpo), while his Passive Ability can let him see potentially useful Items that make escape easier.

•**Scraps** (situational): Scraps' Active Ability allows her grapple to a nearby Toon or Machine, letting her escape Twisted Glisten. However, like Glisten, this relies on a teammate or a Machine being in a convenient spot, as Scraps will struggle to get away with her below average speed, though her high Stamina can (slightly) mitigate this.

• **Sprout**: Sprout can see his teammates from anywhere with his Passive Ability Overprotective. This can help Sprout see if anyone is extracting the last machine, and prepare himself for Twisted Glisten's enraged mode. His high mobility also gives him an advantage.

•**Vee** (situational): Vee's Passive Ability will allow her to see the progress of the last Machine and if it is being completed. This can be useful in runs where your team isn't very communicative. However, it's recommended to just let Vee do the extracting herself, as an inattentive Vee could result in disaster due to her bad mobility and stealth. She can also be useful for locating Twisted Glisten if he is lost from sight.

It's also recommended to have a Tisha on your team, as her Active Ability, **Tidy Up!**, can help others either get to the Elevator or outrun Twisted Glisten (slightly better than Flyte's **Gust**).

Do note that Twisted Glisten will outrun most Toons during Panic Mode, as his chasing speed is 28.8 during Panic Mode (without the Suppression Card used), which means that Toons with 5 Star Movement Speed (or more), being Bassie, Eclipse (in Blackouts), Looey (on 1 Heart), Pebble, Razzle, and Waxwell, might have difficulty fleeing from him without Items or Movement Speed Trinkets. Having Twisted Vee chasing you is unfortunate, as Twisted Glisten's chasing speed is the same as Pebble's running speed, including in Panic Mode, reducing your chances of survival.

twisteds.name: Twisted Goob
twisteds.speed:
8 walking, 16 chasing
Panic Mode: 9.6 walking, 19.2 chasing
Suppression: 9.2 walking, 18.4 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Goob will pull any Toon in his line of sight, This can however be prevented by staying out of this Twisted's sight, or hiding behind an object as he tries to pull you. Has a cooldown of 12.
twisteds.research: Twisted Goob is a roaming Twisted that wanders the halls aimlessly. Much like how every other Twisted attacks, he will start chasing any Toon that is in his Line of Sight. However, quite similar to Twisted Scraps, when spotting a Toon, he can stretch out his arms to grab and pull them, setting their location to his, and typically being able to use his melee attack immediately after. His ability requires Line of Sight with a Toon, meaning it will not drag them in if it connects through objects. After using his ability, he won't be able to use it again for another 10 seconds. However, he is still able to hit you with a melee attack if you get too close to him.
twisteds.strategies:
Since Twisted Goob can grab Toons at range, being alert is important when you know he is on a Floor, especially in a Blackout as he can get you while he is hiding in the darkness. Stay away from wide, open spaces, and look around before turning corners or leaving cover and duck behind something the second he pauses.

His ability will fail if the Toon leaves his Line of Sight, and you can tell this if he appears to pull you to no effect. This either means ducking behind cover or outranging him. Thus, Speed Candies, Boxes o' Chocolates, Eject Buttons, or Toon Abilities, such as Flutter or Rudie's, have the potential to save you if you notice him in time when he spots you. If you can't reach cover, run directly away from him to hope to escape his range as Twisted Goob's ability has a shorter cooldown than Twisted Scraps' cup tail attack. His ability will also fail if his Toon counterpart or his sister's use their Abilities, due to invincibility frames. This allows Goob to grab Toons before his Twisted can, or allows Scraps to grapple onto Machines or Toons before being grabbed.

When Twisted Goob uses his ability, he is stalled for a few moments. Therefore, if you know it's impossible to avoid being detected, approach the edge of your current cover, let him see you, and quickly duck back behind it so his ability misses and you have time to get away. This will put his ability on cooldown and let you run away as normal.

In Blackouts it’s advised to be cautious as Twisted Goob can easily catch you off guard, grabbing you from the darkness. Try to look out for his glowing eyes, preferably around a corner. You should also trying to listen for his wind-up sound, as that can assist you in the case that visual cues otherwise wouldn’t.

Unlike Twisted Scraps, there is still a way to avoid the attack after being pulled, and that is if a lower Stealth Toon appears in his Line of Sight while pulling. He will pull you as normal, but will then ignore you and start chasing after the lower Stealth Toon, not using his melee attack. This can be helpful if you're playing as a low Stealth Toon, because then you can save people under attack by distracting him with your presence as well as not being pulled by him. This can be especially helpful to new distractors dealing with Twisted Goob.

When distracting Twisted Goob, be wary not only of his ability, but the amount of time he is stalled. This can mess with your looping pattern. Giving yourself additional space to move around him if you are distracting multiple Twisteds is important; pay attention to when he's about to use his ability and use Stamina to duck around a corner if you suspect he's about to use it, because distracting him and other Twisteds could be quite risky if you don't know what you're doing. Listening to his wind-up sound can prove useful, though if it’s not possible or difficult to hear, you may benefit from looking back at him and reacting to his ability animation. You can also turn on the "Spotted Visualizer" setting, giving a visual cue for his wind up.

Smoke Bombs do not work against his ranged attack when seen: he will still pull you like normal. This also applies to Connie's Active Ability. Interestingly, however, Bobette's Active Ability works on his ranged attack, though he will still pull your box like usual depending on your timing. This can be used to tank hits if desired, but remember Bobette will be immobile while in her present.

Keep in mind that if you are hiding, when Twisted Goob's ability stalls him, his attention span will still decrease like if he is pursuing another Toon. That would also mean that if he spots you and you immediately hide behind something, if it's far away, he would fail the ability. Run near the object, and Twisted Goob will finally lose interest and leave. It would be wise to do that at your own risk, however.

Twisted Goob's ability can be used to one's advantage, though with a risk of losing a. One can use it to get to certain spots more easily, especially if Twisted Goob is close to spots where one needs to go to with urgency, like the Elevator during Panic Mode. Though, once again, this is risky, so only do this if you have more than 1 Heart to spare and there are no other choices. If you're running low on Stamina while being chased, and Twisted Goob is in a good position far away, you can let him pull you away from the other Twisteds; you lose a Heart to him, but in turn get good distance away from other Twisteds, letting you shake them off, especially as Connie or with a Smoke Bomb. This may be done without losing a Heart as Bobette due to her Active Ability, but this requires good timing to be pulled by Twisted Goob, but activating the Ability before he actually hits you; during Panic Mode, her Active Ability needs to be ready, and is only really helpful if there’s more than 12~ seconds left of Panic Mode, as you will have to accommodate for her hard 8 seconds of hiding.

Due to Twisted Goob being very similar to his Toon counterpart from behind, you may accidentally get close to him thinking he is a Toon, so be wary. However, you should be able to distinguish Goob between Twisted Goob easily. Just note he will move much slower (if he's wandering) compared to his Toon counterpart. Another way to tell the difference between the two depends on your eyesight and how far you are away from him, but you can also notice his claws are much sharper compared to his Toon counterpart's, and his head doesn't move as much. In Blackouts his eyes will also glow.

twisteds.mechanic: Her special ability allows her to attack a toon at range using her tail, dealing one heart's worth of damage. Has a cooldown of 15.
twisteds.research: Twisted Scraps is a roaming Twisted who acts similarly to her brother. She has a special ranged attack with a cooldown of 15 seconds, where she stretches her tail towards a player to hit them. Twisted Scraps can also attack with a melee attack up-close, much like other Twisteds. Like Twisted Goob's ranged attack, Twisted Scraps' ranged attack will fail if you are able to get behind an object in time, use Bobette's **Precious Packaging** Ability at the right moment, Cardboard 'Armor' (works once per Floor), or if you are currently being gaurded by Soulvester.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Scraps, just like Twisted Goob, has a ranged attack. However, unlike him, Twisted Scraps does not pull you towards her, or pulls herself into you as a reminiscent of her Toon counterpart's Active Ability. She instead stretches her tail up to a Toon to attack them, having a cooldown of 15 seconds afterwards. To prevent getting hit, get out of Line of Sight immediately if she suddenly swings her tail to the side. An easy way to break Line of Sight is by covering yourself behind an island.

Twisted Scraps' way of attacking is similar to Twisted Goob's, so the best way to survive her is having strategies related to him. Plan out your way of distraction with her bad attention span and speed. If there are no possible distractors at the moment, it's best to stall her by wasting her own ranged ability and take easy steps of escaping her from sight, like Twisted Goob.

If a Goob sees Twisted Scraps prepare to attack a teammate, he can pull them out of danger with good timing, as they'll be invincible while being pulled. Scraps becomes invincible when she uses **Crafty Grapple**, so she can use an anchor point (Toons and Machines) to effectively tank or dodge Twisted Scraps' attack. Just note that in Scraps' case, she has lower speed and average Stealth; the speed can make it a bit tedious to escape Twisted Scraps, while the Stealth could potentially cause her to swap aggro with a lower Stealth teammate; keep these things in mind when using her Ability in this way.

Twisted Scraps should not be underestimated during Blackouts, much like her brother. If you are on a Floor and are aware that Twisted Scraps is on it, and if you are spotted by her, it's best you duck behind an island, as her snake-like tail cup can easily catch you off guard. Brightney and Vee are both good choices to counter Twisted Scraps. It can also be good to check around corners and look for her glowing eyes. If you’re able to, listen for her wind-up sound as well, as that can allow you to react in time if visual cues otherwise wouldn't due to the darkness.

If you're distracting Twisted Scraps, try to revolve around an object as her tail cannot reach you behind there, but do return to let Twisted Scraps see you again so she doesn't lose aggro and go after other important assets of your team. If you struggle to hear her wind-up sound, it can help to look back at her and react to her attack animation instead. You can also turn on the "Spotted Visualizer" setting, giving a visual cue for her wind up. Her incredibly low speed means even a 3 Star Movement Speed Toon can distract her alone, but they have to brush against an island often since if they don't have a speed Trinket they can't fully outwalk her, and they'd have to be cautious during Panic Mode.

Twisted Scraps is a bigger threat in wide, open spaces with little to no objects. You should hide behind objects often. Remember, if she sees you, run as fast as you can towards an object and get behind it. Keep in mind that she does have above average detection in terms of vision than other Twisteds, so be careful when she is an area where you need to be. Be careful when doing Machines in these kinds of areas. If there are no nearby hiding spots and you have no mobility/immunity based Ability, your best bet is to run directly away from her, as you can possibly escape the range of her attack.

Smoke Bombs won't work against her ranged attack when she sees you. This also applies to Connie's Ability. However, she will lose interest in you if her tail strike is on cooldown.

If you are in the unfortunate situation of Twisted Scraps near the Elevator during Panic Mode, try to remember if she had used her tail strike before. If she has, then just try to get in without getting hit. Otherwise, "disarm" her tail whip by taking her aggro, hiding behind an obstacle, and waiting until her attack fails, then make a quick getaway into the Elevator. Try to take note and memorize her tail strike's cooldown and when she last used it—taking too long outside the Elevator could get you hit. Bobette can tank Scraps' attack, which proves useful for herself or her teammates. Bobette's **'Precious Packaging'** lasts for 8 seconds and she’s immobile while it’s active, thus it’s highly not recommended to use her Ability if there are around 10 or less seconds of Panic Mode, as she can’t cancel it early.

The disadvantage she has is her low speed, so if you are going around an island and constantly missing her attacks, she isn't one of the biggest threats anymore. Unlike Twisted Goob she has a lower attention span, so that can help too.

twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Squirm appears on the ceilings. Getting too close to him will cause him to reach down and grab the player. Clicking side to side quickly enough will let the player go, otherwise, Twisted Squirm damages them. After Twisted Squirm grabs a player, or if left alone for long enough, he traverses to a different area.
twisteds.research: Twisted Squirm, unlike all other Twisteds, spawns on the ceiling rather than the ground. Getting too close will trigger him, and he will reach down and grab the player. The player must click side to side (the A and D or arrow keys if on PC) to break free from his grasp. If the player fails to do so, Twisted Squirm will take 1 away from the player, and will proceed to relocate himself. You can see where he relocated to by following a line of dust puffs on the ceiling that indicate which direction he went.
twisteds.strategies:
Generally, if you have a watchful eye or can click fast, Twisted Squirm is not that difficult, as his attack is easily defended by rapid clicks, similar to Treadmill Machines Skill Checks. However, on some devices, like consoles, it can prove tricky as you need to rapidly move your joystick a lot, though if you can practice that, you should be fine.

If you are not that good with defending though, looking up most of the time (while avoiding other Twisteds and/or the distractor) can be helpful if you know he is on the Floor. If you see him, simply turn around or find a way to maneuver around him. It's additionally important to be cautious around doorways as they can obscure your view and get you grabbed by him.

However, if he hangs above an high rarity Item, a Machine, or blocks off an important pathway, either bite the bullet or have a more skilled/stealthy teammate ward him off for you. When you see him, you should alert your teammates, as if someone triggers him, it will cause him to relocate (though he does relocate if not provoked for long enough), albeit he makes a sound when doing so.

When distracting while Twisted Squirm is on the Floor, it can be a good habit to look up at the ceiling every so often, just so you can adjust your path or change location when needed. Being grabbed by him will heavily endanger you, as other Twisteds will continue chasing you, potentially hitting or killing you in the process. A teammate with higher Stealth than you could volunteer to force Twisted Squirm to change location, but this may be too risky if any such teammates are on 1 Heart or are Cosmo.

Some Abilities work when someone or the player themself is grabbed by Twisted Squirm, so they can be useful to save or be saved from one of his attacks. These Abilites include Connie's **Haunting Escape**, Goob's **Hug!**, Scraps' **Crafty Grapple**, and Bobette's **Precious Packaging**. Twisted Squirm cannot grab you if you quickly break his line of sight or range, similar to ranged Twisteds, so if you run into him, just try to turn back or continue forward at full speed. It's far easier to dodge him with higher Movement Speed. Additionally, using a Smoke Bomb immediately discourages him from pouncing you if he already did.

Some Floors, such as the Main Character themed Floors (like the outdoors section of Sprout's Floor or the fossil area of Shelly's Floor), have very tall ceilings. If you know he is there, it could be hard trying to find him, especially if it's a Blackout. However, as long as you can master the clicks, you can easily deal with this.

Do note that during Blackouts, his eyes glow, so finding him will not be that much harder, though you may be more thrown off-guard, especially in the aforementioned large maps. Toons such as Brightney and Vee can help as their Abilities can highlight Twisted Squirm for you, though do remember to look up as Twisted Squirm resides there.

twisteds.name: Twisted Waxwell
twisteds.speed:
8 extinguished, 18 lit, 20 extinguishing

Panic Mode: 9.6 extinguished, 21.6 lit, 24 extinguishing
Suppression: 9.2 extinguished, 21.7 lit, 23 extinguishing
twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Waxwell leaves a trail of flames when roaming around the Floor, giving Ignited for 30 seconds to Twisteds who walk on the trail, but if any Toon is near him, Twisted Waxwell will stop producing his flames and run away from the said Toon.
twisteds.research: Twisted Waxwell will have his flame lit when a new floor begins that he has spawned on, leaving a fire trail. This trail provides the Ignited buff to any Twisteds that cross it. If a Toon enters the small ring around him for a short period of time, his flame will go out. He cannot in any way harm a Toon directly.
twisteds.strategies:
For the most part, one can simply ignore Twisted Waxwell as he cannot deal any damage himself, especially if you have a distractor. Ensuring his flame is kept out is vital however, as he can wander into the area the distractor is working in. This becomes far more important if you have no distractor, as the chances of Twisted Waxwell's trail reaching a Twisted increases exponentially.

He has a very high walk and run speed, so one should ideally leave faster Toons such as Pebble, Bassie, Flutter, etc. to the task of chasing him down to put out his flame.

The Ignited -giving trail will continuously spawn behind him until his flame is put out, which can be very troublesome as the vision increase and attack cooldown decrease are rather significant. It can especially make ranged Twisteds and Main Character Twisteds more dangerous due to their abilities and/or stats.

The vision buff can also be annoying for distractors if there are any Toons with lower Stealth than them, especially when it comes to Twisteds with already high detection radii like Twisted Brusha, Twisted Pebble, and Twisted Shrimpo; Ignited amplifies their sight even more.

The attack cooldown buff can be dangerous if you're trying to escape from a Main Character Twisted, since they already have a lower attack cooldown. This can also make it more dangerous and difficult to damage boost, as the point of the strategy is to get hit on purpose to escape from Twisteds since they'd usually be stunned for long enough. A reduced cooldown means they may not be stunned long enough for you to escape.

If Twisted Scraps, Twisted Goob, Twisted Gigi, and/or Twisted Sprout are afflicted by Ignited, their ranged attack cooldowns are reduced. It is **highly** recommended that you only encounter or distract these Twisteds if you already know how to dodge consistently, as you will have to dodge much more often. For this reason, it's paramount to have someone on top of extinguishing Twisted Waxwell's flame if someone distracts Ignited ranged Twisteds. Since you will have to dodge more often, you may also expend more Stamina, so having a Toon like Astro on your team can be very useful. If there’s multiple distractors, one of them can also take Ignited ranged Twisteds, only having to focus on solely their sped up attacks, leaving the other to distract ones without ranged attacks.

With all of these hurdles amplified in a solo run, where no one else can help you, it is advised to stay as cautious as possible. Make sure you're next to islands at all times, as the Twisteds' higher vision radii can repeatedly interrupt you and chase you. Be sure to know where the Machines are so that when you are stuck waiting for Twisteds to exit your Machine, you can go to another one. Redirecting Twisteds is also easier to do, as the heightened vision radius can get their attention quickly. Also, this becomes a large problem in smaller maps, as Twisteds are more likely to get to you, so you should have Items to escape those situations or finish Machines quicker and relocate. Finally, extinguishing Twisted Waxwell is unadvised unless you have good mobility, as his high speed could make you lose Stamina and maybe run into Twisteds.

Using Blushy Bat or having Soulvester on your team can directly counter the cooldown reduction from Ignited. The extra 3 seconds from Blushy Bat and the 1.5 extra seconds from **Soul Shield** should give enough time to escape from an Ignited Twisted, with Soulvester additionally preventing Health loss.

twisteds.name: Twisted Dandy
twisteds.speed:
9 walking, 16 chasing
Panic Mode: 10.8 walking, 19.2 chasing
Suppression: 10.35 walking, 18.4 chasing
twisteds.mechanic: Twisted Dandy is alerted to completed Machines, along with instantly killing anyone he attacks, like any other Lethal.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Dandy is a massive, dangerous roaming Twisted that wanders the Floors aimlessly. Reflecting his enigmatic Toon counterpart, he has a unique spawning condition that must be met before he has a chance to spawn: players must not buy any Item from Dandy's Store for at least three Floors that Dandy appears on. Each time every surviving Toon skips a shop, Dandy will become increasingly upset. Upon skipping the third shop in a row, Dandy will become angry and Twisted Dandy will gain a spawn weight of 5.

On every subsequent shop players skip, Twisted Dandy's spawn weight increases by another 5. If the spawn weight is 15 or higher, the music in Dandy's Shop will stop playing. The Mastery TV will flash with Dandy's icon if Twisted Dandy can spawn. When this occurs, or if anyone buys an item from Dandy's Shop at any time, Dandy will return to his cheerful self, and players must skip three more shops for a chance to spawn Twisted Dandy again.

Twisted Dandy continuously emits the sound of a distorted version of music box 'Clair de Lune', and he makes stomping noises as he walks. These sounds are loud enough that they can be used to determine his location and if he has spawned on a Floor before the Elevator has opened. When a Toon fails a Skill Check or completes any Machine, Twisted Dandy will immediately charge towards that Machine unless another Toon has his attention. If he doesn't find a Toon at the location of the Machine, he will go back to wandering the Floor.

If you ignore Dandy's Shop 5 times in a row after he becomes angry, Twisted Dandy is guaranteed to spawn on the next Floor.

As he is a Lethal Twisted, he will instantly kill any Toon; he is also not dispelled by Smoke Bombs, Savory Charm's effects (unless you got by another non-Lethal Twisted), Connie's Active Ability, or Guarded, similarly to Twisted Dyle. However, Bobette’s Active Ability works on him.
twisteds.strategies:
**Spawning**

Make sure that all players are on the same page before attempting to spawn Twisted Dandy. Since Dandy's Shop is an important source of Items that will be fully off-limits while attempting this, try to avoid bringing Toons that are more reliant on Items such as Connie and Shrimpo, as they'll have a much harder time surviving. If you do intend to bring them, try to alert them to helpful Items found on Floors and reserve extra for them.

**Twisted Dandy**

As Twisted Dandy is attracted to completed Machines from anywhere on the map, try to prime one or two to complete as bait if you see him drawing close to a poorly-equipped teammate. Priming means to fill a Machine to be almost complete, but not fully completed. Do not prime Machines near the Elevator (unless you can wait for him to be on the other side of the map) when he is present, as having him run there during Panic Mode is the last thing you want. Instead, prime a Machine that is either far away from or out of sight of the Elevator and have a teammate with a high Extraction Speed complete it once the other Machines are done; conversely, if you trust your teammates, prime many Machines near each other and finish them all at once in order to minimize the amount of time you spend running back and forth.

Once you complete any Machine while Twisted Dandy is present, duck behind cover or take the long way around to escape; his pathfinding will prioritize the shortest route towards it.

Even if Teagan, Sprout, or Ginger aren't present in your party, it's still recommended to pick up any Tapes you find. Dandy runs can be difficult, and you may choose to abort one after he spawns, or if your party members are depleted, or if he sells some particularly useful Items. In these scenarios, having Tapes on hand is great. They're also good to have in the case that a team member forgets that you're trying to summon him and makes a purchase, you should immediately seize the opportunity and buy anything good during that intermission because his spawn rate will be reset anyway.

Since Twisted Dandy moves at the same speed as Twisted Finn, the best thing to do is remain aware. He can be distracted and evaded as normal. Kiting him is both easier and harder due to his size, as he might switch directions. Try to stand at the end of a long island and feint to one side or the other to make him lose aggro faster. He has a harder time with corners, so use them to your advantage when you can, making sharp and sudden turns around objects. If sandwiched by Twisted Dandy and another Twisted, prioritize running past the other Twisted, as both the hitbox and damage difference make them much less of a risk. Avoid small objects unless you already have distance on him—he will just swap directions and get a hit.

If you decide to solar distract with a Bobette on your team, it is highly advised to NOT loop around an island or take sharp turns, as Twisted Dandy could easily switch aggro onto her and instantly kill her. Instead try to find an open area where you can follow a medium-large circular path. Try to give Bobette a slight head start for getting to the elevator during Panic Mode, as this allows her to avoid being left behind and insta-killed.

In the event of a Blackout, you'll have to make use of the music and footsteps emitting from Twisted Dandy. These sounds should be easy to hear, but if you otherwise aren't able to, make use of his glowing eyes, have Brightney or Vee highlight him and other Twisteds consistently, use/have a light-producing Toon, and use the Spotted Visualizer Setting to signify where he spots you from. Be careful if his back is turned (and you're unable to hear the sounds he emits), as only his eyes glow, with his body generally being darker and thus harder to see in a Blackout.

When an Ichor Leak occurs, try to avoid Ichor Puddles as much as you can, since the Slow I and Ichor Stains can make it harder to escape or avoid Twisted Dandy. The reduced Skill Check size from Illness III means failing Skill Checks is a generally more likely occurrence, which combined with Twisted Dandy's extreme hearing range means he'll constantly be alerted. Having or playing as Tisha can prove useful, as she can temporarily clean up puddles in particularly dangerous or troublesome spots. If there's a distractor distracting Twisted Dandy, Tisha should try to clear up their looping spot of any puddles to make it easier and safer, but she should utilize careful timing so Dandy doesn't switch aggro to her. Prioritizing easier Machines (typically Treadmill Machines) is also a good strategy while affected with Illness if you struggle with the reduced size.

**Suited Toons**

Some Toons that are especially well-equipped for Dandy runs include:

• Sprout/ Teagan/ Ginger: Tapes that otherwise wouldn't have much purpose could be turned into something that heals the party/themselves, so try to give them any Tapes you find.

• Coal/ Pebble: Pebble's Passive Ability, **Fetch!**, highlights Items in the vicinity, ensuring less get left behind, while Coal's Active Ability, **Scout**, can highlight Items for other players, making it even easier to find Items like Health Kits or Bandages which could prove an advantage. Pebble's **Speak!** Ability can be used to lure Twisted Dandy from anywhere on the map, redirecting him away from teammates or objectives.

• Gigi: Her Active Ability gives you a random Item, so she can have more Items and more saves (like getting a Speed Candy to get Twisted Dandy off someone, or getting a Valve to extract a Machine instantly). Plus she's a bit more likely to get rarer Items than Dandy's Shop and even Items exclusive to the shop, so not buying from it doesn't affect her much.

• Bassie: Her Ability to share Items allows her to make sure that all are contributed fairly, which considering the scarcity of them is quite important. This way, she can store Bandages and Health Kits for emergencies rather than having to wait for the right person to pick it up.

• Yatta: Her Passive Ability being able to drop candy can give her really good Items, making you need to buy less from him. Due to Twisted Dandy's high attention span, speed Items like Box o' Chocolates or Speed Candies are necessary, something she drops.

• Blot: He can use Tapes to activate **Blot Jr.** when his teammates are being chased by Twisted Dandy. However, it shouldn't be used if Twisted Dandy is distracted.

• Cocoa: She can constantly drop BonBons, helping the team/herself stock up on a well-rounded item. The speed increase can help with keeping distance from Twisted Dandy, while the Extraction Speed increase can help with getting Machines filled faster.

• Finn/ Shelly: Both of their Passive Abilities give them a Movement Speed boost every time a Machine is completed, countering Twisted Dandy's ability to charge towards completed Machines. Finn's **Reel In** gives 35% while Shelly's **Problem Solver** gives 25%, thus Finn may have better survivability, depending on the other Twisteds present, while Shelly can also use **Inspiration** to help teammates complete Machines faster.

• Vee: She can highlight all Machines on the map consistently with **Mic Check**, therefore allowing people to plan out which of them to complete first, and find those in blind spots. She will also be able to highlight all Twisteds, helping her and her team avoid getting caught off guard, especially if Twisted Dandy rushes to a completed Machine.
