This is shown through a meter above him. He can instantly kill anyone he attacks in one hit regardless of the current health status or Trinkets, just like any other Lethal.
twisteds.research:
Twisted Dyle is a special Twisted found exclusively on his Floor upon picking the TIME'S UP Card. Without player intervention, he is very slow and will patrol like any other Twisted.

Similarly to Twisted Glisten and Twisted Gourdy, Twisted Dyle has a meter above his head that is often visible through obstructions. It starts empty and dictates how quickly he moves: the fuller the meter, the faster he becomes. He emits constant ticking noises that speed up as the meter increases. If he spots a Toon, his meter will slowly fill up until he either kills the Toon or loses them. If he kills the Toon, his meter will instantly reset. If he loses them, his meter will slowly deplete until it is empty or until he spots another Toon. Unlike Twisted Dandy, Twisted Dyle can't hear a machine being completed, but he can still hear a failed Skill Check, Pebble's Active Ability, or an Air Horn from anywhere on the Floor. If this happens, his meter will immediately fill up to halfway (unless it's already past that), and he will start rapidly accelerating towards the location of the noise. When the meter is very full and Twisted Dyle is nearby, your screen will gradually turn red the closer he gets to your position. As he is a Lethal Twisted, he is not dispelled by Smoke Bombs, Savory Charm's effects (unless you got by another non-Lethal Twisted), Connie's Active Ability, or Guarded. However, Bobette’s Active Ability works on both Twisted Dandy and Twisted Dyle.
twisteds.strategies:
Twisted Dyle can be a very belligerent and hazardous Twisted to deal with, being able to reach the speeds higher than any Toon and rapidly speeding up upon hearing a failed Skill Check from anywhere on the Floor.

If you encounter Twisted Dyle (found exclusively on odd Floors once per run upon picking the TIME'S UP Card), it is recommended to have Toons in your team who are great at finishing machines quickly, such as Shelly, Gourdy, Vee, or Yatta. Using Magnifying Glass or other Trinkets that speed up extraction can be helpful, as there are 25 Machines on the Floor. It is **NOT** recommended to try to distract Twisted Dyle, since he speeds up the longer you are in his Line of Sight and instantly kills you no matter how many you have. Thankfully, Twisted Dyle's moving sounds are easy to hear, and he has a very short attention span. If you get spotted by him, sprint and take cover until he loses sight of you.

If you accidentally pick up an Air Horn and don't want to endanger yourself or your teammates, you can wait until the Floor is finished, or you can let Twisted Dyle see you and use it while you're in his Line of Sight. This will prevent Twisted Dyle from heading to your location and speeding up even more. However, this should only be attempted if you are near a place you can hide behind.

If you get a Blackout when Twisted Dyle is present, having a Brightney or Vee on your team is great, as their Active Abilities allow them to highlight Twisted Dyle and other Twisteds that appear on the Floor. Do note that only Common Twisteds can appear to support Twisted Dyle, so there's no threat of other dangerous Twisteds. If Brightney or Vee are not on your team for a Blackout, you can also detect Twisted Dyle in the dark and through walls using his rage bar.

If you get an Ichor Leak when Twisted Dyle is present, having a Tisha on your team can help reduce the danger of Ichor Puddles, since she can temporarily remove them with her Ability. Illness III can be very dangerous, especially for Toons with a low Skill Check Stat or for players who struggle with hitting them. If you step in an Ichor Puddle and aren't confident in your abilities, it's best to wait until Illness wears off before you extract. Watch out for Twisted Tisha if she's on the Floor, as she can increase the size of puddles, making it harder to avoid them and thus potentially increasing the likelihood of failed Skill Checks.

Please note it is near to **IMPOSSIBLE** to distract Dyle if you are not prepared for it beforehand without Items or external boosts, even if you are using Bassie with Bone and Feather Duster, due to Bone's cap to 40 Movement Speed, however, it is still possible to pull this off. It's also not possible unless you have really intense skill to kite him around an island like you would with Twisted Pebble due to his extremely low attention span, as he would lose aggro easily, not to mention his obviously higher speed. Therefore, it's best to just take the other Twisteds if you are distracting, and let him roam around. Make sure to communicate to your teammates where he is in case someone fails a Skill Check, so they don't get caught off guard. If you accidentally fail a Skill Check and you hear Twisted Dyle speeding up to your location, having speed Items, like Speed Candies, a Box o' Chocolates, or an Eject Button, are highly recommended as they give you higher speeds to outrun Twisted Dyle and escape him if he spots you.

However, although you can't completely preoccupy him, he can be tricked into losing his speed by getting in his Line of Sight and quickly leaving it, which is easily done due to his aforementioned low attention span. This is advised in case someone in your team misses a Skill Check, uses an Air Horn and such other cases, though it's not recommended if you are a Toon with less than 3 Movement Speed (including 3 Star sometimes) and/or if Twisted Dyle's bar is halfway filled, assuming you don't have Movement Speed enhancing Trinkets or Items, as you will be in danger and likely die. Attempt this only if you're extremely familiar with him.

The only Toon who can outrun Twisted Dyle with a full meter is Looey on 1 Heart using Clown Horn and Pink Bow (41.38 run speed). Because of this, you might intend to distract. However, because of the constant need to sprint, you still shouldn't do it. The only scenarios where it would be possible to pull off distracting Twisted Dyle in this case is with a large amount of Boxes o' Chocolates or Pop items at hand, placed around your distracting area from Bassie's, but even then you would have to have good communication with your team to speedrun the Floor, as you'll run out of items eventually and have to flee, especially if Panic Mode is imminent. Despite this, some people have been able to pull this off for the duration of the Floor, though they are quite skilled. Another distracting strategy for Twisted Dyle is equipping Feather Duster/Bone and Glazed Fondant Bag and having Cocoa place BonBons in a circle so the distractor can repeatedly use them while distracting Twisted Dyle.

Failed Skill Checks make Twisted Dyle charge to the Machine you have failed on in the shortest path towards it regardless of how close he is, so it is important to get behind some obstacles, so that while he goes through the path, he won't be able to see you. Although, it can sometimes be hard to detect where Twisted Dyle's path is before it's too late, which is why you should be more careful when he is closer to you, and this technique can be more difficult the lower the Movement Speed you have. Even when Twisted Dyle gets to the Machine, he will traverse at raging speeds in unpredictable random directions because his meter is still high, so it is in general safer to use Mime Makeup or Thinking Cap, and make sure to stay clear of Ichor Puddles.

In dire straits, getting hit by another Twisted will grant immunity for a while, allowing you to use Items or Abilities to escape or pass through Twisted Dyle's instant kill if he's too close to evade immediately (this is because of the Twisteds' cooldown effect). This is inadvisable unless you believe you are going to die otherwise.

These Toons may have special advantages for encountering Twisted Dyle:

•**Bassie**: Bassie's 4 Star Stealth, 5 Star Movement Speed, and 4 Star Stamina give her extremely good survivability. Using Bone can raise her highest speed to 40, matching Twisted Dyle's max speed. Her 1 Star Skill Check is an issue for some, but it can be fixed with Mime Makeup or eased by Thinking Cap. You can, if you want to, also help Looey by distributing Boxes o' Chocolates if he intends to distract Twisted Dyle/or wants to distract him herself—Bassie always plays a key role here. She can also help with Treadmill Machines, completely negating the need to use the Trinkets above.

• **Blot**: His supporting Ability can save yourself or other Toons from Twisted Dyle. Beneficially, once Twisted Dyle attacks the decoy, his meter goes back to zero. Blot's 1 Star Skill Check may impede him similar to Bassie, Cosmo and Shrimpo, but you can easily negate this with Mime Makeup and/or Thinking Cap, and if an Ichor Leak occurs on the Floor, Blot will be immune to the Illness and Slow Debuffs, and Ichor Stains. Like Bassie, he can help with Treadmill Machines, negating the use of Skill Check Trinkets.

• **Bobette**: Her high Skill Check, which reduces Skill Check failure, and max Stamina, making escapes easier, results in Bobette being a solid choice. Her Passive Ability can help some Toons get a small boost to escape Twisted Dyle, and more passive Toons can regenerate Stamina. While risky, her Active Ability can save her, even from Twisted Dyle, but caution should be advised as it can leave her vulnerable.

•**Brightney**: Her Ability and good Extraction/Stamina Stats can help her deal with Twisted Dyle, especially when a Blackout occurs, though her 1 Star Stealth can bring unwanted attention. If you understand the mechanics at play, use her low Stealth to aggro Twisted Dyle from far away and save teammates when they are chased, but also be able to save yourself in a timely manner. Fortunately, due to Twisted Dyle's low attention span, you still can easily lose him.

• **Brusha**: She is able to make extraction faster for other Toons as well as herself, and her 4 Star Skill Check isn't shabby. Her low Stealth can be an issue, but it can also be used to protect others. With the abundance of Machines, she should have no issue with using her Ability to paint every Machine she sees, heating up the overall extraction of a team effectively, though it will be a little tricky to keep the Machines highlighted for everyone if Twisted Brusha or Twisted Tisha are on the floor, as they can either override or clear up the paint.

•**Cocoa**: Her good Movement Speed and Stealth makes traversing easy. In spite of her bad extractability, her Bonbons can help in almost every scenario, with the +50% Extraction Speed boost countering her low extraction and generally speeding up Floor progression, and the +25% Movement Speed buff aiding in escapes (whether its for her or teammates) and extracting Treadmill Machines. Escaping from Twisted Dyle also could be less difficult if your inventory is filled with Bonbons, as well as if you lay them on the floor.

• **Eclipse**: Her good mobility and lower Stealth makes her suited towards helping redirect Twisteds. Her Blackout buff helps strengthen this, making her a lot faster, glow bright, and ease traversal, being as fast as Looey on 1 Heart. The Twisted highlight at the start of a Blackout can also be really useful, letting her and her team know right off the bat where all threats are. Her average extraction Stats make her an okay extractor, but there are better alternatives to extract, though she has an advantage with Treadmill Machines, particularly in Blackouts.

• **Eggson**: Eggson's Passive Ability can help make Floor progression faster, with his average extractability and mobility making him be able to move at an okay pace and finish Machines decently fast.

• **Finn**: Finn's good mobility (with his Passive) and Extraction can make the Floor progress faster, though he could be in trouble with his 2 Star Stamina. Priming Machines can help teammates assist him out of sticky situations.

• **Flyte**: His Ability can help himself and other Toons escape Twisted Dyle; he himself has good mobility, making him a good choice. Do note that his Ability is a bit weak, and his 2 Star Skill Check could prove tricky. Regardless, Flyte's high extraction is a bonus. Additionally, he can assist with working on Treadmill Machines with his 4 Star Movement Speed, or provide his Ability to teammates on Treadmill Machines so they can speed up its completion as well.

• **Flutter**: Flutter's Ability, **Floaty Dash**, gives her a Walk Speed of 67.5, which already makes her significantly faster than Twisted Dyle during her dash, even without running. Do note that Flutter's Ability only lasts three quarters of a second, has a long cooldown, and her 2 Star Skill Check may cause some issues, with her bad extractability overall not making her be able to extract Machines efficiently, except her high mobility helping with Treadmill Machines. Her Ichor Leak immunity can also help to reduce the risk of Skill Check failures, being slowed while chased, or having valuable information obscured.

• **Gigi**: Like Shelly, her 5 Star Skill Check helps Skill Check failure happen less frequently. The reduced Stamina does make it a lot harder to survive, but her Ability, **Surprise!**, can be extremely potent, from instantly completing Machines with Valves to easy escapes with Eject Buttons, though the long cooldown and RNG involved make it unreliable. Detrimentally, it has the potential to grant Air Horns, which could get the user in trouble in the moment where they need to swap them for something else. To counter this, you could try to use your Air Horn while already being chased by Twisted Dyle to stop him from getting his bar full, then pick up the Item you want.

• **Glisten**: His good Extraction Speed and Ability make surviving easier, his Ability being best applied to cut chase with Twisted Dyle before he speeds up. However, 2 Star Skill Check and Stealth Stats can make things difficult if under pressure. Do note that his Ability has a long cooldown, relies on teammates and has a rather small targeting range, so reliance on it shouldn't be maintained. Twisted Dyle's low attention span may make this more viable, but if he's at full speed, be careful.

• **Goob**: His Active Ability can help pull other Toons away from danger, and can also be used to bring Toons with high Extraction Speed and Skill Check towards incomplete Machines, making it quicker to complete the Floor. His low Stealth is the least of your worries, as Twisted Dyle's attention span is incredibly low, and Goob's 4 Star Movement Speed and Stamina allow him to outrun all Common Twisteds. Despite his low Extraction Speed, Goob's excellent mobility lets him extract Treadmill Machines quickly, and his 3 Star Skill Check can lower the risk of failing a Skill Check.

•**Gourdy**: Gourdy's high Extraction Stats and good mobility makes him perfect, with the boost from his Active Ability helping with survivability and extracting and his Passive Ability making returning to the Elevator easier all adding to bonuses. However, his 1 Star Stamina and Stealth could make getting rid of Twisteds a hassle, especially if Twisted Dyle sees you, though skill and some Trinkets could mitigate them, with the Stealth also being able to save teammates.

•**Looey**: Looey's good mobility and Extraction make him one of the best Toons for combating Twisted Dyle, even being able to outrun him with Clown Horn and Pink Bow and help distract the other Common Twisteds for your teammates. Do note that you still can't distract Twisted Dyle full-time as Looey unless you are really well prepared. If not distracting, Looey is still quite good at every Machine, having high Skill Check for minimal failure and good Movement Speed for Treadmill Machines.

•**Pebble**: Despite the dangerous Active Ability and lackluster extraction, his Movement Speed and Stamina can be useful for extracting Treadmill Machines and distracting Common Twisteds and his Passive Ability helping with locating potentially helpful Items. Just be really careful to not use the Active Ability, as it causes Twisted Dyle's meter to fill up immediately and cause trouble for you and your teammates, since Pebble is unable to outrun Twisted Dyle at his fastest regardless of what Trinkets are used on him.

• **Razzle & Dazzle**: Note that, since Dyle's Floor can only appear on odd-numbered Floors, Razzle is always going to be active, meaning that you will always have 5 Star Movement Speed and 1 Star Extraction Speed. Similarly to Pebble, Razzle's high Movement Speed can help with Treadmill Machines or distracting. There's also the added bonus of having higher Health so even if you slip up and run into a Common Twisted, you can still have Hearts to spare.

• **Rudie**: Rudie is a decent all-rounder, being able to glow in the dark in Blackouts, and whose Active Ability can be useful if caught in a pinch with Twisted Dyle, although it may not serve you as well compared to Flutter's **Floaty Dash**. Use it to cut behind objects or walls.

•**Shelly**: Shelly has great Abilities that buff extraction and repositioning, making Floor progression faster. Her high Skill Check makes failing really sparse and speeds extraction, letting her excel in dealing with Twisted Dyle. If multiple players use Vee's Remote (usually the case in coordinated runs), she will gain high Movement Speed from her Passive Ability and can scout the Floor out. 2-4 more Shellies in a run can easily make floor progression quicker. The high amount of Machines makes boosting other players more viable, as you can remain paired more easily. However, like Finn, her 2 Star Stamina could prove hard to manage.

• **Sprout**: Despite his poor Extraction Speed and Skill Check, his Passive Ability, that allows him to see other Toons and heal them with Tapes can be useful for preventing death (though the Common Twisteds are a really small threat compared to Twisted Dyle). He is also most likely to get more Tapes quickly by extracting on Dyle's Floor, due to the high amount of 25 Machines on the Floor. Like Pebble and Bassie, Sprout's high Movement Speed and Stamina can also be useful for extracting Treadmill Machines. Keep in mind, his 2 Star Skill Check can be tricky.

• **Squirm**: Although his survivability is sub-par, his extraction potential makes up for it. With his 100% Extraction Speed boost, a Machine can be done in around 15 seconds, and even without it, it takes around 30 seconds. However, with winding up your Ability slowing you down and the slight scarcity of bookshelves, you should try to use your Ability sparingly. Additionally, manage Stamina well and take note of your Stealth.

•**Tisha**: Her Ability allows her to help slower Toons out of chases, and her 4 Star Movement Speed and Skill Check make completing it somewhat less challenging, though they are slightly opposed by her 2 Star Stamina and Extraction Speed. If an Ichor Leak occurs, she can sweep up troublesome Ichor Puddles, helping everyone complete Machines and get through the Floor more easily.

•**Vee**: Locating Machines and Twisteds makes it easier for her to plan routes to certain tricky placements. This, along with her good Extraction and Blackout glow, make her a decent pick, although her bad mobility and survival can really trouble players using her.

• **Waxwell:** Waxwell's well balanced stats make him a great option for encountering Twisted Dyle, as his 5 Star Skill Check and Movement Speed make up for his low Stealth, Stamina, and Extraction Speed respectively. His Active ability can be very useful for supporting Toons with high Ability Cooldowns, although it doesn't work on himself or other Waxwells.

•**Yatta**: She has good mobility, Extraction, and an Ability that can produce both speed and extraction-based items, making her an excellent Toon for taking on Twisted Dyle. She's additionally able to make the Boxes o' Chocolates needed for Looey's temporary Twisted Dyle distraction. Her 1 Star Stamina and 2 Star Stealth can be a bit hindering like Gourdy, but her higher Stealth can help with passing Twisteds to Brightneys, Gourdies, and Shrimpos in case of lower Stamina and many factors are able to mitigate these for an experienced player.

The below Toons, however, may have disadvantages when encountering Twisted Dyle:

• **Boxten**: Although he has good extraction, this is heavily dependent on your teammates' experience. If they are unreliable, there's a good chance they will die quickly and Boxten won't have any other bonuses that make it worth using him. He could be good if they can survive, but it still isn't recommended to use him.

• **Connie**: Her extremely low mobility, 2 Star Skill Check, and now near-useless Ability make her an awful choice for handling Twisted Dyle. Though she does possess 5 Stealth, 4 Star Extraction Speed, Ichor Leak immunity and glowing in Blackouts, it's just not worth it.

• Astro, however, can be a decent alternative if you still want to do a Twisted Dyle run with high Stealth, as he has average mobility, also glows in Blackouts, his Active Ability can provide support for other Toons (especially if someone plans to distract Twisted Dyle) and his Passive Ability allows for quick Stamina regeneration, though, like Connie, his 2 Star Skill Check can cause issues if you are inexperienced with hitting them.

• **Ginger**: Her below-average mobility and average extraction potential makes her a less valuable asset to the run, with the mobility also making escaping Twisted Dyle difficult. Her 4 Star Stealth could be useful, though solo/small runs usually make it hard to pass Twisteds off, and giving Twisteds to Toons could risk the Toon's Health. Her Ability is also quite difficult to utilize properly, as Twisted Dyle insta-kills and the map is quite large, making healing opportunities sparse.

•Low Skill Check Toons like Cosmo without Mime Makeup or Thinking Cap, as hitting the Skill Checks, especially for the Circle Machines, can be difficult, and the pressure from Twisted Dyle doesn't help. However, they can choose to help with Treadmill Machines, reducing any risk associated with the low Skill Check Stats. Slipping up could bring disaster to yourself and others, so it's recommended to stay back and support other Toons when they need it, as all Toons with 1 Star Skill Check (except for Shrimpo) provide some type of support (Bassie can distribute Items, Cosmo can heal struggling teammates, and Blot can use Blot Jr. to divert attention and reset Twisted Dyle's speed if needed).

• **Poppy**: Like Boxten, Poppy's all rounded Stats make her extraction quite mediocre. Her Ability is also situational and won't offer any value for Twisted Dyle due to his instakill, and won't offer much assistance with helping you get away from Common Twisteds due to them being already easy to escape. Even when her ability is active, her run speed (37.5) won't be enough to get away from him if his meter is too high or if the chase goes on too long.

• **Ribecca**: Ribecca's Passive Ability, **The Undead**, makes her immune to all Debuffs and non-Trinket negative Multipliers. However, the only Common Twisted who can cause debuffs (being Twisted Brusha) isn't guaranteed to spawn on Dyle's Floor. If Twisted Brusha does spawn though, Ribecca can get a random 10% Stat boost by purposefully extracting from vandalized Machines. Her ability can also be useful when an Ichor Leak occurs, as she won't be affected by the Illness or Slow Debuffs, however this is entirely based on chance; when it does happen, she can run through the puddles to constantly get a Stat boost. The other Common Event Toons' Abilities, being Rudie's **Antler Charge** and Eggson's **Fixer Upper**, may make them more viable options due to the consistency.

• **Scraps**: Her below-average Skill Check and speed can be deadly when encountering Twisted Dyle, though her really situational Ability could save her sometimes. She does have some pros though, as her high Stamina can (somewhat) mitigate her mobility, and her Ability can provide easy escapes with the abundant amount of Machines on the Floor.

•**Shrimpo**: His already terrible Stats make him really bad at normal Floors and some Twisteds, so Twisted Dyle is basically impossible for him. His bad Skill Check can also make the other Toons get in trouble when Twisted Dyle is charging towards their direction. His Stealth can be used to your advantage to lure Twisteds away, but you likely won't escape without a hit or two or without using an escape Item due to his awful mobility. However, he can be used at an advantage by having Mime Makeup and Vanity Mirror, to help with escape and Skill Check. Surviving Dyle's Floor will also grant you the Hissy Fit Achievement, so it's still worth the challenge.

• **Soulvester**: In a similar way, despite his extraordinary extraction, his poor mobility makes his extraction really underutilized. Paired with how the Common Twisteds could be a large hassle and that his Ability is negated by Twisted Dyle's instakill, it's best to use him if you are extremely experienced and careful with him. However, the ability to reach 2 Star Movement Speed if guarding a Toon (or himself in a solo run) could make things a tad bit safer and easier. Additionally, the teammate he's guarding can deliberately take a hit to teleport him to safety if Twisted Dyle is on Soulvester's tail, though this will require a Twisted to be close to the teammate in question, and a lot of coordination. Doing this is a little easier if the teammate is distracting the Common Twisteds.

• **Toodles**: Although she has 4 Star Stealth, it isn't worth it, especially outside of multiplayer since, most of the time, other Toons will be able to get out of sight more quickly than usual. Her low Extraction Speed, small buffs from her Ability, and the fact that each buff is 1 in a 5 (20%) chance makes her less viable here; even with the low cooldown, you won't get that much value from her unless you're using good extraction combos like Magnifying Glass and Participation Award, if you're good at Skill Checks.
